ideas.title: Door Pop-Up Ready Tab

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded door tab
new_nodes.detail: A spring-loaded tab on the door that pops out a few millimetres when the cycle ends.

new_nodes.label: Cam-actuated spring release
new_nodes.detail: Reuses the timer cam to release a spring, the same mechanism that already releases the door.

new_nodes.label: Gives physical end-of-cycle cue
new_nodes.detail: The user feels or sees the door tab move, signalling that the cooking has finished.

ideas.rationale: A tactile tab that physically rises when the food is done gives feedback the user can notice even when they are not listening for a bell.

ideas.title: Transparent Conductive Door

new_nodes.label: ITO-coated clear door panel
new_nodes.detail: A fully transparent indium-tin-oxide coated glass door that shields microwaves while letting ambient light show the food.

new_nodes.label: Transparent conductive coating
new_nodes.detail: A thin conductive film that reflects microwaves and remains clear to visible light.

new_nodes.label: Shows food clearly without a bulb
new_nodes.detail: Gives an unobstructed view of the food using ambient kitchen light.

new_edges.to: Shows food clearly without a bulb

new_edges.from: Shows food clearly without a bulb
Shows food clearly without a bulb

ideas.rationale: A clear door that needs no bulb lets the user see the food's progress at a glance, with no bulb to fail and no mesh to obscure the view.

ideas.title: Odour-Signature Doneness Sensor replacing the timer bell

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer and bell (legacy)
new_nodes.detail: Mechanical 0-30 min timer that signals elapsed time, not food state.

new_nodes.label: Volatile-organic-compound and humidity sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide gas sensors and a humidity sensor mounted in the exhaust duct, sampling the vapour plume.

new_nodes.label: On-device pattern classifier for food aroma
new_nodes.detail: Small classifier trained per food class that maps the vapour-signature trend to a doneness score.

new_nodes.label: Detect onset of browning or drying from vapour chemistry
new_nodes.detail: Flags the moment the surface reaches the target doneness, independent of wattage or load size.

new_edges.to: Function: Detect onset of browning or drying from vapour chemistry

new_edges.from: On-device pattern classifier for food aroma
Detect onset of browning or drying from vapour chemistry

ideas.rationale: The user learns that the food is ready from what the food itself is emitting, not from a guess about how many minutes have passed.

ideas.title: Thermal-Map Viewport replacing the interior lamp and glass window

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp (legacy)
new_nodes.detail: 20-25 W lamp that lets the user see the food through the door glass.

new_nodes.label: Low-cost thermal imaging array in door frame
new_nodes.detail: Uncooled microbolometer behind a germanium-free plastic lens, mounted in the door frame and aimed at the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Thermal surface-gradient analysis
new_nodes.detail: Converts the surface temperature map into cold-spot and hot-spot alerts on a paired phone or the door display.

new_nodes.label: Show cold spots and even heating across the load
new_nodes.detail: Reveals which parts of the food are still cold, so the user knows when the whole dish is ready, not just the edges.

new_edges.from: Low-cost thermal imaging array in door frame
new_edges.to: Function: Show cold spots and even heating across the load
Low-cost thermal imaging array in door frame

new_edges.from: Low-cost thermal imaging array in door frame
Show cold spots and even heating across the load

ideas.rationale: The user sees the actual heat distribution across the food, which indicates readiness more reliably than seeing its colour under a lamp.

ideas.title: Weighing Turntable that tracks moisture loss

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable (legacy)
new_nodes.detail: Passive glass plate that rotates the load for even heating.

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable hub
new_nodes.detail: Strain-gauge load cells under the tray, measuring the mass of the load with about 1 g resolution.

new_nodes.label: Mass-loss doneness model
new_nodes.detail: Converts cumulative water loss, from the mass trend, into a percentage of target doneness for each food type.

new_nodes.label: Report percentage of water evaporated
new_nodes.detail: Shows progress toward the target dryness of the dish, such as roasted or reheated to a set point.

new_edges.to: Function: Report percentage of water evaporated

ideas.rationale: The tray that once only rotated the food now measures how much water has left it, giving a direct progress readout toward the desired result.

ideas.title: Pop-and-Sizzle Acoustic Readout replacing the bell

new_nodes.label: Bell striker (legacy)
new_nodes.detail: Mechanical striker on the timer that rings once at the end of the set time.

new_nodes.label: Contact microphone on cavity wall
new_nodes.detail: Piezo transducer picking up boiling, popping and crackling sounds from the food.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic emission classification
new_nodes.detail: Spectral features of bubbling and crust-crackle, classified against a food-specific library.

new_nodes.label: Announce readiness from sound events
new_nodes.detail: Plays a short tone and a spoken cue when the characteristic sound pattern of the finished food is detected.

new_edges.to: Function: Announce readiness from sound events

ideas.rationale: The alarm fires when the food actually sounds finished, so the user is told about readiness rather than about a timer.

ideas.title: Aroma-Cue Scent Emitter replacing the bell (wild)

new_nodes.label: Audible bell alarm (legacy)
new_nodes.detail: Audible alarm sounded at the end of the timer cycle, which is easy to miss in a noisy kitchen.

new_nodes.label: Micro-cartridge aroma emitter
new_nodes.detail: Piezo-driven microfluidic pump releasing a food-specific scent from a sealed cartridge into the kitchen air.

new_nodes.label: Olfactory cueing
new_nodes.detail: Uses scent as a non-auditory signal that carries through rooms, doors and hearing-impaired environments.

new_nodes.label: Deliver a ready-signal by smell
new_nodes.detail: Releases the target aroma when doneness is detected, so the user knows from the kitchen or the next room.

new_edges.to: Function: Deliver a ready-signal by smell

ideas.rationale: The user is alerted by a scent that is already associated with the finished dish, which reaches them even when they cannot hear or see the microwave.

ideas.title: Solid-state 2.45 GHz amplifier replaces magnetron and high-voltage chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Phase-combined gallium-nitride transistor array driven from about 48 V DC, producing 2.45 GHz with no cathode, leakage transformer or voltage doubler.

new_nodes.label: Gallium-nitride RF power semiconductors
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap transistors that switch efficiently and deliver high power density at microwave frequencies.

new_nodes.label: Electronic continuous power-level control
new_nodes.detail: Sets output power through gate drive, replacing the 5-step mechanical duty-cycle cam and its wear.

ideas.rationale: Removing the transformer and doubler stages eliminates their iron, copper and rectifier losses and lets power be set electronically so the oven delivers only the RF energy the food needs.

ideas.title: Dielectric-feedback endpoint replaces the timer and power cam

new_nodes.label: Waveguide directional-coupler dielectric sensor
new_nodes.detail: Coupler in the waveguide reads forward and reflected RF; the changing reflection tracks food permittivity and absorbed energy.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric load-impedance sensing
new_nodes.detail: Temperature-dependent food permittivity shifts cavity reflection, giving a proxy for absorbed energy and core temperature.

new_nodes.label: Terminates cycle at target absorbed energy
new_nodes.detail: Stops RF once the food reaches the set state instead of running a fixed timer that overshoots.

new_edges.to: Terminates cycle at target absorbed energy

new_edges.from: Terminates cycle at target absorbed energy

ideas.rationale: Ending RF at the energy the food has actually absorbed, rather than at a clock time, prevents the wasted input power that overcooking and reheating otherwise produce.

ideas.title: Convection-driven, magnetically floated turntable

new_nodes.label: Convection-driven turntable vane hub
new_nodes.detail: Bladed hub under the glass tray turns in the warm air plume rising from the food, replacing the 5 rpm motor.

new_nodes.label: Thermal-buoyancy turbine
new_nodes.detail: Heat-driven rising air spins a low-torque rotor whose speed tracks cavity temperature, with no electrical input.

new_nodes.label: Ferrite magnetic bearing ring
new_nodes.detail: Non-contact sintered ferrite rings on the tray and floor support rotation, replacing the roller ring and coupler.

ideas.rationale: Driving the tray from the heat the food already gives off and floating it on microwave-transparent magnets removes the continuous motor draw and the friction losses of the roller ring.

ideas.title: Room-temperature nanotube cathode replaces the heated filament

new_nodes.label: Carbon-nanotube field-emission cathode
new_nodes.detail: Gated nanotube tips emit electrons at room temperature, replacing the heated thoriated filament and its 3 V winding.

new_nodes.label: Field electron emission from nanostructures
new_nodes.detail: A high local field at nanotube tips pulls electrons out cold, allowing near-instant start.

new_nodes.label: Instant electron emission without preheat
new_nodes.detail: Supplies cathode electrons on demand, removing filament standby draw and warm-up time.

ideas.rationale: Removing the filament eliminates continuous heater power during standby and warm-up, which is energy spent before any food is heated.

ideas.title: Ferrite circulator routes reflected RF into a rectenna

new_nodes.label: Ferrite circulator with rectenna load
new_nodes.detail: Non-reciprocal ferrite junction diverts reflected RF from the magnetron anode into a rectenna array instead of heating the magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Rectenna (rectifying antenna) conversion
new_nodes.detail: Antenna-diode array converts stray microwave power into low-voltage DC for controls and lighting.

new_nodes.label: Harvests reflected microwave energy as DC
new_nodes.detail: Reclaims energy that would otherwise heat the magnetron anode and waveguide.

new_edges.to: Harvests reflected microwave energy as DC

new_edges.from: Harvests reflected microwave energy as DC

ideas.rationale: Turning the reflected power that is normally dumped as heat into usable DC recovers part of the input energy and reduces thermal stress on the magnetron.

ideas.title: Light-pipe window replaces the interior lamp

new_nodes.label: Acrylic light-pipe door window
new_nodes.detail: Light-guiding acrylic rods in the door channel ambient kitchen light into the cavity, with a microwave-opaque but light-transparent metal-mesh face.

new_nodes.label: Total internal reflection light guiding
new_nodes.detail: Light trapped in a polymer rod by TIR is carried from the outside ambient light to the cavity without a power source.

new_nodes.label: Illuminates cavity interior passively
new_nodes.detail: Provides the same visibility as the 20-25 W incandescent lamp at zero electrical draw.

new_nodes.label: Optical waveguide engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field governing light transmission through polymer light guides.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 20-25 W incandescent lamp with a passive light pipe removes a continuous electrical load while keeping the cavity visible, directly cutting energy use during every cook cycle.

ideas.title: Food-impedance sensing replaces the clockwork timer

new_nodes.label: Cavity load-impedance sensor
new_nodes.detail: Waveguide-coupled directional probe reads reflected power and the food's dielectric loading to estimate heating progress.

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power dielectric load sensing
new_nodes.detail: Changes in the magnetron's reflected RF power track the food's permittivity as it heats, indicating doneness.

new_nodes.label: Terminates cooking at the energy-optimal point
new_nodes.detail: Stops RF output when the target state is reached, replacing guess-based timed cooking.

new_nodes.label: RF sensing and control
new_nodes.detail: Field covering directional couplers, reflected-power measurement and feedback control.

new_edges.to: Terminates cooking at the energy-optimal point

new_edges.from: Terminates cooking at the energy-optimal point

new_edges.to: Terminates cooking at the energy-optimal point

ideas.rationale: Ending RF output when the food reaches its target state prevents the overcooking and idle-heating waste of fixed mechanical timers, so less energy is drawn per meal.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN amplifier replaces magnetron and HV chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz power amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Gallium-nitride transistor amplifier running at 2.45 GHz on low-voltage DC from a switched-mode supply.

new_nodes.label: Gallium-nitride RF power transistors
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap semiconductors deliver high-efficiency RF gain at 2.45 GHz without a high-voltage cathode.

new_nodes.label: Generates 2.45 GHz RF at low voltage
new_nodes.detail: Produces the same microwave energy as the magnetron while eliminating the 4 kV conversion stage.

new_nodes.label: Wide-bandgap power semiconductor engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field covering GaN device design, RF power amplification and switched-mode power supplies.

new_edges.to: Generates 2.45 GHz RF at low voltage

new_edges.from: Generates 2.45 GHz RF at low voltage

ideas.rationale: Removing the transformer, voltage doubler and magnetron cathode eliminates their conversion and filament losses and lets the amplifier run at higher efficiency and with far lower standby draw.

ideas.title: Phased-array beam steering replaces the turntable motor

new_nodes.label: Dual-feed phased RF array
new_nodes.detail: Two or more electronically phased feeds on the cavity walls shift the standing-wave pattern to sweep hot spots across the food.

new_nodes.label: Electronic RF phase-shift beam steering
new_nodes.detail: Changing the relative phase of feeds moves the field maxima without any moving part.

new_nodes.label: Distributes heat evenly without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Achieves the even heating of turntable rotation with no motor, roller ring or coupler.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array antenna engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field covering electronically steered RF arrays and cavity mode control.

ideas.rationale: Electronic beam steering removes the 5 rpm turntable motor and its friction-driven roller ring, cutting parasitic power and standby losses while improving heating uniformity.

ideas.title: Magnetron heat-pipe preheats the cooking cavity

new_nodes.label: Magnetron heat-pipe thermal bridge
new_nodes.detail: Sealed copper heat pipe carries waste heat from the magnetron anode fins into a thermal plate under the cavity floor.

new_nodes.label: Two-phase heat-pipe heat transport
new_nodes.detail: Evaporation and condensation of a working fluid moves heat passively with very low thermal resistance.

new_nodes.label: Recovers magnetron waste heat for cooking
new_nodes.detail: Routes heat that the magnetron would otherwise vent through louvres into the cavity to warm food and reduce heating demand.

new_nodes.label: Thermal management engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field covering heat pipes, heat exchangers and waste-heat recovery.

new_edges.to: Recovers magnetron waste heat for cooking

new_edges.from: Recovers magnetron waste heat for cooking

new_edges.to: Recovers magnetron waste heat for cooking

ideas.rationale: Capturing magnetron waste heat that is currently vented to air and feeding it into the cavity reduces the energy the magnetron must supply to bring food to temperature.

ideas.title: Solid-State GaN Amplifier Replaces the Magnetron High-Voltage Chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier array (2.45 GHz)
new_nodes.detail: Phase-combined transistor power modules running on low-voltage DC, replacing the magnetron and its ~4 kV supply.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductor amplification
new_nodes.detail: Generates 2.45 GHz RF directly from a low-voltage supply with no cathode to wear out.

new_nodes.label: Zone-by-zone power modulation
new_nodes.detail: Each amplifier module can be switched or dimmed independently, so only the region holding food draws power.

new_edges.from: GaN solid-state RF amplifier array (2.45 GHz)
GaN solid-state RF amplifier array (2.45 GHz)
GaN solid-state RF amplifier array (2.45 GHz)
GaN solid-state RF amplifier array (2.45 GHz)

ideas.rationale: Removing the transformer-capacitor-diode chain and switching power only where food sits cuts idle losses, and the cooler, quieter, low-voltage unit feels more modern and precise, which users read as efficient.

ideas.title: Food-State Sensing Replaces the Mechanical Timer Dial and Bell

new_nodes.label: Infrared and humidity food-state sensor
new_nodes.detail: Reads surface temperature and moisture loss so cooking stops when the food is ready, not when a dial says so.

new_nodes.label: Auto-terminates heating at target food state
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle at the right point, avoiding both overcooking and wasted run time.

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermography and moisture-loss sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost thermopile and humidity sensing used in appliances to infer doneness.

new_edges.to: Auto-terminates heating at target food state

new_edges.from: Auto-terminates heating at target food state

ideas.rationale: Ending each cycle at the moment of doneness removes the energy spent on overshoot, and the appliance seems to 'know' the food, which reduces the user's urge to second-guess and run extra time.

ideas.title: Phased Multi-Feed Antenna Array Replaces the Turntable Motor and Roller Ring

new_nodes.label: Phased dual-feed RF antenna array
new_nodes.detail: Several feed points with electronically steered phase that shift hot spots around the cavity without moving the food.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array beam steering at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Interference patterns are shifted electronically to smooth standing-wave hot and cold spots.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without mechanical rotation
new_nodes.detail: Achieves the even distribution the turntable provided, with no motor and no drive ring.

ideas.rationale: Dropping the motor and its drive ring removes a continuous electrical and mechanical load, and seeing the food stay still while it heats makes the process feel more deliberate and controlled.

ideas.title: Shrinking Cavity: Sliding Baffles Replace the Fixed 20-Litre Chamber

new_nodes.label: Sliding metal baffle walls
new_nodes.detail: Motorised or spring-loaded conductive panels that shrink the active cavity around a small portion or a large one.

new_nodes.label: Cavity volume matched to load
new_nodes.detail: Only the volume that holds the food is energised, so the field fills a smaller space.

new_nodes.label: Reconfigurable resonant cavity
new_nodes.detail: Adjustable conductive walls change the resonant mode so it stays efficient at different volumes.

ideas.rationale: Heating only the space the food occupies wastes far less energy, and a cavity that visibly 'fits' the meal feels thoughtful rather than wasteful.

ideas.title: Phone Camera Replaces the Interior Lamp and Door Window

new_nodes.label: Low-power CMOS camera with app live feed
new_nodes.detail: A few-milliwatt sensor inside the cavity streams the food to the user's phone, with the progress shown as a visual cue.

new_nodes.label: Remote visual check and progress display
new_nodes.detail: Shows the user the cooking state without any light inside the oven.

new_nodes.label: Shielded low-power imaging sensor
new_nodes.detail: A micro-camera behind a metal-mesh window works in the microwave environment with little power.

new_edges.from: Low-power CMOS camera with app live feed
Low-power CMOS camera with app live feed
new_edges.to: Remote visual check and progress display

new_edges.from: Low-power CMOS camera with app live feed
Remote visual check and progress display

ideas.rationale: Replacing a 20–25 W lamp that burns throughout every cycle with a milliwatt camera cuts a constant draw, and a visible progress feed lets people stop opening the door to peek, which keeps heat in.

ideas.title: Dual-band solid-state RF core thawing

new_nodes.label: Dual-band solid-state RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Switched 915 MHz and 2.45 GHz GaN amplifier chains replace the single 2.45 GHz magnetron, so a frozen block can be irradiated at the lower frequency, which penetrates much deeper into ice.

new_nodes.label: Magnetron 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Base-product heat source that is substituted; its penetration into frozen food is shallow, so thawing starts at the surface.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric thawing of frozen core
new_nodes.detail: Delivers RF energy into the centre of a frozen block so it thaws from inside rather than from the outside in.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF power amplification
new_nodes.detail: Semiconductor amplification of microwave power, allowing frequency and power to be switched electronically.

ideas.rationale: Deeper RF penetration at 915 MHz lets a frozen block heat from the centre outward, which shortens total defrost time and reduces the cooked-edge, raw-centre problem.

ideas.title: Graphite-ceramic susceptor tray replaces glass turntable

new_nodes.label: Graphite-loaded ceramic susceptor tray
new_nodes.detail: Microwave-lossy rotating tray that heats itself and conducts heat by contact into the underside of the frozen food, where RF absorption is weakest.

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Base-product tray that is substituted; it is microwave-transparent and so contributes no heat to the food.

new_nodes.label: Conductive basal thawing
new_nodes.detail: Supplies heat through the contact face of the food, complementing the RF field that reaches the top and sides.

new_nodes.label: Microwave susceptor heating
new_nodes.detail: Conversion of absorbed microwave energy into heat in a lossy material, which is then conducted to the load.

ideas.rationale: Heating the food from below through contact closes the thawing gap at the bottom of a frozen block, which is the slowest part to defrost in a conventional microwave.

ideas.title: Load-cell mass sensing replaces clockwork defrost timer

new_nodes.label: Turntable load cell
new_nodes.detail: Strain-gauge load cell under the turntable spindle measures the mass of the frozen load, and the controller computes the defrost time from that mass.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer knob
new_nodes.detail: Base-product 0-30 min dial that is substituted; the user has to guess the duration of the defrost.

new_nodes.label: Automatic mass-based defrost duration
new_nodes.detail: Sets the defrost time from the actual weight of the frozen food, with no user estimate needed.

new_nodes.label: Under- or over-thawed food from guessed time
new_nodes.detail: A manual time guess leaves the food partly frozen or starts to cook it.

new_edges.to: Under- or over-thawed food from guessed time

ideas.rationale: A load cell removes the guesswork from defrost timing so that a frozen block of any size is thawed for the time it actually needs.

ideas.title: Reflected-power thaw-front detection replaces power-level cam

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power thaw-front sensor
new_nodes.detail: Directional coupler and detector measure forward and reflected RF power; the step in dielectric loss as ice melts near 0 °C switches the drive to a higher duty cycle automatically.

new_nodes.label: 5-step power knob duty-cycle cam
new_nodes.detail: Base-product mechanical cam that is substituted; it applies a fixed duty cycle regardless of food state.

new_nodes.label: Adaptive power ramp at phase change
new_nodes.detail: Raises the applied power when the food reaches the thaw point, so energy goes in at the rate the load can absorb it.

new_nodes.label: Closed-loop RF impedance monitoring
new_nodes.detail: Uses changes in the load's impedance and reflected power as a feedback signal for controlling the magnetron or amplifier.

new_edges.to: Adaptive power ramp at phase change

new_edges.from: Adaptive power ramp at phase change

ideas.rationale: Ramping power at the moment the food starts to thaw avoids the long low-absorption stage at the start of defrost and reduces the time spent on the cold phase.

ideas.title: Steam-filled cavity for latent-heat surface thawing

new_nodes.label: Flash-steam generator
new_nodes.detail: Small reservoir in the base that flash-boils a metered water dose into the cavity, filling it with 100 °C steam.

new_nodes.label: Dry cavity air
new_nodes.detail: Base-product cavity atmosphere that is substituted; it carries little heat to the frozen surface.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat surface thawing
new_nodes.detail: Steam condenses on the ice, releasing about 2260 kJ/kg of latent heat, which melts the surface quickly.

new_nodes.label: Condensation heat transfer
new_nodes.detail: Heat transfer by condensation of vapour onto a cold surface, which is far more effective than convection in air.

new_nodes.label: Surface water film on food
new_nodes.detail: Condensate can pool on the food and must be drained or absorbed to avoid soggy results.

ideas.rationale: Steam condensing onto frozen surfaces delivers far more heat per unit area than dry air, so the outer layers thaw in a fraction of the time needed for conventional microwave heating.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN amplifier replaces magnetron and high-voltage chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF power amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Two-stage GaN HEMT amplifier with Wilkinson power combining, delivering about 700 W without a cathode or HV supply.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride HEMT RF amplification
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap transistors amplify 2.45 GHz directly from a low-voltage DC rail.

new_nodes.label: Low-voltage switched-mode DC supply
new_nodes.detail: Compact SMPS giving a 50 V or lower DC rail in place of the 2 kV transformer, capacitor and diode stack.

new_nodes.label: Switch-mode power conversion
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency converter topology that steps mains down to a low-voltage rail with small magnetics.

new_nodes.label: Provides continuously variable RF output power
new_nodes.detail: Analogue gain control sets output from 0 to 100% continuously, removing 30 s on/off duty cycling.

new_edges.from: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF power amplifier
GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF power amplifier
GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF power amplifier
GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF power amplifier
new_edges.to: Provides continuously variable RF output power

new_edges.from: Provides continuously variable RF output power
GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF power amplifier
GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF power amplifier
Provides continuously variable RF output power

ideas.rationale: A continuously adjustable low-power RF output lets the oven hold a gentle defrost setting without the cycling that stalls thawing, while removing the lethal HV capacitor and the cathode wear that limit the magnetron.

ideas.title: Reflected-power thaw detector replaces power knob and timer

new_nodes.label: Directional coupler thaw controller
new_nodes.detail: Microstrip coupler on the magnetron output plus a microcontroller that tracks reflected power and VSWR.

new_nodes.label: Load-impedance (reflected-power) sensing
new_nodes.detail: Cavity loading and reflected RF power shift sharply as ice melts and its dielectric loss rises.

new_nodes.label: Detects thaw onset from cavity load change
new_nodes.detail: Recognises the onset of melting from the reflected-power trend and triggers an automatic step-down in power.

new_edges.to: Detects thaw onset from cavity load change

new_edges.from: Detects thaw onset from cavity load change
Detects thaw onset from cavity load change

ideas.rationale: Stepping power down automatically at the moment ice starts to melt avoids the superheated pockets that slow and uneven thawing, so the user no longer has to guess a time and power level.

ideas.title: Phased multi-port feed replaces turntable and roller ring

new_nodes.label: Four-port phased antenna array with electronic beam steering
new_nodes.detail: Four feed ports around the cavity, driven coherently at controlled relative phase, steer the standing-wave pattern electronically.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array beam steering
new_nodes.detail: Relative phase between coherent RF sources moves interference maxima and minima across the load in milliseconds.

new_nodes.label: Moves hot and cold spots across the load without moving food
new_nodes.detail: Electronic phase sweeping replaces mechanical tray rotation as the means of even heating.

new_edges.from: Four-port phased antenna array with electronic beam steering
Four-port phased antenna array with electronic beam steering
Four-port phased antenna array with electronic beam steering
Four-port phased antenna array with electronic beam steering
new_edges.to: Moves hot and cold spots across the load without moving food

new_edges.from: Moves hot and cold spots across the load without moving food
Moves hot and cold spots across the load without moving food
Four-port phased antenna array with electronic beam steering
Moves hot and cold spots across the load without moving food

ideas.rationale: Sweeping the field pattern electronically removes the cold cores that stall the thawing of large frozen items, and it removes the motor and roller ring that add cost and failure points.

ideas.title: 27 MHz capacitive RF defrost replaces 2.45 GHz magnetron and waveguide

new_nodes.label: 27.12 MHz solid-state RF generator
new_nodes.detail: LDMOS or GaN oscillator with a matching network feeding the electrodes, with no waveguide or magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Parallel-plate RF electrodes
new_nodes.detail: Upper electrode above the food and the grounded tray below form a capacitor across the load.

new_nodes.label: Radio-frequency capacitive dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Food between electrodes forms the dielectric; the field heats volumetrically at about 11 m free-space wavelength, far larger than the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Heats frozen food volumetrically across the whole load
new_nodes.detail: Field wavelength far exceeds the cavity, so the load sees a near-uniform field with no standing-wave hot spots.

new_edges.to: Heats frozen food volumetrically across the whole load

new_edges.from: Heats frozen food volumetrically across the whole load
Heats frozen food volumetrically across the whole load

ideas.rationale: A long-wavelength field that heats the whole load at once avoids the surface-first, cold-core pattern of 2.45 GHz heating, so a frozen block thaws more evenly and in less time.

ideas.title: Susceptor tray with microwave-absorbing film replaces glass turntable

new_nodes.label: Microwave-absorbing susceptor tray
new_nodes.detail: Thin carbon-loaded ceramic or PET plate that absorbs RF near the food and conducts heat into the ice surface.

new_nodes.label: Lossy-film susceptor heating
new_nodes.detail: Film with a tuned loss tangent heats conductively, supplementing dielectric heating of ice.

new_nodes.label: Conducts heat into the frozen base to start melting
new_nodes.detail: Conduction forms a thin liquid interface, which couples strongly to microwaves and speeds thawing of the rest of the food.

new_edges.to: Conducts heat into the frozen base to start melting

new_edges.from: Conducts heat into the frozen base to start melting
Conducts heat into the frozen base to start melting

ideas.rationale: Conductive heat from below starts a thin melt layer that absorbs microwaves strongly, so the frozen block thaws from the base upward and the cold core that slows defrosting is reduced.

ideas.title: Ice-Sense Auto-Thaw

new_nodes.label: Base: 5-step power knob (duty-cycle cam)
new_nodes.detail: Base product component being substituted; user guesses power level and thaw time.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric impedance sensor electrodes
new_nodes.detail: Electrodes in the cavity wall read the food's dielectric loss, which shifts sharply as ice turns to water.

new_nodes.label: Auto-detect thaw state
new_nodes.detail: Measures the ice-to-water transition in real time and adjusts power or stops automatically.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric spectroscopy
new_nodes.detail: Low-power RF sensing of the food's electrical properties.

new_nodes.label: Electromagnetics
new_nodes.detail: Field in which dielectric sensing is rooted.

ideas.rationale: Sensing the actual ice-to-water transition removes guesswork, so frozen food thaws in the shortest safe time without overcooking the edges.

ideas.title: Thaw Tag

new_nodes.label: Base: mechanical clockwork timer knob
new_nodes.detail: Base product component; user dials in a time from 0 to 30 minutes.

new_nodes.label: Passive NFC thaw tag on food packaging
new_nodes.detail: Printed tag that stores the manufacturer's thaw profile: power, cycles, and total time for that product.

new_nodes.label: Supply optimal thaw profile
new_nodes.detail: Hands the correct power schedule to the oven without any user input.

new_nodes.label: Near-field communication
new_nodes.detail: Short-range wireless read of a passive tag with no battery.

new_nodes.label: Wireless communication
new_nodes.detail: Field in which NFC is rooted.

new_edges.from: Passive NFC thaw tag on food packaging
Passive NFC thaw tag on food packaging
Passive NFC thaw tag on food packaging

ideas.rationale: Each frozen product carries its own thaw recipe, so users get fast, even defrosting by scanning the pack rather than guessing settings.

ideas.title: Radio-Thaw Plates

new_nodes.label: Base: 700 W magnetron
new_nodes.detail: Base product's 2.45 GHz heat source, which penetrates only a few centimetres into frozen food.

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz solid-state RF electrode plates
new_nodes.detail: Two parallel plates that flank the food and generate a deeper, more uniform RF field.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric thaw of frozen core
new_nodes.detail: Penetrates deep into frozen blocks so the centre thaws as fast as the surface.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF generation
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost transistor oscillator that replaces the high-voltage transformer and magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Radio-frequency engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field in which RF electrode heating is rooted.

ideas.rationale: Lower-frequency RF penetrates frozen food far deeper than microwaves, so the core thaws evenly instead of the outside cooking first.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Thaw Window

new_nodes.label: Base: 20-25 W interior incandescent lamp
new_nodes.detail: Base product lamp that lets the user see inside the cavity; draws power and produces heat.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door panel
new_nodes.detail: Door window coated with ice-blue film that turns clear as the food thaws past 0 C.

new_nodes.label: Show thaw progress at a glance
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user see which parts of the food are still frozen, without opening the door.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigment
new_nodes.detail: Passive colour-changing dye that responds to temperature with no power input.

new_nodes.label: Materials chemistry
new_nodes.detail: Field in which thermochromic pigments are rooted.

new_edges.to: Show thaw progress at a glance

new_edges.from: Show thaw progress at a glance

ideas.rationale: A panel that changes colour as the food thaws shows progress with zero electricity and no heat-producing bulb, so users know when to stop.

ideas.title: Phase-Change Thermal Battery Plate

new_nodes.label: Base: glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Base product plate that rotates food to even out hot and cold spots.

new_nodes.label: Graphite-paraffin phase-change plate
new_nodes.detail: Thermal battery plate that absorbs microwave heat and stores it as latent heat, then releases it into the food's underside.

new_nodes.label: Store and release heat for conductive thaw
new_nodes.detail: Adds conductive heat from below during thaw, so the bottom of frozen food melts without extra magnetron power.

new_nodes.label: Latent heat storage
new_nodes.detail: Phase-change materials that absorb and release heat at a fixed temperature.

new_nodes.label: Thermal engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field in which latent heat storage is rooted.

new_edges.to: Store and release heat for conductive thaw

new_edges.from: Store and release heat for conductive thaw

ideas.rationale: The plate banks surplus energy and feeds it into the frozen block from below, so the food thaws faster and more evenly with less peak power.

ideas.title: Thermal-Map Window Replaces the Interior Lamp

new_nodes.label: Low-power thermal IR sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Cheap uncooled sensor mounted behind the door that maps surface temperature across the food in real time.

new_nodes.label: Show ice-to-water progress at a glance
new_nodes.detail: Displays which parts of the food are still frozen and which have thawed, so the user can see defrost progress.

new_nodes.label: Low-cost microbolometer imaging
new_nodes.detail: Mass-market thermal imaging technology that costs little more than the bulb it replaces.

new_edges.to: Show ice-to-water progress at a glance

new_edges.from: Show ice-to-water progress at a glance

ideas.rationale: The sensor replaces the lamp's visibility function with a view of thaw state, so users can see exactly when the food is ready to be cooked.

ideas.title: Impedance Sensing Replaces the Clockwork Timer
anchors: mechanical clockwork timer knob (0-30 min, bell)

new_nodes.label: Dielectric impedance electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Two contact pads in the cavity floor that measure how the food's electrical properties change as ice turns to water.

new_nodes.label: Stop automatically at the right thaw point
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle when the food reaches a set thaw level, with no guessing from the user.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric spectroscopy
new_nodes.detail: Measures the change in dielectric properties of ice versus liquid water to detect thaw state.

new_edges.to: Stop automatically at the right thaw point

new_edges.from: Stop automatically at the right thaw point

new_edges.to: mechanical clockwork timer knob (0-30 min, bell)

ideas.rationale: Sensing the actual thaw state replaces a guessed time with a measured end point, which speeds defrosting and prevents cooked edges.

ideas.title: Graphite Susceptor Turntable Replaces the Glass Plate

new_nodes.label: Graphite susceptor plate
new_nodes.detail: A flat plate that absorbs microwaves and conducts heat upward into the underside of the food.

new_nodes.label: Conductive bottom-up thaw assist
new_nodes.detail: Adds heat from below so the underside thaws alongside the microwave-heated top, reducing cold centers.

new_nodes.label: Microwave susceptor materials
new_nodes.detail: Carbon-based materials that heat under microwave energy and are already used in packaging.

ideas.rationale: The plate supplies heat from below as well as above, so frozen food thaws faster and more evenly than microwave energy alone can manage.

ideas.title: Pulsed Tempering Replaces the Power Knob Cam

new_nodes.label: Firmware duty-cycle controller
new_nodes.detail: A small microcontroller that runs short high-power bursts followed by rest periods on a programmable schedule.

new_nodes.label: Heat-soak rest intervals
new_nodes.detail: Rest periods let heat spread by conduction through the frozen mass, so the interior catches up without burning the outside.

new_nodes.label: Pulse-width modulation
new_nodes.detail: Standard low-cost control method that replaces mechanical cams with precise, programmable cycles.

ideas.rationale: Alternating bursts with rest periods lets heat move into the frozen core, which defrosts food faster and with fewer hot spots than continuous power.

ideas.title: Warm Liquid Bath Replaces the Air-Filled Cavity

new_nodes.label: Sealed warm-water jacket
new_nodes.detail: A shallow water reservoir in the cavity floor that the food sits in, sealed in a waterproof pouch.

new_nodes.label: Liquid-medium thaw transfer
new_nodes.detail: Warm water surrounds the food and transfers heat evenly and quickly, far faster than air.

new_nodes.label: Immersion thawing
new_nodes.detail: Well-established cold-water and warm-water thawing method, combined here with microwave heating of the water.

ideas.rationale: Using water instead of air as the heat medium gives much faster, more even thawing of frozen food, which is the core of M4.

ideas.title: Scent-Sense Doneness Sensor

new_nodes.label: MOX gas sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide sensors in the vent that track volatile aroma compounds and steam humidity as food heats.

new_nodes.label: Volatile organic compound (VOC) sensing
new_nodes.detail: Electrochemical detection of the aroma curve that rises and then plateaus as food approaches done.

new_nodes.label: Infers doneness from aroma and steam curve
new_nodes.detail: Compares the live VOC and humidity trend against learned profiles for each food type.

new_edges.to: Infers doneness from aroma and steam curve

new_edges.from: Infers doneness from aroma and steam curve
Infers doneness from aroma and steam curve

ideas.rationale: The user no longer guesses a time and waits for a bell, because the oven reads the food itself and reports when it is actually ready.

ideas.title: Weigh-to-Done Platter

new_nodes.label: Load-cell weighing platter
new_nodes.detail: A turntable platform on strain-gauge load cells that continuously measures the food's mass.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge weighing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost bridge sensors that detect gram-level mass change in real time.

new_nodes.label: Tracks moisture loss by weight
new_nodes.detail: Mass falls predictably as water evaporates, so a set weight loss means the food is done.

ideas.rationale: The food reports its own progress through the weight it sheds, so the user knows the exact moment it is ready without opening the door or checking a clock.

ideas.title: Self-Opening Door

new_nodes.label: Shape-memory alloy door latch
new_nodes.detail: A spring latch that releases the door a few centimetres ajar when triggered by heat.

new_nodes.label: Thermally actuated shape-memory alloy
new_nodes.detail: A wire that contracts at a set temperature with no electronics, power, or software needed.

new_nodes.label: Pops door ajar at target temperature
new_nodes.detail: The door physically announces completion, visible and audible from across the room.

new_edges.to: Pops door ajar at target temperature

new_edges.from: Pops door ajar at target temperature
Pops door ajar at target temperature

ideas.rationale: The door itself becomes the alarm, so the user receives an unmissable physical cue that the food is ready, with no electronics or batteries.

ideas.title: Electrochromic Doneness Window

new_nodes.label: Electrochromic door window
new_nodes.detail: A door glass panel that tints from clear to amber as the food reaches its target, with no bulb inside.

new_nodes.label: Electrochromic glass
new_nodes.detail: Voltage-driven film that changes colour and draws almost no power while holding its state.

new_nodes.label: Shows food state as colour across the room
new_nodes.detail: The tint shifts in step with the food's temperature, readable from across the kitchen.

new_edges.to: Shows food state as colour across the room

new_edges.from: Shows food state as colour across the room

ideas.rationale: The door window tells the user the state of the food at a glance, replacing a bulb and a guessing game with a colour they can read without opening the door.

ideas.title: Magnetron Acoustic Listener

new_nodes.label: Cavity microphone
new_nodes.detail: A small piezo microphone mounted on the cavity wall that listens to the cooking sounds.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic signal analysis
new_nodes.detail: Detects the change in bubbling, popping, and magnetron load pitch as food approaches done.

new_nodes.label: Detects bubbling and load change
new_nodes.detail: Hears the sound of food reaching its end point and triggers a signal.

ideas.rationale: The microwave listens to the food as it cooks and reports completion at the right moment, so the user is alerted by what is happening inside rather than by a fixed countdown.

ideas.title: Phone-Viewed Cook Cam

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp (base)
new_nodes.detail: 20-25 W bulb that is switched on whenever the user wants to look inside; it is the component being replaced.

new_nodes.label: Micro camera module
new_nodes.detail: Sub-1 W, heat-shielded CMOS camera with IR LEDs at under 0.2 W, mounted behind the door mesh.

new_nodes.label: View cooking progress without illumination
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user check food through a phone app, so the bulb is no longer needed.

new_nodes.label: Low-power wireless video streaming
new_nodes.detail: Bluetooth LE or Wi-Fi link that streams the camera feed to the user's phone.

ideas.rationale: Swapping a 20-25 W lamp for a sub-1 W camera cuts the light's energy use by more than 95% while keeping the function of checking food.

ideas.title: Solid-State Phased Feed, No Turntable

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable drive motor (base)
new_nodes.detail: Small synchronous motor that rotates the glass plate so the heating pattern evens out; it is the component being replaced.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array solid-state RF feed
new_nodes.detail: Array of 2.45 GHz solid-state emitters whose phase is steered electronically to move hot spots around the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without moving parts
new_nodes.detail: Spreads energy across the food electronically, so the motor and mechanical rotation are no longer needed.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF amplification
new_nodes.detail: GaN-based amplifiers that generate microwaves at high efficiency without a vacuum tube.

ideas.rationale: Electronic beam steering removes the motor and the dead energy it consumes, and it lets the RF energy land only where the food is, so less is wasted heating air and the cavity.

ideas.title: Thermal-Battery Power Smoothing

new_nodes.label: Direct grid feed to magnetron (base)
new_nodes.detail: The 700 W magnetron draws its full power straight from the 230 V mains, creating peak demand spikes.

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat-storage block
new_nodes.detail: Paraffin or salt-hydrate block charged slowly from a low-power source; it releases heat during a cook cycle and needs no peak electricity.

new_nodes.label: Deliver cooking heat from stored energy
new_nodes.detail: Supplies burst cooking power from a store charged over time, lowering the grid peak needed.

new_nodes.label: Latent heat thermal storage
new_nodes.detail: Phase-change materials that store and release large amounts of energy at a constant temperature.

new_edges.to: Deliver cooking heat from stored energy

new_edges.from: Deliver cooking heat from stored energy

ideas.rationale: Charging a thermal store off-peak or from a small solar input and drawing cooking power from it flattens the household energy curve and reduces the grid demand each cook creates.

ideas.title: Continuous Inverter Power Dial

new_nodes.label: 5-step duty-cycle power cam (base)
new_nodes.detail: Mechanical cam that switches the magnetron fully on and off, so it runs at full power and wastes energy during each off phase.

new_nodes.label: Variable-frequency inverter driver
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state drive that sets the magnetron's output continuously from 10% to 100% with no on/off cycling.

new_nodes.label: Continuous, precise power control
new_nodes.detail: Holds the chosen power level steadily, so food is not repeatedly over-heated and rested.

new_nodes.label: Power electronics inverter
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency switching converter that regulates magnetron power accurately.

ideas.rationale: Continuous inverter control matches delivered power to the food's needs, removing the energy lost to repeated start-stop cycling and to overshooting the target.

ideas.title: Self-Terminating Doneness Sensor

new_nodes.label: Mechanical 0-30 min clockwork timer (base)
new_nodes.detail: Dial timer with a bell that runs for a fixed time whether or not the food is ready, causing overcooking and wasted energy.

new_nodes.label: Humidity and gas sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide and humidity sensors that detect steam and volatile compounds and signal when the food is done.

new_nodes.label: Stop heating at doneness
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle as soon as the food reaches the target state, instead of running to a preset time.

new_nodes.label: Embedded gas and humidity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost sensors with onboard processing that classify cooking state from the exhaust.

ideas.rationale: Ending each cook at the moment of doneness avoids the energy wasted by overcooking food that was already ready, and the sensors cost less than the timer's fixed-duration design wastes over a year.

ideas.title: Ambient-Light Fibre Window

new_nodes.label: Daylight fibre-optic light guide
new_nodes.detail: Optical fibre bundle that collects ambient room light at the door and pipes it into the cavity through a sealed, microwave-blocking grille.

new_nodes.label: Passive light guide
new_nodes.detail: Zero-power optical channel replacing the 20-25 W incandescent lamp and its wiring.

new_nodes.label: Illuminate cavity without electricity
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user see food through the door using only light already in the room.

ideas.rationale: Removing the lamp's continuous 20-25 W draw and using ambient light for viewing directly cuts standby-independent energy use while keeping the user's visibility function.

ideas.title: Dielectric Doneness Sensor replacing the Timer

new_nodes.label: Dielectric permittivity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Measures changes in the food's dielectric loss or moisture content through the cavity's existing antenna and feed as cooking progresses.

new_nodes.label: Doneness detector
new_nodes.detail: Electronic sensor that ends the cycle when the food reaches a target state, replacing the 0-30 min clockwork timer and bell.

new_nodes.label: Stop heating at the right moment
new_nodes.detail: Prevents both under-heating that needs a re-run and over-heating that wastes microwave energy.

new_edges.to: Stop heating at the right moment

new_edges.from: Stop heating at the right moment

ideas.rationale: Ending the cycle when the food is actually done, rather than after a guessed time, removes the largest source of wasted magnetron energy in everyday use.

ideas.title: Solid-State Power Stage replacing the Duty-Cycle Cam

new_nodes.label: GaN switched-mode magnetron drive
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency gallium-nitride converter that sets magnetron power continuously and matches the load in real time.

new_nodes.label: Continuous power controller
new_nodes.detail: Electronic controller replacing the mechanical cam that cycles the magnetron on and off at five fixed steps.

new_nodes.label: Deliver only the power the food absorbs
new_nodes.detail: Avoids the overshoot and cycling losses of fixed duty steps and the efficiency loss of the 50 Hz iron-core transformer.

new_edges.to: Deliver only the power the food absorbs

new_edges.from: Deliver only the power the food absorbs

ideas.rationale: A switched-mode drive that matches delivered power to the load and replaces the bulky 50 Hz transformer lowers conversion losses across every power setting.

ideas.title: Phased-Array Feed replacing the Turntable

new_nodes.label: Multi-feed phased microwave array
new_nodes.detail: Several electronically phased feed points that steer the field across the cavity so hot spots are evened out without moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Electronic field steering
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state phase control that replaces the motor-driven glass turntable and its drive coupling.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Achieves uniform heating while removing the motor's power draw and the turntable's mass that must be heated and cleaned.

ideas.rationale: Steering the field electronically removes the turntable motor's continuous energy draw and the mechanical losses while still giving even heating.

ideas.title: Thermoelectric Magnetron Heat Recovery

new_nodes.detail: Solid-state Seebeck modules bonded to the magnetron's finned heat sink that convert its waste heat into electricity.

new_nodes.label: Waste-heat power module
new_nodes.detail: Thermoelectric array that generates low-voltage power from waste heat to run the fan, controls and lamp replacement.

new_nodes.label: Recover magnetron waste heat as electricity
new_nodes.detail: Turns heat that is currently exhausted to the room into usable power, reducing the net electrical draw of the auxiliary systems.

new_edges.to: Recover magnetron waste heat as electricity
Thermoelectric generator on magnetron heat sink

new_edges.from: Recover magnetron waste heat as electricity

ideas.rationale: Capturing the magnetron's waste heat to power the auxiliary electronics directly reduces the energy the appliance must draw from the mains.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Door Window

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door film
new_nodes.detail: Heat-sensitive film on the door that shades to show hot and cold zones of the food, with no power draw.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigment
new_nodes.detail: Leuco-dye or liquid-crystal pigment that changes colour at set temperatures.

new_nodes.label: Show food progress without light
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user judge doneness and spot hot spots without the interior lamp.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 20-25 W lamp with a passive colour-changing film removes a continuous power draw while still letting users see inside.

ideas.title: Steam-Sensed Stop Replaces the Timer

new_nodes.label: Steam-sensing stop
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost humidity sensor that ends cooking when food stops releasing steam.

new_nodes.detail: Mass-produced sensor already used in cheap appliances.

new_nodes.label: Stop cooking when done
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle at doneness instead of at a guessed time.

ideas.rationale: Stopping at doneness rather than running a fixed clock avoids overheating and wasted watt-hours, so the appliance uses only the energy the food needs.

ideas.title: Cost-Per-Cook Dial Replaces the Bell

new_nodes.label: Energy-cost dial
new_nodes.detail: Mechanical counter on the timer face that shows pence or grams of CO2 for the chosen cycle.

new_nodes.label: Make energy use visible
new_nodes.detail: Changes how users perceive cooking time, nudging them toward lower power settings.

new_nodes.label: Users default to full power
new_nodes.detail: Behavioural habit that drives unnecessary energy use.

ideas.rationale: Turning the end-of-cook bell into a visible running cost reframes efficiency as a pleasure of saving, so people choose lower power without any engineering change.

ideas.title: Phase-Change Heat Battery

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat pack
new_nodes.detail: Salt-hydrate block in the base that stores heat charged off-peak and releases it during cooking.

new_nodes.label: Latent heat storage
new_nodes.detail: Phase-change materials that store and release large amounts of heat at a stable temperature.

new_nodes.label: Supply cooking heat from storage
new_nodes.detail: Provides part of the heat so the magnetron runs at lower output or shorter duty.

ideas.rationale: Charging stored heat when grid power is cheap or low-carbon shifts demand and reduces peak-hour draw from the 700 W magnetron.

ideas.title: Susceptor Plate Replaces the Turntable

new_nodes.label: Fixed susceptor plate
new_nodes.detail: Ceramic-coated metal plate that absorbs microwaves and conducts heat up into the food, replacing the rotating glass turntable.

new_nodes.label: Microwave susceptor coating
new_nodes.detail: Material that heats strongly under microwave fields.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Spreads heat across the base of the food so no turntable motor is needed.

ideas.rationale: Removing the turntable motor and using a heat-conducting plate lets food cook more evenly at lower power, saving energy on both drive and heating.

ideas.title: Mains-current doneness sensing (timer replaced by power-draw inflection detection)

new_nodes.label: Load-absorption inference from magnetron supply current
new_nodes.detail: Water loss from food lowers absorbed RF power, which appears as a measurable inflection in the mains current envelope that a shunt and ADC can sample without any extra sensor.

new_nodes.label: Current-envelope comparator MCU
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost microcontroller that samples the existing supply-current shunt, computes a rolling derivative, and flags the inflection point.

new_nodes.label: Detect food-readiness from power-draw inflection
new_nodes.detail: Converts the current-envelope signal into a binary or graded ready/not-ready state with no user-set time.

new_edges.to: Load-absorption inference from magnetron supply current

ideas.rationale: It tells the user when food is ready from what the food is actually doing rather than from a guessed time, and it reuses the magnetron's existing electrical signal at almost no added hardware cost.

new_nodes.detail: Low-resolution non-contact sensor that produces a grid of surface temperatures across the turntable.

new_nodes.label: Render food surface temperature map to the user
new_nodes.detail: Shows a colour heat map of the food on a small door-mounted display or a companion app, so the user sees hot and cold spots directly.

ideas.title: Glow-in-the-Dark Cavity

new_nodes.detail: Microcontroller that reads the reflectometer and stops or throttles RF output when the load reaches a target state, replacing the mechanical timer knob and 5-step power cam.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic film on borosilicate glass
new_nodes.detail: Leuco-dye film on the door window changes from frosted blue (frozen) to clear (thawed) as the food surface warms.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door window
new_nodes.detail: Door window that replaces the 20-25 W lamp and shows thaw progress at no running cost.

new_nodes.label: Shows thaw progress visually
new_nodes.detail: The frosted-to-clear transition gives an at-a-glance reading of how far the defrost has got.

ideas.rationale: Watching frosted food turn clear turns an invisible wait into visible progress, which makes the defrost feel faster and removes the need to open the door and check.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat phase-change storage (salt hydrate)
new_nodes.detail: Stores and releases heat near a fixed melting point, giving steady conduction heating without extra RF power.

new_nodes.label: Conducts stored heat into frozen food from below
new_nodes.detail: Adds conductive thawing alongside dielectric heating, so the magnetron does less of the work.

new_nodes.label: Piezo sound module
new_nodes.detail: Cheap piezo buzzer that plays a crackle which gets busier and then fades as the food thaws, replacing the bell.

new_nodes.label: Makes the wait feel shorter through progressive audio
new_nodes.detail: A changing soundscape keeps the user engaged and makes the wait feel shorter, which reduces the perceived defrost time.

ideas.title: Salt-Gel Thaw Sleeve replaces the frozen food's missing dielectric coupling

new_nodes.label: Reusable salt-gel thaw sleeve
new_nodes.detail: Flexible polymer sleeve with ionic salt gel that wraps frozen meat and couples strongly to the 2.45 GHz field.

new_nodes.label: Ionic conduction heating
new_nodes.detail: Dissolved ions in the gel oscillate in the RF field and heat the sleeve, which then warms the frozen food by conduction.

new_nodes.label: Couples microwave energy into frozen food that absorbs it poorly
new_nodes.detail: Ice absorbs RF weakly, so the sleeve supplies the coupling that frozen food lacks.

new_nodes.detail: Pigment changes colour at a set temperature and needs no power or bulb.

ideas.title: Door pops when done

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded door pop
new_nodes.detail: At cycle end the latch releases and a spring cracks the door open a few centimetres.

new_nodes.label: Makes end-of-cycle impossible to ignore
new_nodes.detail: The door visibly and physically moves, so the cue is felt as well as heard.

ideas.rationale: The door already has a push-release and a spring-return mechanism, so letting it pop open when the timer finishes gives unmissable feedback at almost no extra cost, and the cooked food is fetched sooner.

ideas.title: Steam sniffer replaces the timer

new_nodes.label: Environmental sensing (humidity and temperature)
new_nodes.detail: Field covering low-cost sensing of vapour and heat in appliances.

new_nodes.label: Thermistor-based vapour sensing
new_nodes.detail: Resistive humidity sensing costs a few cents and reads the vapour curve in the vent.

new_nodes.label: Vent vapour sensor
new_nodes.detail: A small sensor in the exhaust path detects rising vapour and its plateau as food nears done.

new_nodes.label: Infers food readiness from vapour
new_nodes.detail: Estimates doneness from the steam curve instead of counting down minutes.

ideas.rationale: Replacing minutes with the food's own steam gives the user a real signal of readiness instead of a guess, which answers the open-loop problem and the short-duration imprecision together.

new_nodes.label: Microencapsulated fragrance release
new_nodes.detail: A heat-triggered sealed capsule releases scent when the heater fires.

new_nodes.label: Toast-scent capsule
new_nodes.detail: A sealed micro-reservoir of toasted-bread aroma that a tiny heater releases at cycle end.

new_nodes.label: Signals end of cooking through smell
new_nodes.detail: An olfactory cue reaches the user in a different room, which a bell cannot do.

new_edges.from: Signals end of cooking through smell

ideas.rationale: A smell of toast arriving from the kitchen tells the user the food is ready through a sense the bell never used, so people come to the kitchen because they can smell that the meal is done.

new_nodes.detail: Crackle and bubble sounds indicate readiness, replacing the need to look inside.

ideas.title: Solid-State RF Defroster

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Low-voltage (48 V) semiconductor power stage that generates 2.45 GHz or 915 MHz RF in place of the magnetron and HV chain.

new_nodes.label: Frequency-agile defrost mode
new_nodes.detail: Switches to 915 MHz for deeper penetration into frozen blocks while keeping 2.45 GHz for cooking.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride RF power amplification
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state power transistors deliver continuous, finely adjustable RF output with no kV supply.

ideas.rationale: Frequency-agile, continuously adjustable low-voltage RF lets the appliance defrost frozen food deeper and more evenly, with no lethal capacitor or short-lived magnetron.

ideas.title: Ice-Sensing Auto-Defrost Pad

new_nodes.label: Dielectric-impedance sensing plate
new_nodes.detail: Printed electrode pad in the tray that measures the loss-factor change as ice turns to liquid water.

new_nodes.label: Automatic ice-to-water endpoint detection
new_nodes.detail: Pulses power while frozen and stops or drops power when the food reaches the thaw point.

new_nodes.label: Capacitive dielectric sensing
new_nodes.detail: Measures how food absorbs RF energy, which changes sharply at the ice-water transition.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the guessed timer and power knob with a sensor that stops at the exact thaw point means frozen food defrosts quickly without overcooking the edges.

ideas.title: Susceptor Thaw Tray

new_nodes.label: Microwave-susceptor thaw plate
new_nodes.detail: Thin carbon- or ferrite-loaded plate that absorbs RF and conducts heat evenly into the frozen food.

new_nodes.label: Conductive even thawing
new_nodes.detail: Spreads heat by conduction across the frozen surface, avoiding standing-wave hot and cold spots.

new_nodes.label: Susceptor-film heat conversion
new_nodes.detail: Lossy coating converts microwaves to heat at the surface, so the field acts as a heat source instead of a direct heater.

ideas.rationale: A susceptor plate that conducts heat into the frozen block removes uneven hot and cold spots and avoids surface cooking while the centre is still frozen.

ideas.title: Compact Thaw Drawer

new_nodes.label: Compact high-density thaw drawer cavity
new_nodes.detail: Small resonant drawer sized for one or two frozen packs, with the RF field concentrated in its smaller volume.

new_nodes.label: High-density field thawing
new_nodes.detail: Concentrates the same 700 W into a small volume, raising energy density per gram of frozen food.

new_nodes.label: Resonant cavity volume scaling
new_nodes.detail: Smaller cavities have stronger field intensity and shorter standing-wave cycles.

ideas.rationale: A smaller drawer with a denser field gets a single frozen pack thawed much faster than heating a full 20 L cavity, which suits busy parents.

ideas.title: Insertable Probe Thawing

new_nodes.label: Insertable RF thaw probes
new_nodes.detail: Thin coaxial probes pushed into frozen blocks, delivering RF from inside the ice mass.

new_nodes.label: Internal-source deep thawing
new_nodes.detail: Heats from the core outward, so the centre thaws as fast as the surface.

new_nodes.label: Coaxial RF probe coupling
new_nodes.detail: Transfers RF energy through a coaxial line into the load, like a meat thermometer probe.

ideas.rationale: Delivering energy from the centre of the frozen mass removes the slow surface-first thaw and cuts the time needed to defrost a block.

ideas.title: Steam-Latent Defrost Chamber

new_nodes.label: Micro-steam generator
new_nodes.detail: Small sealed boiler (about 30 mL water reservoir) replaces the magnetron as the main energy source, producing steam at about 100 C.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat condensation
new_nodes.detail: Steam condenses on the cold food surface and releases about 2260 kJ/kg of latent heat, which penetrates through condensate films into the frozen mass.

new_nodes.label: Condensing heat transfer
new_nodes.detail: Delivers thermal energy to frozen food by phase change rather than by electromagnetic absorption, so heating is not limited to the outer layer.

ideas.rationale: Condensation heats the whole surface of a frozen block at a uniform rate and avoids the edge-overheating and cold-centre problems of microwave defrost, which speeds up M4.

ideas.title: Solid-State RF Dielectric Defrost

new_nodes.label: GaN RF oscillator and electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state 27.12 MHz RF source drives two electrode plates that bracket the food, replacing the 2.45 GHz magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Radio-frequency dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Longer wavelength gives deeper, more uniform penetration into frozen food and reduces hot spots at the edges.

new_nodes.label: RF power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Field from which the solid-state RF source is drawn.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Heats the food bulk evenly, which shortens total defrost time and avoids cooking the edges.

new_edges.from: GaN RF oscillator and electrode pair
GaN RF oscillator and electrode pair

ideas.rationale: Deeper, volumetric RF heating thaws the centre of a frozen block at the same time as the surface, which reduces the total time to a usable defrost state for M4.

ideas.title: Ice-Melt Impedance Endpoint

new_nodes.label: Dielectric impedance probe
new_nodes.detail: Pair of stainless contacts in the cavity floor measures the food's loss factor, which changes sharply when ice melts into liquid water.

new_nodes.label: Phase-transition sensing
new_nodes.detail: Detects the ice-to-water transition from the impedance shift and treats it as the defrost completion signal.

new_nodes.label: Automatic defrost termination
new_nodes.detail: Ends the defrost cycle when the food reaches a usable thaw state, replacing the user's guess at a time.

new_nodes.label: Uneven ice distribution
new_nodes.detail: Food with partial thaw in some zones can trigger false endpoints and needs a multi-point probe.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the clockwork timer with an endpoint that senses the actual ice-to-water change stops over-thawing and under-thawing, which directly serves the speed-and-quality goal of M4.

ideas.title: Phase-Change Thermal Buffer

new_nodes.label: Phase-change thermal pad
new_nodes.detail: Sealed salt-hydrate pad in the cavity wall that absorbs magnetron heat while melting and releases it slowly while solidifying.

new_nodes.label: Latent thermal storage
new_nodes.detail: Stores surplus energy during full-power bursts and releases it during rest periods, replacing the duty-cycle cam.

new_nodes.label: Sustained low-temperature heat delivery
new_nodes.detail: Delivers a steady heat flux during rest periods so the frozen core warms without surface cooking.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the mechanical power-cycling cam with a latent thermal buffer keeps the frozen core warming through rest periods, which lets full power be used for defrosting without scorching the surface.

ideas.title: Conductive Cradle with Thermal-Map Feedback

new_nodes.label: Induction-heated conductive cradle
new_nodes.detail: Stainless tray replaces the glass turntable and is heated by induction coil beneath it, conducting heat into the underside of frozen food.

new_nodes.label: Low-cost thermal sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Small grid of infrared sensors replaces the 20-25 W incandescent lamp, mapping surface temperature to show which zones are still frozen.

new_nodes.label: Conductive contact heating
new_nodes.detail: Heat moves directly from the cradle into the food, which is more efficient for the bottom of a frozen block.

new_nodes.label: Frozen-zone visualisation
new_nodes.detail: Shows the user, and the controller, which parts of the food remain frozen.

ideas.rationale: Direct conductive heating from below combined with a live map of frozen zones lets the user and controller target the coldest areas, which speeds up M4 and replaces the old light-based viewing function.

ideas.title: Pop-Up Doneness Pin

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob (base)
new_nodes.detail: Replaced component: guesses doneness from elapsed time, so it can be wrong for any given food.

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded wax-tipped pin
new_nodes.detail: Inserted into the food; a meltable tip releases a spring when the core reaches serving temperature, and the pin pops up.

new_nodes.label: Tactile signal of doneness from the food's own core temperature
new_nodes.detail: The food itself announces readiness by physically rising, which is a feedback channel no timer can provide.

new_nodes.label: Passive thermal actuation (wax melt release)
new_nodes.detail: Needs no electronics, power or software; the physics of heat does the signalling.

new_edges.to: Tactile signal of doneness from the food's own core temperature

new_nodes.detail: Fades from cold blue through amber to a bright red-gold as the plate and food reach serving heat.

new_nodes.label: Continuous visual gradient of readiness
new_nodes.detail: Shows progress toward done, not just a binary finished state, so the user can judge timing.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigments
new_nodes.detail: Cheap printed pigments already used in mugs and kettles, activated by the heat itself.

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable plate
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the passive glass plate with a thin weighing platform that tracks the food's mass in real time.

new_nodes.label: Track moisture loss as weight
new_nodes.detail: Cooked food loses water in a predictable curve, so the falling mass shows progress toward doneness.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge weighing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost load cells with a microcontroller that filters out turntable motion.

new_nodes.label: Progress ring on front panel
new_nodes.detail: Shows percentage of expected mass loss as a simple arc.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door film
new_nodes.detail: A passive film on the door glass that changes colour with heat, showing hot and cold zones without any power.

new_nodes.label: Show heat distribution at a glance
new_nodes.detail: Reveals cold spots and hot spots in the cavity without the user needing to look at the food directly.

new_nodes.label: Leuco-dye thermochromic coating
new_nodes.detail: A printed or laminated dye layer that shifts colour over a set temperature range.

new_nodes.label: Humidity and VOC gas sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Tracks steam and volatile aroma compounds rising from the food as it heats.

new_nodes.label: Detect readiness from vapour trend
new_nodes.detail: Stops heating when the vapour curve flattens or the aroma peaks, which marks doneness for most foods.

new_nodes.label: Trend-based control logic
new_nodes.detail: Uses rate of change in the sensor readings rather than absolute values, so it works across food types.

new_nodes.label: Haptic pulse in door handle
new_nodes.detail: Gives a short vibration when the food is ready, so the user feels the signal before opening the door.

new_nodes.label: Communicate progress through touch
new_nodes.detail: The user feels how close the food is to done through the knob, without looking at a display.

new_nodes.label: Magnetorheological fluid actuation
new_nodes.detail: Changes fluid viscosity with an electromagnetic field to vary torque on the knob.

ideas.title: Solid-State GaN Defrost Amplifier Replacing the Magnetron Chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Low-voltage transistor amplifier with continuously variable output, replacing the magnetron and its 4 kV supply.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride RF power transistors
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap semiconductors that amplify 2.45 GHz directly from a low-voltage DC rail.

new_nodes.label: Continuously variable defrost power
new_nodes.detail: Sets any power level by analogue gain control, with no on/off cycling.

ideas.rationale: Continuous low-power output lets the defrost cycle hold frozen food at sub-melting power for longer, which reduces cooked edges and serves M4 better than cycling a full-power magnetron.

ideas.title: Self-Sensing Reflectometer Auto-Defrost Replacing the Power and Timer Knobs

new_nodes.label: Directional RF reflectometer
new_nodes.detail: Coupler in the waveguide that measures reflected power and detects the dielectric jump when ice melts into water.

new_nodes.label: Detects ice-to-water phase transition
new_nodes.detail: Reads the change in load impedance to decide when to lower power or stop.

new_nodes.label: Load-impedance sensing for dielectric state
new_nodes.detail: Uses reflected RF power as a proxy for the food's permittivity and loss.

ideas.rationale: Sensing the ice-to-water transition directly removes the need for a user to guess the weight and time, so frozen food defrosts quickly without partial cooking.

ideas.title: Phased-Array Beam Steering Replacing the Turntable

new_nodes.label: Electronically steered antenna array
new_nodes.detail: Several 2.45 GHz feed elements whose phases are shifted to move the hot spot across the food.

new_nodes.label: Electronic hot-spot sweep
new_nodes.detail: Shifts the standing-wave pattern many times per second without any moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array beamforming
new_nodes.detail: Varies the relative phase of coherent RF sources to steer the field pattern.

ideas.rationale: Moving the hot spots electronically across a frozen block lets every part thaw at a similar rate, which shortens the defrost time and removes the cold centre that makes users overcook the outer edges.

ideas.title: 27 MHz Electrode-Cavity Defrost Replacing the 2.45 GHz Magnetron

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz RF oscillator with cavity-electrode plates
new_nodes.detail: Low-frequency solid-state oscillator whose cavity walls act as capacitor plates across the food.

new_nodes.label: Radio-frequency electrode heating (RF tempering)
new_nodes.detail: Heats the load by displacement current between electrodes, penetrating several centimetres uniformly.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric defrost through the food core
new_nodes.detail: Heats the centre and edges of a frozen block at comparable rates.

new_edges.from: 27 MHz RF oscillator with cavity-electrode plates
27 MHz RF oscillator with cavity-electrode plates
new_edges.to: Volumetric defrost through the food core

ideas.rationale: Deeper, more uniform penetration at 27 MHz means frozen food thaws through its core in less time than surface-driven 2.45 GHz heating allows, which directly serves M4.

ideas.title: Wall-Mounted Patch Antenna Array Replacing the Waveguide Feed

new_nodes.label: Distributed patch antennas on cavity walls
new_nodes.detail: Flush printed antennas on the enamelled walls that feed RF directly into the cavity from many points.

new_nodes.label: Printed microstrip antenna on enamelled steel
new_nodes.detail: Thin dielectric-coated patch radiators bonded to the cavity wall.

new_nodes.label: Multi-point RF injection
new_nodes.detail: Injects energy from several walls at once, so no single feed point creates a dominant hot spot.

new_nodes.label: Colour-graded door display strip
new_nodes.detail: Small LED strip on the door frame showing cold, warm and hot zones as the cook progresses

new_nodes.label: Show temperature distribution across the food
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user see cold spots and hot spots, not just whether the food looks cooked

new_nodes.label: Passive infrared thermography
new_nodes.detail: Reads thermal emission from food surfaces without contact or light

ideas.title: Acoustic Doneness Sensing Replaces the Bell

new_nodes.label: Mechanical bell (base product)
new_nodes.detail: Audible alarm that fires at a fixed time regardless of food state

new_nodes.label: MEMS microphone with spectral classifier
new_nodes.detail: Small microphone inside the cavity feeding a classifier trained on bubbling, popping and sizzling sounds

new_nodes.label: Acoustic signature classification
new_nodes.detail: Recognises the sound change that accompanies boiling, steaming and the end of popping

new_nodes.detail: Triggers an alert when the acoustic pattern indicates the food is ready

ideas.title: Fibre-Optic Probe Tip Replaces the Timer Dial

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob (base product)
new_nodes.detail: 0-30 min mechanical dial; replaced because the user must guess the time in advance

new_nodes.label: Microwave-transparent fibre-optic temperature probe
new_nodes.detail: Dielectric (non-metallic) fibre tip inserted in the food, read by an optical sensor outside the cavity

new_nodes.label: Optical fluorescence thermometry
new_nodes.detail: Measures temperature from a phosphor tip's decay time, unaffected by microwave fields

new_nodes.detail: Gives the actual internal temperature, the most direct measure of readiness

new_nodes.detail: Plain glass plate that rotates the food; replaced with a functional indicator layer

new_nodes.detail: Glass turntable with a printed ring of colour-changing ink that changes colour at a set plate temperature
