ideas.title: Brine-Gel Thaw Tray

new_nodes.label: Salt-brine conductive gel pad
new_nodes.detail: Flexible, dishwasher-safe gel pad under the frozen food that absorbs RF and conducts heat into the frozen core by contact.

new_nodes.label: Conducts heat into frozen core by contact
new_nodes.detail: Carries heat from the surface of the pad into the ice that microwaves alone leave cold.

new_nodes.label: Ionic-conduction heat transfer
new_nodes.detail: Dissolved salts give the gel a dielectric loss factor that is high at sub-zero temperatures.

ideas.rationale: The gel pad replaces the glass turntable's passive role with active conduction, so frozen cores thaw as fast as the outside, which directly shortens defrost time.

ideas.title: Crackle-Fade Thaw Chime

new_nodes.label: Perceived-speed audio feedback
new_nodes.detail: Plays an ice-cracking crackle that fades as the food thaws, so waiting feels shorter and progress is audible.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic progress signalling
new_nodes.detail: A cheap piezo buzzer driven by the same duty-cycle timing that already sets the power level.

ideas.rationale: Following Sutherland's logic, a fading crackle makes a parent feel defrosting is nearly done, so the wait seems shorter even when the physical thaw time is unchanged.

ideas.title: Ice-Breaker Vibration Tray

new_nodes.label: Eccentric-mass vibration motor
new_nodes.detail: A cheap coin-type vibration motor replaces the 5 rpm turntable motor and shakes the tray to loosen ice clusters.

new_nodes.label: Breaks up ice clusters mechanically
new_nodes.detail: Vibration separates frozen pieces so microwaves reach more surface area.

ideas.rationale: Vibrating the load breaks ice into smaller pieces that thaw faster and more evenly, and the cheaper motor reduces cost at the same time.

ideas.title: Load-Sensing Thaw Electrode

new_nodes.label: Capacitive load-sensing electrode
new_nodes.detail: A small metal plate in the cavity wall measures the dielectric load and sets the duty cycle automatically, replacing the manual power knob.

new_nodes.label: Auto-sets defrost power from food mass
new_nodes.detail: Reads how much frozen mass is present and chooses the right on/off ratio without user guesswork.

new_nodes.label: Capacitive dielectric sensing
new_nodes.detail: Measures changes in capacitance as the food's dielectric properties shift from frozen to thawed.

ideas.title: Waste-Heat Thaw Cradle

new_nodes.label: Ceramic thaw cradle plate
new_nodes.detail: A ceramic plate on the top of the casing, thermally bonded to the transformer, that warms the frozen food from below using heat the transformer already gives off.

new_nodes.label: Recycles transformer waste heat for thawing
new_nodes.detail: Turns energy that is normally lost as heat into gentle conductive thawing for small items.

new_nodes.label: Passive conductive heat spreading

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN amplifier replaces magnetron and HV chain

new_nodes.label: GaN HEMT power-amplifier array (4 to 8 cells, ~700 W combined)
new_nodes.detail: Transistor amplifiers on a combining manifold generate 2.45 GHz RF with no cathode, filament or 2 kV supply.

new_nodes.detail: Mains is rectified and switched directly to a low-voltage bus, replacing the step-up transformer, doubler and HV capacitor.

new_nodes.label: Wide-bandgap GaN transistor amplification at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: High-efficiency RF transistors with per-cell power and phase control, allowing continuous output without duty-cycle cam cycling.

new_nodes.label: Sets output power continuously with no filament standby loss
new_nodes.detail: Power is modulated electronically, so the oven neither heats a filament nor cycles on and off to approximate a power level.

new_nodes.detail: The effective field pattern is swept electronically so the whole load is covered without a motor.

ideas.title: Sensing Cook-Stop Replaces the Clock

new_nodes.detail: 0-30 min spring timer with bell; present in base spec.

new_nodes.detail: Low-power sensors that detect moisture and volatile compounds released as food cooks.

new_nodes.label: Automatic cook-end detection

ideas.title: Solid-State GaN RF Heater Replaces Magnetron

new_nodes.detail: Semiconductor microwave source that can be dialed to exact power continuously.

new_nodes.label: Continuous precise power output
new_nodes.detail: Delivers any power level with no on/off cycling losses.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap semiconductors that run efficiently at GHz frequencies.

ideas.rationale: Solid-state amplification with continuous modulation removes the magnetron's thermal losses and cycling waste, improving the energy conversion of every watt drawn.

ideas.title: Phased-Array Beam Steering Replaces Turntable

new_nodes.detail: Rotating glass plate and motor that spread heat evenly; present in base spec.

new_nodes.label: Multi-feed phased antenna array
new_nodes.detail: Several small emitters whose phase is shifted electronically to steer the field.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without moving parts
new_nodes.detail: Sweeps energy around the cavity electronically to remove cold spots.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array beamforming
new_nodes.detail: Controls wave interference to focus and move energy without mechanics.

ideas.rationale: Electronic beam steering removes the motor's standby and running energy and lets the field target food directly, so less energy is wasted heating the cavity air and plate.

new_nodes.detail: Salt or wax store charged slowly from off-peak power or waste heat and discharged as needed.

new_nodes.label: Peak-free, off-peak energy supply
new_nodes.detail: Shifts consumption to cheap or renewable hours and flattens grid peaks.

new_nodes.label: Latent heat storage
new_nodes.detail: Stores energy in phase transitions, giving high density with little loss.

ideas.rationale: Buffering energy in a thermal store lets the oven draw cheap, low-carbon power at off-peak times, cutting both the cost and the grid strain of each cooking cycle.

new_nodes.detail: Lower-frequency microwaves penetrate further into dense frozen food, so the core thaws with less surface overheating.

new_nodes.detail: Delivers thaw energy to the centre of a frozen block instead of only heating the outer layer.

ideas.title: Thermal Conduction Plate Replaces Turntable

new_nodes.detail: A flat, heat-conductive plate that replaces the glass turntable and is warmed by the cavity to draw heat up into the food's underside.

new_nodes.label: Conduct heat into food base
new_nodes.detail: Transfers heat by conduction from below, so the food thaws from both sides at once.

new_nodes.label: Conductive heat spreading
new_nodes.detail: Uses high-conductivity metal to spread heat evenly across the tray.

ideas.rationale: Adding bottom-up conduction to microwave energy lets a frozen block thaw from both sides, which speeds defrosting for M4.

new_nodes.detail: A small infrared sensor in the ceiling that replaces the lamp and maps cold spots in the food.

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermography
new_nodes.detail: Reads surface temperature without light, so it works in a dark, heated cavity.

ideas.title: Load-Sensing Timer Replaces Clock Knob

new_nodes.detail: Electrodes in the cavity floor measure how the food's dielectric properties change as it thaws, replacing the dial.

new_nodes.label: Auto-stop at thaw point
new_nodes.detail: Ends the defrost cycle when the sensor reads the target phase, not a guessed time.

new_nodes.label: Capacitive phase detection
new_nodes.detail: Ice and water have different dielectric constants, so the sensor can tell when thawing is complete.

ideas.rationale: Stopping when the food reaches the right thaw state avoids both under-thawing and cooking, which speeds up defrosting for M4.

new_nodes.detail: A small electronic controller that varies power continuously and in real time, replacing the mechanical 5-step cam.

new_nodes.label: Closed-loop power control
new_nodes.detail: Feedback from the load sensor sets the power level continuously.

ideas.rationale: Continuous power control matches the heat to the food's thaw state, cutting cook-through risk while shortening the defrost cycle for M4.

new_nodes.detail: Output power is set by drive level rather than on/off duty cycling, so low-power defrost runs without thermal cycling.

ideas.title: 27 MHz capacitive tempering plates replace magnetron defrost

new_nodes.label: 27.12 MHz capacitive electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Two parallel plates above and below the frozen load, driven by a solid-state 27 MHz oscillator in a dedicated defrost mode.

new_nodes.label: Radio-frequency (ISM 27 MHz) dielectric tempering
new_nodes.detail: Lower frequency gives deeper, more uniform penetration into frozen blocks than 2.45 GHz; used industrially to temper frozen meat.

new_nodes.detail: A solid-state RF generator drives paired electrodes, so the food itself is the dielectric load and heats throughout its volume rather than from the surface inward.

new_nodes.detail: A transistor RF amplifier at 27.12 MHz replaces the 2.45 GHz magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Parallel electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Two insulated metal plates above and below the food replace the waveguide and metal cavity walls.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric penetration heating
new_nodes.detail: Energy penetrates thick frozen blocks more evenly than surface-concentrated microwave heating, reducing cold cores.

ideas.rationale: Volumetric RF heating thaws thick frozen blocks more uniformly and quickly, directly reducing the time to a fully defrosted centre (M4).

ideas.title: Impedance-sensing thaw-end detector

new_nodes.label: Dielectric loss-tangent sensing
new_nodes.detail: Continuous measurement of the load's complex impedance, which shifts sharply when ice melts into liquid water.

new_nodes.label: Impedance sensor electrodes
new_nodes.detail: Two coated contacts in the cavity floor measure load impedance throughout the cycle.

new_nodes.label: Automatic thaw-end detection
new_nodes.detail: Reduces or stops power when the food reaches the near-0°C liquid-surface state, instead of relying on a guessed time.

new_nodes.label: Non-uniform ice-to-water transition
new_nodes.detail: The averaged impedance reading can trip before pockets of ice in the centre have melted.

ideas.rationale: Sensing the physical ice-to-water transition replaces a guessed timer, so defrost stops at the right point and frozen food is neither left icy nor overcooked (M4).

ideas.title: Phase-change thermal platen

new_nodes.label: Salt-hydrate latent heat storage
new_nodes.detail: Sodium acetate trihydrate stores about 260 kJ/kg at its roughly 58°C melting point and releases that heat at a steady temperature.

new_nodes.label: PCM heat platen
new_nodes.detail: A sealed aluminium-clad tray of sodium acetate trihydrate, with a graphite-loaded base that absorbs microwaves to charge it, replaces the glass turntable and conducts heat into the food.

new_nodes.label: Conductive thermal buffering
new_nodes.detail: Holds the food-contact temperature steady, so the underside melts without hot spots that overcook the edges.

new_nodes.label: Edge overheating at contact points
new_nodes.detail: Uneven hot spots at the contact surface cook the edges while the centre stays frozen.

ideas.rationale: Storing microwave energy in a platen and releasing it steadily into the underside of the food adds conductive thawing that speeds up defrosting while protecting the edges (M4).

ideas.title: Steam-saturated condensing defrost chamber

new_nodes.label: Condensing steam heat transfer
new_nodes.detail: Steam condensing on a colder surface releases about 2.26 MJ/kg of latent heat, far faster than convection through dry air.

new_nodes.label: Steam-saturated cavity atmosphere
new_nodes.detail: The cavity is filled with saturated steam at about 100°C instead of dry air, with an ultrasonic piezo atomizer injecting fine water mist that flashes to steam.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat surface transfer
new_nodes.detail: Condensation delivers energy to every exposed frozen surface at a rate well above dry heating.

new_nodes.label: Condensate wets food surfaces
new_nodes.detail: Condensed water can soak packaging or pool around food, making surfaces soggy.

ideas.rationale: Saturated steam delivers latent heat to frozen surfaces far faster than dry air, so food thaws much sooner (M4).

ideas.title: Mass-matched pulse-rest scheduler

new_nodes.label: Pulse-rest thermal equilibration
new_nodes.detail: Microwave bursts alternate with rest periods, so heat conducts from the warmed outer layer into the frozen core before the next burst.

new_nodes.label: Load-cell weighing platform
new_nodes.detail: A strain gauge under the cavity floor estimates food mass and sets the energy budget for the cycle.

new_nodes.label: Firmware duty-cycle scheduler
new_nodes.detail: A microcontroller sets burst length and rest interval from mass and temperature history, replacing the mechanical cam.

new_nodes.label: Mass-matched energy dosing
new_nodes.detail: Energy delivered is proportional to load mass, so small and large packs thaw in comparable times without overheating.

new_nodes.label: Fixed power steps mismatch load mass
new_nodes.detail: Five fixed power levels cannot match the wide range of frozen loads.

new_edges.from: Fixed power steps mismatch load mass

ideas.rationale: Matching energy to the actual frozen mass and letting heat equilibrate between bursts shortens thaw time for any pack size without scorching it (M4).

ideas.title: Aroma Bell: Scent Release Replaces the End-of-Timer Bell

new_nodes.label: Olfactory completion cue
new_nodes.detail: Signals that cooking is finished through a distinct smell, which the user can detect from another room.

new_nodes.label: Microfluidic volatile dispensing
new_nodes.detail: Metered release of volatile compounds through a micro-valve, controlled by the cycle controller.

ideas.title: Weighing Turntable: Mass Loss as a Doneness Gauge

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable
new_nodes.detail: Turntable plate mounted on strain-gauge load cells that measure food mass continuously during cooking.

new_nodes.label: Moisture-loss doneness estimate
new_nodes.detail: Converts cumulative mass loss from evaporation into a percentage of the target dryness or doneness.

new_nodes.label: Continuous gravimetric sensing
new_nodes.detail: Load-cell signal processing that tracks weight change in real time.

ideas.rationale: It replaces the passive glass turntable with a sensor so the user gets a direct, quantitative readout of how much moisture the food has lost, which tracks doneness better than elapsed time.

ideas.title: Haptic Door Handle: Touch-Based Countdown

new_nodes.label: Haptic door handle
new_nodes.detail: Door grip with an embedded eccentric-mass vibration motor that pulses at a rate proportional to the remaining cook time.

new_nodes.label: Tactile remaining-time signal
new_nodes.detail: Communicates how much cooking time remains through touch, without requiring the user to look at a display or hear a sound.

new_nodes.label: Haptic pulse-rate encoding
new_nodes.detail: Maps remaining time to vibration pulse frequency and pattern.

ideas.rationale: It replaces the door push-release button with a handle that tells the user how long remains by touch, so feedback is available in a dark kitchen or to a user who cannot see or hear the appliance.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Tray: Colour Change at Serving Temperature

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic turntable plate
new_nodes.detail: Food-safe ceramic plate with a thermochromic layer that changes colour when its surface reaches a set temperature, correlated with food core temperature.

new_nodes.label: Visual temperature threshold indicator
new_nodes.detail: Shows by colour change whether the food has reached a safe serving temperature.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigment systems
new_nodes.detail: Reversible or irreversible colour-changing pigments that respond to temperature thresholds.

ideas.rationale: It replaces the inert glass turntable with a surface that changes colour when the food is hot enough to serve, giving a direct visual readiness signal without any electronics.

ideas.title: Sonic Cavity: Acoustic Doneness Sensing Replaces the Lamp

new_nodes.label: Ultrasonic transducer pair
new_nodes.detail: Transmitter and receiver mounted in the cavity walls that measure how sound velocity and attenuation change as the food cooks.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic state inference
new_nodes.detail: Infers food state, such as boiling or solidification, from changes in the acoustic signal.

new_nodes.label: Ultrasonic time-of-flight sensing
new_nodes.detail: Measures the travel time and amplitude of ultrasonic pulses through the cavity contents.

ideas.rationale: It substitutes the lamp, which lets the user look inside, with a sensor that reports the food's internal state without requiring the user to watch it.

ideas.title: Hear-Done Cavity

new_nodes.label: Cavity acoustic pickup
new_nodes.detail: A miniature microphone behind the mesh picks up popping, bubbling and sizzling from inside the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Cavity microphone and speaker
new_nodes.detail: A cheap MEMS microphone and piezo speaker replace the 20-25 W filament lamp, with no bulb to burn out.

new_nodes.label: Streams cooking sound so the user hears doneness
new_nodes.detail: Activity audibly fades as food finishes, so the kitchen itself reports readiness.

new_edges.from: Streams cooking sound so the user hears doneness

ideas.rationale: Hearing the food settle gives the user continuous, ambient evidence of doneness, which satisfies the need to know when food is ready without anyone having to look.

ideas.title: Solid-State RF Defrost Plates

new_nodes.detail: Field governing RF energy generation and dielectric coupling.

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz solid-state RF dielectric heating

new_nodes.detail: Thaws the whole frozen block, including the centre, at roughly uniform speed.

ideas.rationale: Volumetric RF heating thaws the frozen core as fast as the surface, which removes the cold-centre, hot-edge problem that makes conventional microwave defrost slow and uneven.

ideas.title: Thermal Vision Cold-Spot Window

new_nodes.label: Infrared sensing
new_nodes.detail: Field covering thermal imaging and infrared detection.

new_nodes.label: Show frozen cold spots
new_nodes.detail: Displays the thawed and still-frozen zones so the user knows when to stop or flip.

ideas.rationale: Showing the frozen cold spots in real time tells the user exactly when a defrost is complete and where to reposition the food, so they stop wasting time on guesswork.

ideas.title: Core-Probe Auto-Thaw Replaces Timer Dial

new_nodes.label: Embedded sensor engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field covering thermistors, probes and low-power wireless sensing.

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob (base)
new_nodes.detail: Base product's mechanical 0-30 min timer and bell, being substituted.

new_nodes.label: Auto-set defrost duration
new_nodes.detail: Ends the defrost automatically when the core reaches a safe thawed temperature.

ideas.rationale: Measuring the food's core temperature replaces guessing a time, so defrost stops at the right point and users no longer have to babysit the oven.

ideas.title: Graphite Susceptor Tray Replaces Glass Turntable

new_nodes.label: Materials science
new_nodes.detail: Field covering conductive and microwave-absorbing materials.

new_nodes.label: Microwave susceptor conduction
new_nodes.detail: A microwave-absorbing graphite layer heats up and conducts heat into the food from below.

ideas.title: Pulse-Sip Thaw Controller Replaces Power Cam

new_nodes.label: Power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Field covering switching, power control and waveform modulation.

ideas.rationale: Reframing the end-of-cycle signal as a reward for efficient use changes what users care about, so they cut energy use without any hardware gain in performance.

Detects thaw endpoint and sets duty cycle automatically

ideas.rationale: By reading the magnetron's own load response, the oven stops defrosting at the right moment without relying on a user-selected power level, so frozen food thaws quickly without overcooking the edges.

ideas.title: Solid-state RF engine replaces magnetron and HV chain

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Multi-stage gallium-nitride power amplifier running from a 48 V DC bus, replacing the magnetron, transformer, capacitor and diode.

new_nodes.label: Gallium-nitride HEMT power amplification at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Transistor amplifiers produce continuously adjustable RF power with no cathode, filament or kilovolt supply.

new_nodes.label: Continuously variable RF power without on/off cycling
new_nodes.detail: Output power is set by amplifier bias and drive, giving a smooth low-power thaw rather than pulsed heating.

new_edges.to: Gallium-nitride HEMT power amplification at 2.45 GHz

new_edges.from: Gallium-nitride HEMT power amplification at 2.45 GHz

new_edges.to: Continuously variable RF power without on/off cycling

new_edges.from: Continuously variable RF power without on/off cycling

ideas.rationale: A continuously variable low-power RF output removes the on/off pulsing that makes thawing slow and uneven, and it does so without the magnetron's wear-out life and lethal high-voltage supply.

ideas.title: 27 MHz capacitive electrode shelf

new_nodes.label: Parallel-plate RF electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Two perforated plates flank the food, replacing the waveguide duct and the mica cover.

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz solid-state RF driver
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost solid-state oscillator and matching network that drives the electrode pair.

new_nodes.label: Capacitive RF heating at 27.12 MHz
new_nodes.detail: The ISM-band field heats food throughout its volume and penetrates thick frozen blocks more deeply than 2.45 GHz.

new_nodes.label: Heats thick frozen blocks volumetrically through capacitive coupling
new_nodes.detail: The field reaches the centre of a frozen block, so the core thaws along with the surface.

new_edges.to: Heats thick frozen blocks volumetrically through capacitive coupling

new_edges.from: Heats thick frozen blocks volumetrically through capacitive coupling

ideas.rationale: A lower-frequency capacitive field penetrates a frozen block evenly from the outside in, so the centre thaws alongside the surface and the defrost takes less time.

ideas.title: Airflow-driven mode stirrer replaces turntable drive

new_nodes.label: Cooling-airflow-driven rotary mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: Metal impeller vane in the cavity, turned by air from the existing magnetron cooling fan, replaces the turntable motor and roller ring.

new_nodes.label: Impeller drive from cooling airflow
new_nodes.detail: Air moving through a small turbine hub gives the stirrer rotation without a separate motor.

new_nodes.label: Standing-wave pattern is fixed in a stationary cavity
new_nodes.detail: Without rotation or stirring, the field pattern leaves persistent cold spots in frozen food.

new_edges.to: Standing-wave pattern is fixed in a stationary cavity

ideas.rationale: Continuously moving the field pattern removes the standing-wave cold spots that stop frozen food from thawing evenly, and it does so with fewer parts and no motor.

ideas.title: Conductive-thaw ceramic tray

new_nodes.label: RF-absorbing ceramic thermal-bridge tray
new_nodes.detail: Silicon-carbide and ferrite composite tray that absorbs some RF and conducts heat into the food's underside, replacing transparent glass.

new_nodes.label: Thermal-bridge heating via RF-absorbing ceramic composite
new_nodes.detail: The tray warms under the field and transfers heat by conduction into the contact surface of ice.

new_nodes.label: Conducts heat into frozen food base to start thaw
new_nodes.detail: Supplies heat to the ice from below, so thaw starts even where the food itself absorbs little microwave energy.

new_nodes.label: Frozen food absorbs very little 2.45 GHz energy
new_nodes.detail: Ice has far lower dielectric loss than liquid water, so frozen food barely heats at the start of a defrost.

new_edges.to: Thermal-bridge heating via RF-absorbing ceramic composite

new_edges.from: Thermal-bridge heating via RF-absorbing ceramic composite

new_edges.to: Conducts heat into frozen food base to start thaw

new_edges.from: Conducts heat into frozen food base to start thaw
Conducts heat into frozen food base to start thaw

new_edges.to: Frozen food absorbs very little 2.45 GHz energy

ideas.rationale: Supplying heat from the tray into the ice's base gets thawing started where the frozen food itself barely absorbs microwave energy, shortening the time before normal dielectric heating takes over.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Doneness Wall

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic doneness enamel
new_nodes.detail: Cavity wall enamel with a colour-shifting layer that changes when food reaches serving temperature, replacing the interior lamp.

new_nodes.label: Interior lamp (20-25 W incandescent)
new_nodes.detail: Legacy lamp removed; it was the only means of viewing food during cooking.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic leuco-dye pigment
new_nodes.detail: Organic dye that changes colour at a set temperature with no power input.

new_nodes.label: Shows doneness with zero electricity
new_nodes.detail: Signals readiness through colour change instead of illumination.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 20-25 W lamp with a colour-shifting wall lets users judge doneness with no electrical draw, and because the colour cue reduces needless door-opening checks, it also cuts heat loss.

ideas.title: Steam-Turbine Turntable

new_nodes.label: Steam-turbine turntable drive
new_nodes.detail: Small impulse wheel under the plate, spun by food steam vented through the cavity louvres, replacing the 5 rpm motor.

new_nodes.label: Impulse steam turbine
new_nodes.detail: Bucket wheel that converts the kinetic energy of a steam jet into slow rotation.

new_nodes.label: Rotates food with zero electrical draw
new_nodes.detail: Steam-powered rotation of the turntable for even heating.

new_edges.to: Rotates food with zero electrical draw

new_edges.from: Rotates food with zero electrical draw
Rotates food with zero electrical draw

ideas.rationale: Harvesting the steam that would otherwise escape through the vents to spin the plate turns a lost energy stream into useful motion and removes the motor's electricity draw.

ideas.title: Solid-State Low-Voltage Oven

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier array
new_nodes.detail: Transistor array that produces 2.45 GHz directly from low-voltage DC, replacing the magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Switch-mode DC supply (48 V)
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency converter that replaces the HV transformer, capacitor and diode stack.

new_nodes.label: GaN HEMT power amplification
new_nodes.detail: Gallium-nitride transistors that amplify microwave signals at high efficiency.

new_nodes.label: Switch-mode power conversion
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency DC-DC conversion using compact magnetics.

new_nodes.label: Generates 2.45 GHz from low-voltage DC
new_nodes.detail: Direct RF synthesis that avoids a kilovolt stage.

ideas.rationale: Running the RF amplifier at low voltage with no transformer or resonant stage removes most conversion losses and lets more of the mains draw become energy in the food.

ideas.title: Flush Cavity-Wall Antenna

new_nodes.label: Flush patch antenna on cavity wall
new_nodes.detail: Printed copper radiator on the cavity wall that feeds RF straight into the chamber, replacing the duct.

new_nodes.label: Ceramic splatter plate
new_nodes.detail: Glazed ceramic sheet flush with the wall that blocks splatter and replaces the mica cover.

new_nodes.label: Printed microstrip patch antenna
new_nodes.detail: Planar resonant radiator printed on a dielectric substrate.

new_nodes.label: Delivers RF with near-zero line loss
new_nodes.detail: Couples microwave energy into the cavity without a transmission duct.

new_edges.from: Flush patch antenna on cavity wall
Flush patch antenna on cavity wall
Flush patch antenna on cavity wall
new_edges.to: Delivers RF with near-zero line loss

new_edges.from: Delivers RF with near-zero line loss
Flush patch antenna on cavity wall

new_edges.to: Flush patch antenna on cavity wall

new_edges.from: Flush patch antenna on cavity wall

ideas.rationale: Removing the waveguide duct and its transmission losses means more of the magnetron's output reaches the food, so the same cooking uses less electricity.

ideas.title: Plate-Sized Mesh Dome

new_nodes.label: Perforated mesh food dome
new_nodes.detail: Small metal-mesh dome over the plate; holes under about 6 mm reflect 2.45 GHz while letting light and steam pass.

new_nodes.label: Sub-wavelength mesh screening
new_nodes.detail: Perforations much smaller than a twentieth of the wavelength act as a solid reflector to microwaves.

new_nodes.label: Confines field to the food volume
new_nodes.detail: Limits heating to the food and reduces stray field and wasted air heating.

new_edges.to: Confines field to the food volume

new_edges.from: Confines field to the food volume
Confines field to the food volume

ideas.rationale: A dome sized to the plate means the magnetron heats only the food rather than about 20 L of air and steel, so less energy is wasted on each meal.

ideas.title: Vapour-Sensing Doneness Loop

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide vapour sensor
new_nodes.detail: Heated metal-oxide element whose resistance falls as water vapour and volatiles rise; a plateau in the trend marks doneness.

new_nodes.label: Exhaust-duct vapour sensor
new_nodes.detail: One low-cost metal-oxide sensor in the exhaust path replaces the motor-driven cam timer as the cycle controller.

new_nodes.label: Detects food state and triggers end-of-cook
new_nodes.detail: Closed-loop end-point detection from the sensed vapour curve instead of elapsed minutes.

new_edges.to: Detects food state and triggers end-of-cook

new_edges.from: Detects food state and triggers end-of-cook

ideas.rationale: The user is told when the food is actually ready, sensed from the food itself, rather than when an arbitrary number of minutes has elapsed.

ideas.title: Weigh-the-Plate Doneness

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge load cell (Wheatstone bridge)
new_nodes.detail: Metal-foil strain gauges in a bridge read mass to about 1 g; the mass lost tracks water evaporated from the food.

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable support
new_nodes.detail: The glass tray rests on three load cells beneath the cavity floor, outside the RF field, so the plain turntable becomes a scale.

new_nodes.label: Measures moisture loss as a doneness proxy
new_nodes.detail: The weight-loss curve gives a food-state readout that is independent of wattage setting and portion size.

new_edges.to: Measures moisture loss as a doneness proxy

new_edges.from: Measures moisture loss as a doneness proxy

ideas.rationale: Weight loss from the plate gives a direct, measured signal of how cooked the food is, so the user learns the food's state instead of guessing from a dial.

ideas.title: Door That Pops Open When Ready

new_nodes.label: Nitinol shape-memory wire actuator
new_nodes.detail: Nickel-titanium wire contracts when a 2 W electrical pulse heats it, releasing a latch without a motor or solenoid.

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded door-ajar latch
new_nodes.detail: At cycle end the door is sprung to crack open about 15 mm, venting steam; an interlock confirms the magnetron is off before release.

new_nodes.label: Signals end of cooking by movement
new_nodes.detail: A visible gap and a touchable cue work in noisy kitchens and for users who cannot hear a bell.

new_edges.to: Signals end of cooking by movement

new_edges.from: Signals end of cooking by movement

ideas.rationale: The door itself announces that cooking has finished, through a visible and tactile signal that does not depend on hearing the bell.

ideas.title: Thermal Heat-Map in Place of the Lamp

new_nodes.label: Thermopile infrared sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost 8x8 thermopile reads food surface temperature without contact, through a 1 mm perforated plate that passes 8-14 um infrared but blocks 12 cm microwaves (T5 principle).

new_nodes.label: Thermal heat-map display on door rim
new_nodes.detail: A small colour display or LED ring shows hot and cold zones across the dish, replacing the lamp as the way the user sees the food.

new_nodes.label: Shows where food is still cold
new_nodes.detail: The heat-map reveals what the eye cannot see through the mesh, including the cold centre of a dish.

new_edges.from: Thermal heat-map display on door rim

new_edges.to: Thermal heat-map display on door rim

new_edges.from: Thermal heat-map display on door rim
new_edges.to: Shows where food is still cold

new_edges.from: Shows where food is still cold
Thermal heat-map display on door rim
Thermal heat-map display on door rim

ideas.rationale: The user gets a quantitative readout of which parts of the food are done and which are not, which tells them more than a dim bulb showing the food is in the oven.

ideas.title: Doneness Label Travels With the Food

new_nodes.label: Enzymatic time-temperature indicator
new_nodes.detail: Enzyme-substrate film whose colour front advances with cumulative heat exposure, giving a per-portion readout.

new_nodes.label: Doneness label on food packaging
new_nodes.detail: A printed indicator strip on the food pack replaces the appliance bell as the ready signal, so it stays with the item.

new_nodes.label: Signals readiness per portion on the food itself
new_nodes.detail: Each item reports its own state, so mixed loads and reheats are each read correctly.

new_edges.to: Signals readiness per portion on the food itself

new_edges.from: Signals readiness per portion on the food itself

ideas.rationale: Each portion carries its own visible readiness indicator, so the user can see which item is done without relying on a single appliance-level alarm.

ideas.title: Sensing Stop

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob and bell
new_nodes.detail: Original 0-30 min mechanical timer, removed; it overcooks food and wastes energy.

new_nodes.label: Infrared and humidity surface sensor
new_nodes.detail: Watches the food's steam and surface temperature and ends the cycle when it is actually done.

new_nodes.label: Detect doneness
new_nodes.detail: Stops heating at the moment the food is ready, not after a guessed time.

new_nodes.label: Infrared and humidity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-power sensing that replaces guesswork with measurement.

ideas.rationale: Stopping at doneness instead of at a guessed time removes the wasted energy of overcooking, which is the largest hidden loss in a timer-driven microwave.

ideas.title: Dark-Glow Cavity

new_nodes.label: 20-25 W incandescent lamp
new_nodes.detail: Original interior lamp, removed; it draws power continuously to light the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescent cavity liner
new_nodes.detail: Coating that absorbs ambient light during the day and glows in the dark, lighting the interior at zero watts.

new_nodes.label: Let user see food inside
new_nodes.detail: Keeps the food visible without any electrical draw.

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescence
new_nodes.detail: Stores light energy from the room and releases it slowly.

ideas.rationale: Replacing a constantly powered lamp with a liner that runs on stored room light eliminates a 20-25 W load while keeping the cavity visible, so the user loses nothing they notice.

ideas.title: Passive Cradle

new_nodes.label: Motor-driven glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Original turntable and its drive motor, removed; the motor draws power and adds parts.

new_nodes.label: Fixed ceramic wave-reflector cradle
new_nodes.detail: Stationary dish with a reflective geometry that spreads microwaves evenly, so food heats without rotating.

new_nodes.label: Even heating across the food
new_nodes.detail: Achieves uniform heating without any motor.

new_nodes.label: Microwave reflection geometry
new_nodes.detail: Shapes the field so the energy distribution needs no mechanical stirring.

ideas.rationale: Removing the turntable motor deletes a standing power draw and a moving part while keeping even heating, so the cooking energy goes into the food.

ideas.title: Inverter Power Dial

new_nodes.label: 5-step duty-cycle power cam
new_nodes.detail: Original power knob that switches the magnetron fully on and off, wasting energy in start-stop cycles.

new_nodes.label: Variable-frequency inverter drive
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state drive that gives a continuous range of power output with no on-off cycling.

new_nodes.label: Deliver power at the needed level
new_nodes.detail: Supplies only the power the chosen setting requires.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state power inversion
new_nodes.detail: Modern electronics that deliver power with less conversion loss.

new_edges.to: Deliver power at the needed level

new_edges.from: Deliver power at the needed level

ideas.rationale: Continuous power matched to the load avoids the surge losses of cycling on and off, so each watt drawn does more cooking.

ideas.title: Waste-Heat Kettle Loop

new_nodes.label: Cavity wall heat leakage
new_nodes.detail: Heat that escapes through the cavity walls and is lost to the kitchen.

new_nodes.label: Thermoelectric heat-recovery panel
new_nodes.detail: Panel on the outer cavity wall that captures leaking heat and feeds it to a water reservoir.

new_nodes.label: Recover waste heat
new_nodes.detail: Turns escaping heat into useful warm water for the next use.

new_nodes.label: Thermoelectric generation
new_nodes.detail: Converts temperature differences into electricity or preheated water.

ideas.rationale: Capturing heat that would otherwise escape means the microwave's energy is counted twice, once for the food and again for warm water, which changes the user's sense of what the appliance costs to run.

ideas.title: Steam Scale Turntable

new_nodes.label: Load-cell glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Glass turntable sits on strain-gauge load cells that track the mass lost as water evaporates, replacing the 0-30 min clockwork timer knob.

new_nodes.label: Real-time moisture-loss tracking
new_nodes.detail: Converts measured mass loss into a doneness percentage shown on a small display ring.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge weighing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost load-cell electronics already used in kitchen scales.

new_nodes.label: Food thermodynamics
new_nodes.detail: Evaporative mass loss is a reliable proxy for cooking progress.

ideas.rationale: It tells the user how cooked the food actually is, not how long the machine has been running, so feedback comes from the food itself.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Window Glow

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door pane
new_nodes.detail: Door window coated with a thermochromic film that shifts colour across temperature bands, replacing the 20-25 W incandescent lamp.

new_nodes.label: Passive heat-state display
new_nodes.detail: Shows the interior's temperature zones as colour, with no electricity used.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic polymer film
new_nodes.detail: Leuco-dye or liquid-crystal film that changes colour with temperature.

new_nodes.label: Smart materials chemistry
new_nodes.detail: Engineered colour-changing polymers.

ideas.rationale: The door itself shows whether the food is still heating, cold, or steaming hot, so the user reads progress at a glance without opening the door or drawing power.

ideas.title: Crackle Listener

new_nodes.label: Acoustic doneness microphone
new_nodes.detail: A cheap MEMS microphone in the cavity that listens to steam popping and sizzling, replacing the clockwork timer and bell.

new_nodes.label: Sound-based doneness detection
new_nodes.detail: Tracks the decay of crackle rate and pitch and chimes when the food reaches its target state.

new_nodes.detail: A semiconductor amplifier that generates the 2.45 GHz microwave energy in place of a magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Power electronics and RF engineering

new_nodes.label: Phased-array antenna engineering

new_nodes.label: Move hot spots across the cavity without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Gives even heating of food without a motor, a rotating plate, or the drag they add.

ideas.title: Thermoelectric recovery of magnetron waste heat replaces the cooling fan

new_nodes.label: Thermoelectric generator on magnetron heatsink
new_nodes.detail: Bismuth telluride modules clamped between the magnetron heatsink and the cooling airflow, generating DC from waste heat.

new_nodes.label: Seebeck thermoelectric conversion
new_nodes.detail: Direct conversion of a temperature difference into electrical voltage.

new_nodes.label: Thermoelectric energy conversion
new_nodes.detail: Materials and module design for converting waste heat to electricity.

new_nodes.label: Power control electronics from waste heat
new_nodes.detail: Supplies the control board and display from the heat the magnetron would otherwise vent.

new_nodes.label: Standby control electronics
new_nodes.detail: Low-power board for the display, sensors and controls.

new_edges.to: Power control electronics from waste heat

new_edges.from: Power control electronics from waste heat

ideas.rationale: Turning the magnetron's rejected heat into electricity for the control board recovers energy that is otherwise lost to the kitchen, reducing the appliance's net mains draw.

ideas.title: Waste-heat Stirling turntable drive

new_nodes.label: Magnetron-coupled Stirling engine
new_nodes.detail: Small free-piston Stirling engine clamped to the magnetron heat sink, converting the roughly 30-40% of input power the magnetron wastes as heat into shaft motion.

new_nodes.label: Gear-free rim drive for turntable
new_nodes.detail: Stirling output shaft drives the roller ring by friction or magnetic coupling, with no mains-powered motor.

new_nodes.label: Thermoacoustic / Stirling heat-to-motion conversion
new_nodes.detail: Converts a low-grade temperature difference of about 80-120 K into rotary torque with no electrical input.

new_nodes.label: Recovers magnetron waste heat as turntable torque
new_nodes.detail: Turns heat that would otherwise be dumped into the room into the rotation needed for even heating.

new_edges.from: Recovers magnetron waste heat as turntable torque
Recovers magnetron waste heat as turntable torque

ideas.rationale: It removes the motor's electrical draw by running the turntable on heat that the magnetron would otherwise waste, so the appliance uses less energy per cook.

ideas.title: Static phased-array field steering replaces turntable

new_nodes.label: Phased-array feed antennas in cavity walls
new_nodes.detail: Four to eight small patch or slot antennas on the cavity walls, each with independent phase and amplitude control, steering the standing-wave pattern.

new_nodes.label: Electronic beam steering at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Relative phase shifts between feeds move hot spots across the food without any mechanical movement.

new_nodes.label: Electronically sweeps the field across the load
new_nodes.detail: Replaces mechanical rotation with a programmed sweep that also reaches off-axis positions the turntable cannot.

new_edges.from: Phased-array feed antennas in cavity walls

ideas.rationale: Removing the turntable motor, roller ring and their friction losses, and aiming energy directly where the food is, cuts wasted input power and heating time.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN amplifier replaces magnetron and HV chain

new_nodes.label: GaN-on-SiC 2.45 GHz power amplifier array
new_nodes.detail: Array of gallium-nitride transistor modules, each delivering about 100 W at 2.45 GHz, combined in a waveguide or patch combiner.

new_nodes.label: Low-voltage SMPS supply (24-48 V DC)
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency switch-mode supply at tens of kHz replacing the 50 Hz leakage transformer, voltage doubler and kilovolt capacitor.

new_nodes.label: Wide-bandgap solid-state RF amplification
new_nodes.detail: Class-E or Doherty-mode GaN amplification at 2.45 GHz with efficiency above 60% and no cathode to wear out.

new_nodes.label: Generates 2.45 GHz RF with high conversion efficiency
new_nodes.detail: Delivers microwave power at 2.45 GHz with fewer conversion stages and no kilovolt rail.

new_edges.from: Generates 2.45 GHz RF with high conversion efficiency

ideas.rationale: Solid-state amplification with a high-frequency supply avoids the magnetron's and the leakage transformer's conversion losses, which are a large share of the appliance's input power.

ideas.title: Reflected-power dielectric sensing replaces the clockwork timer

new_nodes.label: Waveguide reflected-power and phase sensor
new_nodes.detail: Directional coupler and detector in the waveguide that measure the reflected power and phase, which change as the load absorbs energy.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric load-state estimation
new_nodes.detail: Estimates the food's absorbed energy and temperature rise from reflected-power trends, so cooking can end when the target is reached.

new_nodes.label: Ends cooking when energy absorbed reaches target
new_nodes.detail: Stops the magnetron once the food has absorbed the needed energy, instead of running on a fixed clock.

new_edges.from: Ends cooking when energy absorbed reaches target
Ends cooking when energy absorbed reaches target
Ends cooking when energy absorbed reaches target
Ends cooking when energy absorbed reaches target

ideas.rationale: Stopping at the energy the food actually needs, rather than on a timer that runs past it, avoids energy spent on overcooking and on the standby losses of waiting.

ideas.title: Fibre-optic daylight light-pipe replaces interior incandescent lamp

new_nodes.label: Exterior-facing optical light collector
new_nodes.detail: Lens on the top or front of the casing that gathers ambient room light and channels it into the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Microwave-shielded polymer light-pipe
new_nodes.detail: Metal-free acrylic or fibre-optic guide running through a shielded port into the cavity, with mesh blocking microwave leakage.

new_nodes.label: Total internal reflection light guiding
new_nodes.detail: Guides visible light through a transparent polymer with near-zero loss and no electrical input.

new_nodes.label: Illuminates cavity with zero electrical power
new_nodes.detail: Provides visibility of the food for the user using ambient light, removing the lamp's 20-25 W draw.

new_edges.from: Illuminates cavity with zero electrical power
Illuminates cavity with zero electrical power

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 20-25 W lamp with passive daylight channelling removes a continuous electrical load and its heat while keeping the food visible.

ideas.title: Daylight Window: Passive Light-Pipe Replaces the Lamp

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp
new_nodes.detail: Existing 20-25 W bulb that lights the cavity so the user can check food; to be removed.

new_nodes.label: Fibre light-pipe optics
new_nodes.detail: Transparent acrylic light guides that carry ambient room light through the door window into the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Door light-pipe window
new_nodes.detail: Door panel with embedded optical fibres that draw in room light and spread it across the cooking space.

new_nodes.label: Visual inspection of food
new_nodes.detail: The user can see the food and check for mistakes without any electrical lighting.

ideas.rationale: Removing the 20-25 W lamp and using free room light keeps the same visibility while cutting the appliance's own electrical draw toward zero.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Done-Strip Replaces the Clockwork Timer Bell

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer and bell
new_nodes.detail: 0-30 min knob and bell that signal the end of a fixed cooking time, regardless of food state.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic done-strip
new_nodes.detail: Heat-sensitive strip on the door that changes colour when the food reaches a set temperature; needs no power.

new_nodes.label: Signal that food is ready
new_nodes.detail: Tells the user when to stop, so no time is spent overcooking.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigments
new_nodes.detail: Inks that change colour at a set temperature with no electricity.

ideas.rationale: Ending cooking at doneness rather than at a guessed time, with a passive colour cue, stops wasted energy from overcooking and removes the timer's need for power or a bell.

ideas.title: Susceptor Plate Replaces the Turntable Motor

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable and drive motor
new_nodes.detail: Rotating glass plate driven by a motor and belt to even out heating.

new_nodes.label: Microwave susceptor base plate
new_nodes.detail: Stationary ceramic-and-metal-film plate that absorbs microwaves and conducts heat evenly into the food.

new_nodes.label: Even heating across the dish
new_nodes.detail: Prevents cold spots without any mechanical movement.

new_nodes.label: Microwave susceptor materials
new_nodes.detail: Thin metal-oxide films that convert microwave energy into surface heat.

ideas.rationale: Dropping the motor and belt removes a continuous electrical load, while the susceptor directs energy into the food so less of it is lost to uneven heating.

ideas.title: Carry-Over Rest Cycles Replace the Five-Step Power Cam

new_nodes.label: Five-step power knob and duty-cycle cam
new_nodes.detail: Mechanical cam that switches the magnetron on and off in fixed ratios to simulate lower power.

new_nodes.label: Gentle cooking without high power
new_nodes.detail: Lets food heat slowly so it does not toughen or boil over.

new_nodes.label: Heat-soak cooking
new_nodes.detail: Uses residual heat inside the food to finish cooking during rest periods, with the magnetron off.

new_nodes.label: Carry-over (residual) heat
new_nodes.detail: Heat that keeps moving from the surface into the centre of food after the energy source stops.

new_edges.to: Five-step power knob and duty-cycle cam

ideas.rationale: Letting the food's own stored heat do the final work during programmed rests means the magnetron runs for less time, cutting energy use without the mechanical power-cam.

ideas.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Pre-Warms the Next Load

new_nodes.label: Exhaust vent
new_nodes.detail: Vent that lets hot steam and air escape from the cavity, carrying away heat that is lost.

new_nodes.label: Air-to-water heat exchanger
new_nodes.detail: Finned exchanger on the vent that transfers exhaust heat into a water reservoir or the incoming air.

new_nodes.label: Reclaim waste heat
new_nodes.detail: Recovers heat that would otherwise leave the kitchen through the vent.

new_nodes.label: Remove steam
new_nodes.detail: Keeps moisture from condensing inside the cabinet and on the controls.

new_nodes.label: Passive heat exchange
new_nodes.detail: Transfers thermal energy between two flows through a conductive surface, with no pump or fan needed.

ideas.rationale: Turning the exhaust that normally carries heat away into a passive heat source lets the appliance reuse energy it has already paid for, cutting net consumption for every later use.

ideas.title: Ambient light-pipe window replaces the interior lamp

new_nodes.detail: Existing 20-25 W lamp inside the cavity, replaced; it draws power for the whole cook cycle.

new_nodes.label: Rooflight light pipe

new_nodes.label: Cavity visibility
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user check food without drawing electrical power for illumination.

new_nodes.label: Total-internal-reflection light guiding
new_nodes.detail: Light is guided along a mirrored channel with low loss and no electrical input.

new_nodes.label: Continuous 20-25 W parasitic load

new_nodes.detail: Any optical opening risks RF leakage unless it stays below the cut-off dimension.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the continuously powered lamp with passively channelled room light removes the lamp's electrical draw while keeping the cavity visible, so the appliance uses no energy for seeing inside.

ideas.title: Energy-dose cooking replaces the clockwork timer

new_nodes.detail: Existing 0-30 min mechanical timer with end bell, replaced.

new_nodes.label: Thermal-dose controller
new_nodes.detail: Stops heating when the food reaches a target temperature or delivered energy dose, not after a fixed time.

new_nodes.label: Stop at target dose
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cook at the point of doneness so no energy is spent beyond it.

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermopile and dielectric load sensing
new_nodes.detail: Non-contact surface temperature and food-load impedance readings drive the stop decision.

new_nodes.label: Fixed-time cycles overheat and waste energy
new_nodes.detail: A timer cannot know when food is done, so it over-delivers energy.

new_nodes.detail: Produces the microwave field that heats the food.

new_nodes.detail: Several cavity feeds with cycled relative phase that sweep the standing-wave pattern without moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Uniform field without moving parts
new_nodes.detail: Even heating across the cavity with no motor and no rotating load.

new_nodes.label: Shorter cook time
new_nodes.detail: Derived function: even energy delivery finishes food in less time.

ideas.title: Load-cell turntable that weighs the food to infer doneness

new_nodes.label: Load-cell glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Glass turntable mounted on strain-gauge load cells that continuously read the food's mass, replacing the fixed-time clockwork timer.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge weighing
new_nodes.detail: Bridge-amplifier load cells with a microcontroller that logs mass against time.

new_nodes.label: Track moisture loss as a proxy for doneness
new_nodes.detail: Steam evaporation lowers mass in a predictable curve, so the microwave signals when the curve reaches the programmed target.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer (base, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Original 0-30 min clockwork timer knob with bell, which counts time and ignores what the food is doing.

new_edges.to: Track moisture loss as a proxy for doneness

new_edges.from: Track moisture loss as a proxy for doneness

ideas.rationale: The user gets a readiness signal based on what the food is actually doing, not on a guessed time, so they know when it is ready without checking.

ideas.title: Acoustic doneness listening replaces the 5-step power cam

new_nodes.label: Cavity acoustic sensor
new_nodes.detail: Miniature MEMS microphone in the cavity wall that picks up the bubbling and popping of heating food.

new_nodes.label: Spectral audio classification
new_nodes.detail: On-board FFT and a small classifier that identify the rising-then-falling acoustic signature of food reaching simmer and then dryness.

new_nodes.label: Magnetron power controller
new_nodes.detail: Continuous-duty drive for the magnetron, able to modulate output in fine steps in place of the discrete duty cycles.

new_nodes.label: Detect food state from its sound and modulate power to match
new_nodes.detail: Keeps the food at the target state and reports when it is reached.

new_nodes.label: 5-step duty-cycle cam power knob (base, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Original mechanical knob that switches between five fixed power levels regardless of the food.

new_edges.to: Detect food state from its sound and modulate power to match

new_edges.from: Detect food state from its sound and modulate power to match

ideas.rationale: Reading the food's own sound tells the user what state it is in, so they are not left to infer it from a fixed power level and a guessed time.

ideas.title: Scent-release done signal replaces the bell

new_nodes.label: Microencapsulated aroma cartridge
new_nodes.detail: Small capsule bank in the top vent that releases a cooked-food aroma on command.

new_nodes.label: Microencapsulated fragrance release
new_nodes.detail: Heat-triggered or piezo-triggered capsule rupture that releases volatile flavour compounds into the kitchen.

new_nodes.label: Signal readiness through an olfactory cue
new_nodes.detail: A distinct smell tells the user the food is done, even from another room or with the door closed.

new_nodes.label: Electromechanical bell (base, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Original end-of-timer bell, which signals only that time has run out.

new_edges.to: Signal readiness through an olfactory cue

new_edges.from: Signal readiness through an olfactory cue

ideas.rationale: A recognisable food smell gives the user a readiness cue they can perceive without looking into the oven or hearing a bell.

ideas.title: Thermal-haptic door handle replaces the push-release button

new_nodes.label: Thermal-haptic door handle
new_nodes.detail: Door handle with a Peltier element and a capacitive touch surface that warms or cools to mirror the food's surface temperature when touched.

new_nodes.label: Peltier thermal haptics
new_nodes.detail: Thermoelectric modules driven by a controller that map a sensed temperature to a felt warmth or coolness.

new_nodes.label: Convey food temperature through touch at the point of access
new_nodes.detail: The user feels whether the food is hot, nearly ready, or cold just by reaching for the door.

new_nodes.label: Door push-release button (base, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Original button that releases the door latch and gives no information about the contents.

new_nodes.label: Cavity IR temperature sensor
new_nodes.detail: Non-contact infrared sensor that reads the food's surface temperature and feeds the handle.

new_edges.to: Convey food temperature through touch at the point of access

new_edges.from: Convey food temperature through touch at the point of access

ideas.rationale: The user feels the food's readiness in the act of opening the door, so the feedback arrives at the moment they would otherwise be guessing.

ideas.title: IR-transparent thermal window replaces the interior lamp and door holes

new_nodes.label: Microwave-shielding IR-transparent window
new_nodes.detail: Germanium door window with a thin conductive coating that blocks microwaves but passes mid-infrared light, replacing the perforated mesh.

new_nodes.label: Cavity thermal camera
new_nodes.detail: Low-resolution microbolometer array behind the window that images the food's heat distribution.

new_nodes.label: Microbolometer thermal imaging
new_nodes.detail: Uncooled microbolometer detection with a colour-mapping processor.

new_nodes.label: Display a heat map of the food so doneness is visible without light
new_nodes.detail: The heat map is shown on a small screen on the door or on the user's phone, so no interior lamp is needed.

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp (base, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Original 20-25 W lamp that lets the user see inside but shows nothing about temperature.

new_nodes.label: Perforated door mesh (base, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Original hole pattern that shields microwaves while letting visible light out.

new_edges.to: Display a heat map of the food so doneness is visible without light

new_edges.from: Display a heat map of the food so doneness is visible without light

ideas.rationale: A heat map shows the user where the food is hot and where it is still cold, which tells them when it is ready in a way the lamp and holes never could.

ideas.title: Solid-State Frequency-Sweep Amplifier Replacing the Magnetron

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF amplifier (GaN, 2.40-2.50 GHz)
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the fixed-frequency magnetron with a semiconductor source whose output frequency is swept across the ISM band.

new_nodes.label: Magnetron (base product, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Fixed 2.45 GHz tube whose single standing-wave pattern leaves cold spots in frozen food.

new_nodes.label: Frequency-swept field uniformity
new_nodes.detail: Sweeping frequency moves standing-wave nulls and hotspots so energy is spread across the load.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Semiconductor power conversion and frequency control enabling programmable, sweeping output.

ideas.rationale: Sweeping the microwave frequency removes the standing-wave hotspots that make frozen food thaw unevenly, so the whole load defrosts faster and more evenly.

ideas.title: Electronic Phased-Array Beam Steering Replacing the Turntable

new_nodes.label: Phased antenna array (4 to 8 elements)
new_nodes.detail: Set of feed antennas around the cavity whose relative phases are electronically controlled.

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable (base product, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Mechanically rotated plate that averages field non-uniformity by moving the food.

new_nodes.label: Electronic beam steering
new_nodes.detail: Phase control moves the energy focus across the frozen load without any moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Phase-coherent RF control
new_nodes.detail: Coordinated phase and amplitude control of multiple microwave feeds.

ideas.rationale: Moving the energy focus electronically over a stationary frozen block delivers faster, more uniform thawing than a turntable that only averages the field over time.

ideas.title: Reflected-Power Load Sensing Replacing the Mechanical Timer and Bell

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power impedance sensor
new_nodes.detail: Directional coupler and detector that measure how much RF power the load absorbs versus reflects.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer knob (base product, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Fixed 0-30 minute timer that ignores how much the food has actually thawed.

new_nodes.label: Adaptive end-point detection
new_nodes.detail: Stops heating when the absorption signature shows the food has crossed the thaw transition.

new_nodes.label: Real-time RF impedance estimation
new_nodes.detail: Continuous measurement of cavity load impedance from forward and reflected power.

new_edges.to: Mechanical clockwork timer knob (base product, replaced)

ideas.rationale: Stopping on the measured thaw transition, not on a guessed time, avoids both under-defrosting and cooking the edges of frozen food.

ideas.title: 27 MHz RF Capacitive Electrodes Replacing the Magnetron Cavity Source

new_nodes.label: Internal capacitive electrode plates (27.12 MHz)
new_nodes.detail: Cavity walls and a shelf act as opposed electrodes driven by an RF generator, heating the food dielectrically.

new_nodes.label: Magnetron microwave source (base product, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: 2.45 GHz source whose penetration into dense frozen blocks is shallow, so the core thaws last.

new_nodes.label: Deep volumetric dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Lower-frequency RF fields penetrate thick frozen blocks more deeply, heating the core as fast as the surface.

new_nodes.label: RF dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Heating of non-conductive materials by an alternating electric field in the RF band.

ideas.rationale: Lower-frequency RF penetrates a frozen block far deeper than 2.45 GHz microwaves, so the core thaws at roughly the same rate as the outside.

ideas.title: Microwave-Absorbing Susceptor Plate Replacing the Glass Turntable

new_nodes.label: Graphite-ceramic susceptor plate
new_nodes.detail: Plate that absorbs microwave energy and conducts heat into the underside of the frozen food by contact.

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable (base product, replaced)
new_nodes.detail: Transparent, microwave-transparent plate that adds no heat to the food.

new_nodes.label: Conductive heat from below
new_nodes.detail: Heat delivered by contact from the plate fills in the bottom of the frozen block that microwaves reach last.

new_nodes.label: Microwave-induced conductive heating
new_nodes.detail: Conversion of microwave energy into heat in a lossy solid, transferred by conduction.

ideas.rationale: Adding conductive heat from the underside speeds up the coldest, most shielded part of a frozen block, so the whole item defrosts faster.

ideas.title: Reflected-power food-state sensing replaces the timer knob

new_nodes.label: Magnetron reflected-power load sensing
new_nodes.detail: The magnetron's reflected RF power and cavity impedance change as food absorbs energy and its moisture state shifts; a directional coupler and a comparator read this change and infer the cooking state.

new_nodes.label: Directional coupler & reflected-power comparator
new_nodes.detail: A low-cost microstrip coupler on the waveguide feeds a diode detector and comparator that output a food-state signal to the controller.

new_nodes.label: Infers food readiness from load absorption
new_nodes.detail: Estimates when the load has reached its target state (e.g. reheated, defrosted) and triggers the end-of-cycle function.

new_edges.to: Infers food readiness from load absorption

new_edges.from: Infers food readiness from load absorption
Infers food readiness from load absorption
Infers food readiness from load absorption
Infers food readiness from load absorption

ideas.rationale: It replaces a clock with a measurement of the food itself, so the user gets a ready signal based on the actual state of the load rather than an elapsed-time guess.

ideas.title: Steam-actuated whistle replaces the clockwork bell

new_nodes.label: Steam-vent whistle at hinge
new_nodes.detail: A small pressure-activated whistle on the door hinge, opened by steam pressure from the cavity when food reaches boiling or vapour-release point.

new_nodes.label: Pressure-actuated acoustic reed
new_nodes.detail: A flexible reed or Helmholtz resonator that sounds when a set vent pressure is exceeded, needing no electricity or cam.

ideas.rationale: The alert fires when steam shows the food is actually at temperature, not when a timer runs out, so the signal reflects the food rather than the clock.

ideas.title: Thermochromic readout strip replaces the interior lamp

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic indicator strip on window frame
new_nodes.detail: A passive heat-sensitive ink strip on the door frame, shielded from RF, that changes colour as the cavity reaches set temperatures.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic leuco-dye colour change
new_nodes.detail: Leuco-dye microcapsules change colour at a defined temperature; the change is passive and needs no power or bulb.

new_edges.from: Thermochromic indicator strip on window frame

new_edges.to: Thermochromic indicator strip on window frame

new_edges.from: Thermochromic indicator strip on window frame
Thermochromic indicator strip on window frame
Thermochromic indicator strip on window frame
Thermochromic indicator strip on window frame

ideas.rationale: A colour change on the strip shows the food's heat state at a glance, without a bulb that can burn out and without any power draw.

ideas.title: Transparent display door replaces mesh window and lamp

new_nodes.label: Transparent display door glass
new_nodes.detail: A door glass with a see-through display layer and an outer, RF-shielding ITO film. It shows a live food-state bar and a readable cooking progress view.

new_nodes.label: Indium tin oxide shielded transparent display
new_nodes.detail: A transparent conductor gives both RF containment (sheet resistance low enough to reflect microwaves) and visible transmission, with the display driven from outside the cavity.

ideas.title: Aroma-cue diffuser replaces the bell

new_nodes.label: Aroma cartridge with micro-diffuser
new_nodes.detail: A replaceable cartridge holds a food-aroma compound (for example toasted or Maillard notes) and releases it through a vent when the food-state sensor signals ready.

new_nodes.label: Piezo micro-diffuser for volatile release
new_nodes.detail: A piezo-driven atomiser releases a metered dose of volatile aroma compound on command, with no heating element.

ideas.rationale: A scent of cooked food is a sensory cue the user reads without looking or listening, and it is released only when the food is ready.

ideas.title: Photoluminescent Cavity Glow

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescent (afterglow) phosphor coating
new_nodes.detail: Strontium-aluminate enamel glaze charges from ambient room light and glows inside the cavity, so no lamp draws power.

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescent cavity enamel
new_nodes.detail: Phosphor-loaded enamel on the cavity walls that replaces the 20-25 W incandescent lamp.

new_nodes.label: Lets the user see food inside without drawing power
new_nodes.detail: Provides the visibility function of the lamp using stored ambient light.

Lets the user see food inside without drawing power

ideas.title: Food-Tells-Time Load Sensing

new_nodes.label: Magnetron anode-current load sensing
new_nodes.detail: Tracks changes in magnetron anode current and reflected power as the food's dielectric load changes, estimating doneness.

new_nodes.label: Load-sensing control board
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost electronics that end heating at target dielectric state, replacing the mechanical 0-30 min timer knob and bell.

new_nodes.label: Stops heating when the food reaches target state
new_nodes.detail: Terminates microwave output automatically so no energy is spent on overcooking.

Stops heating when the food reaches target state

ideas.title: Convection-Driven Passive Stirrer

new_nodes.detail: A small vane rotor spun by the rising warm air already leaving the cavity through the vent.

new_nodes.label: Vent-driven turntable drive
new_nodes.detail: Converts the convective airflow into slow rotation of the turntable, replacing the 5 rpm AC motor.

Rotates food using waste heat airflow

ideas.title: Solid-State Field Amplifier

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz power amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Gallium-nitride transistor amplifier at 2.45 GHz that runs from low-voltage DC, with no HV cathode or filament.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the magnetron tube, HV transformer, capacitor and diode with a small, tunable RF source.

new_nodes.label: Delivers precisely metered RF power per zone
new_nodes.detail: Matches output to the actual load, avoiding wasted power and magnetron warm-up losses.

Delivers precisely metered RF power per zone

ideas.title: Phase-Change Residual Cooking

new_nodes.label: Phase-change thermal storage (paraffin-graphite composite)
new_nodes.detail: A latent-heat material layer in the cavity wall that absorbs excess magnetron heat and releases it slowly afterwards.

new_nodes.label: Thermal-battery cavity liner
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the bare enamelled steel liner with a liner that stores and returns heat energy.

new_nodes.label: Finishes cooking with stored heat after power-off
new_nodes.detail: Continues gentle heat transfer to food after magnetron shutdown, so the final minutes need no new electricity.

Finishes cooking with stored heat after power-off

ideas.title: Aroma Announcer

new_nodes.detail: Replaces the mechanical clockwork bell as the end-of-cook signal; detects aroma compounds that peak as food browns.

new_nodes.label: Scent diffuser fan

new_nodes.label: Signal doneness via smell

new_nodes.label: Electronic nose (MOS sensing)
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide sensor array that classifies cooking volatiles in real time.

new_nodes.label: Olfactory signalling
new_nodes.detail: Uses smell as an ambient information channel.

ideas.title: Dawn-to-Noon Glow

new_nodes.label: RGB LED light strip
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the 20-25 W incandescent lamp with a low-power LED ring that shifts colour over the cook.

new_nodes.label: Continuous progress display
new_nodes.detail: Shows how far through the cook the food is by colour, not by numbers.

new_nodes.label: Colour-mapped temperature feedback
new_nodes.detail: Maps the internal temperature curve onto a palette running from cold blue through amber to golden.

new_nodes.label: Ambient information design

ideas.title: Sizzle Fade

new_nodes.detail: Replaces the mechanical bell with a sound whose pitch and crackle track the food's moisture loss.

new_nodes.label: Sonic doneness cue
new_nodes.detail: Signals readiness through sound that falls silent as steam stops, so the quiet itself means done.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic emission analysis
new_nodes.detail: Reads the frequency of steam popping and bubbling to estimate how dry the surface has become.

new_nodes.label: Psychoacoustics
new_nodes.detail: Uses how humans perceive pitch and rhythm to convey state.

ideas.rationale: Letting the food's own sounds fade into silence tells people it is done in a way they can hear from anywhere in the home, serving M8 with a cue they understand instinctively.

ideas.title: Weigh-Out

new_nodes.label: Load-cell platform
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the glass turntable's passive support with a weighing platform that tracks mass lost to evaporation.

new_nodes.label: Mass-loss doneness readout
new_nodes.detail: Shows percentage of water lost, a direct physical measure of how cooked the food is.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge weighing
new_nodes.detail: Precision load cells measure small changes in mass during heating.

new_nodes.label: Food physics
new_nodes.detail: Relates moisture loss to doneness for common foods.

ideas.rationale: Measuring how much water the food has lost gives a grounded, physical answer to 'is it ready yet?', which addresses M8 directly rather than relying on guesswork about time.

new_nodes.label: Haptic interface design
new_nodes.detail: Conveys information through touch.

new_nodes.detail: Ceramic-enamel interior that shifts colour with surface temperature, so hot and cold zones show directly on the walls.
