ideas.rationale: Condensing steam delivers latent heat to the whole frozen surface far faster than dry air, so thawing time drops without drying the food.

ideas.title: Thermochromic thaw strip replaces the lamp and the bell

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic thaw indicator
new_nodes.detail: Microwave-transparent ink switches colour once the local temperature passes 0 °C, marking thaw.

new_nodes.label: Printed thermochromic strip on pack or tray
new_nodes.detail: A strip printed on the food packaging or tray that changes from frozen colour to thawed colour.

new_nodes.label: Photodiode colour sensor in door frame
new_nodes.detail: Reads the strip through the door window using a light path that needs no internal lamp.

new_nodes.label: Visual thaw-state check without internal light
new_nodes.detail: The user, or the appliance, reads thaw progress from the strip alone.

new_edges.from: Printed thermochromic strip on pack or tray
Photodiode colour sensor in door frame
new_edges.to: Visual thaw-state check without internal light

new_edges.from: Visual thaw-state check without internal light
Printed thermochromic strip on pack or tray
new_edges.to: Photodiode colour sensor in door frame

new_edges.from: Photodiode colour sensor in door frame
Photodiode colour sensor in door frame

ideas.rationale: A colour change on the pack shows thaw progress and completion directly, so the user no longer has to watch the food or wait for a timed bell.

ideas.title: Solid-state pulse-density power replaces the duty-cycle cam

new_nodes.label: Solid-state pulse-density power modulation
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron supply is switched at any duty cycle within millisecond-scale windows, replacing five fixed mechanical steps.

new_nodes.label: Zero-crossing SCR power switch
new_nodes.detail: A solid-state switch that fires at mains zero-crossings for quiet, precise duty-cycle control.

new_nodes.label: Equalisation rest intervals
new_nodes.detail: Timed low-power dwells let heat conduct from the warmed surface into the frozen core.

new_nodes.label: Edge overcooking during thaw
new_nodes.detail: Continuous high power heats the thawed outer layer while the core is still frozen.

ideas.rationale: Rest intervals between pulses let heat conduct into the frozen core, so the whole block thaws evenly without the thawed edges overheating.

ideas.title: Sulfur Plasma Glow

new_nodes.label: Microwave-excited electrodeless sulfur plasma
new_nodes.detail: Sulfur-filled bulb is energised by the cavity's own microwave field, so it has no filament.

new_nodes.label: Sulfur plasma cavity lamp
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the incandescent lamp; glows only while the magnetron runs, brighter at higher power.

new_nodes.label: Shows cooking is active and at what intensity
new_nodes.detail: Light intensity mirrors power level, giving a live sense of how hard the food is cooking.

new_edges.to: Shows cooking is active and at what intensity

new_edges.from: Shows cooking is active and at what intensity

ideas.rationale: A lamp that is powered by the cooking itself and brightens with heat gives continuous visual feedback on whether food is actually cooking, which is what M8 asks for.

ideas.title: Aroma Sentinel Replaces the Countdown

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide volatile organic compound sensor
new_nodes.detail: Cheap chemiresistor that rises in signal as food aromas build and then plateau.

new_nodes.label: Aroma sentinel
new_nodes.detail: Small sensor in the vent that detects when the food's smell peaks, signalling readiness.

new_nodes.label: Detects food-readiness from smell
new_nodes.detail: Ends cooking at the point the food is ready rather than after a guessed duration.

ideas.rationale: Sensing the food's own aroma replaces a guessed timer with a direct answer to 'is it ready?', which is the feedback M8 actually needs.

ideas.title: Scent Bell

new_nodes.label: Heat-activated fragrance wick
new_nodes.detail: Warmed wick releases a toast or roast aroma when triggered, with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Aroma diffuser vent
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the mechanical bell with a scent that drifts out of the vent at end of cycle.

new_nodes.label: Signals end of cooking by smell
new_nodes.detail: Tells the user the food is done through their nose, even from another room.

new_edges.to: Signals end of cooking by smell

new_edges.from: Signals end of cooking by smell

ideas.rationale: A ding is easy to miss, but the smell of finished food pulls people back to the kitchen, meeting M8 through a cue they cannot ignore.

ideas.title: Chirping Cook-Curve

new_nodes.label: Piezo resonant sounder
new_nodes.detail: Cheap piezo element that synthesises tones with no striker or spring.

new_nodes.label: Progress chirp generator
new_nodes.detail: Emits a rising pitch over the cook, then a bright chord at the end.

new_nodes.label: Conveys progress through sound
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user hear how far along cooking is without looking.

ideas.rationale: A pitch that climbs as cooking progresses turns a single end-point alarm into a continuous signal that answers M8 throughout the wait.

ideas.title: Progress Window

new_nodes.label: Sub-wavelength printed graphic on glass
new_nodes.detail: Printed or etched pattern on glass that stays microwave-opaque to a set level while showing a colour band.

new_nodes.label: Progress band shutter
new_nodes.detail: A cam-driven sliding band behind the door glass that reveals a coloured fill as the timer runs.

new_nodes.label: Shows how far through cooking the food is
new_nodes.detail: A coloured band fills across the door as time elapses, so progress is visible at a glance.

new_edges.to: Shows how far through cooking the food is

new_edges.from: Shows how far through cooking the food is

ideas.rationale: Turning the mesh window into a progress bar that the timer drives lets people see how long is left, so the wait itself feels informative rather than blank.

ideas.title: Reflected-Power Auto-Thaw

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power sensing via magnetron feedback
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron back-reflection rises as ice melts into liquid water, so it can be read through the existing HV circuit with no added sensor.

new_nodes.label: Auto-thaw controller (replaces 5-step cam)
new_nodes.detail: A microcontroller cycles the duty ratio automatically and steps power down as the reflected signal shows the food is thawing.

new_nodes.label: Selects thaw power from the food's own state
new_nodes.detail: Removes the user's guesswork about power level and time.

new_edges.to: Selects thaw power from the food's own state

new_edges.from: Selects thaw power from the food's own state
Selects thaw power from the food's own state

ideas.rationale: By letting the food's own reflected signal set the power, the parent no longer has to guess, so frozen meals thaw at the right rate on the first attempt.

ideas.title: Thaw Story Beacon

new_nodes.label: Thaw-progress LED ring with melody
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the incandescent lamp and bell: a colour ring fills as the thaw advances, and a short jingle marks completion.

new_nodes.label: Makes the thaw wait feel shorter and occupied
new_nodes.detail: Visible progress and a sound give attention something to follow, so the wait feels like activity rather than dead time.

new_nodes.label: Signals thaw status to a distant parent
new_nodes.detail: Pushes progress to the parent's phone so they can leave the kitchen while the children are still nearby.

new_edges.to: Makes the thaw wait feel shorter and occupied
Signals thaw status to a distant parent

new_edges.from: Makes the thaw wait feel shorter and occupied
Signals thaw status to a distant parent
Signals thaw status to a distant parent

ideas.rationale: Reframing the wait as visible, occupied progress makes a defrost feel quicker to the parent even when the thaw time is unchanged.

ideas.title: Susceptor Thaw Plate

new_nodes.label: Carbon-loaded susceptor base plate
new_nodes.detail: A cheap disposable or built-in plate that absorbs microwaves and conducts heat into the frozen underside.

new_nodes.label: Susceptor conductive heating
new_nodes.detail: A thin carbon- or metal-loaded film turns microwave energy into conductive heat that reaches regions the field misses.

new_nodes.label: Conducts heat to frozen underside and edges
new_nodes.detail: Adds a second, conductive heat path that fills the cold spots left by standing waves.

new_edges.to: Conducts heat to frozen underside and edges

new_edges.from: Conducts heat to frozen underside and edges

ideas.rationale: A conductive base brings heat to the frozen underside and edges, which the microwave field alone thaws slowly and unevenly.

ideas.title: Exhaust-Vane Mode Stirrer

new_nodes.label: Stamped steel stirrer vane on cooling-fan shaft
new_nodes.detail: A single stamped vane, spun by the magnetron's existing cooling air, stirs the field and replaces the turntable motor and roller ring.

new_nodes.label: Air-driven rotation (aerodynamic drive)
new_nodes.detail: Cooling airflow the oven already produces turns the vane, so no motor, gearing or coupler is needed.

new_nodes.label: Stirs the field to even out hot and cold spots
new_nodes.detail: A moving field pattern averages out standing-wave hot spots across the food.

new_edges.from: Stamped steel stirrer vane on cooling-fan shaft
Stamped steel stirrer vane on cooling-fan shaft
Stamped steel stirrer vane on cooling-fan shaft
Stamped steel stirrer vane on cooling-fan shaft
new_edges.to: Stirs the field to even out hot and cold spots

new_edges.from: Stamped steel stirrer vane on cooling-fan shaft
Stirs the field to even out hot and cold spots

ideas.rationale: Even thawing without a motor or turntable means frozen food defrosts uniformly on the first pass instead of needing repeated rotations and turning.

ideas.title: Flat-Slab Thaw Insert

new_nodes.label: Flat-slab tray insert
new_nodes.detail: A shaped tray that holds pre-frozen meals pressed into thin slabs, so every thaw front sits close to a surface.

new_nodes.label: Surface-to-volume thaw geometry
new_nodes.detail: Microwaves penetrate only a few centimetres, so thin slabs thaw through from both faces in a fraction of the time.

new_nodes.label: Shortens the depth microwaves must penetrate
new_nodes.detail: Reduces the thickness of frozen mass so the field thaws the whole portion, not just the outer shell.

new_edges.to: Shortens the depth microwaves must penetrate

new_edges.from: Shortens the depth microwaves must penetrate

ideas.rationale: Substituting a thick frozen block with a thin slab means the microwave only has to penetrate a short distance, so the whole portion thaws quickly and evenly.

ideas.title: Convection-spun turntable

new_nodes.label: Convection vane under turntable
new_nodes.detail: A light vaned rotor beneath the glass plate, spun by the hot air already rising from the food, with no motor.

new_nodes.label: Thermal convection drive
new_nodes.detail: Buoyant hot air pushes a vaned rotor, so the waste heat that cooks the food also turns the plate.

new_nodes.label: Rotates food by waste-heat convection
new_nodes.detail: Provides the even-heating rotation (F5) using zero electrical energy.

ideas.rationale: It replaces a continuously powered 5 rpm motor with a rotor driven by heat the cavity already produces, bringing the rotation's electrical draw to zero.

ideas.title: Kitchen light pipe

new_nodes.label: Ambient light pipe door panel
new_nodes.detail: An acrylic light-guide panel in the door that channels room light into the cavity, replacing the 20-25 W lamp.

new_nodes.label: Total internal reflection light guiding
new_nodes.detail: Light from the kitchen is trapped in the acrylic guide and leaks into the cavity through scattering dots.

new_nodes.label: Illuminates cavity for visual checking
new_nodes.detail: Gives the user the view they need to check food without a powered bulb.

ideas.rationale: It removes an always-on 20-25 W lamp and borrows light the kitchen already pays for, so visibility no longer draws energy from the appliance.

ideas.title: Doneness sensing from magnetron current

new_nodes.label: Anode-current doneness detector
new_nodes.detail: Reads the magnetron's own anode current, which shifts as the food's water content changes, with no extra sensor.

new_nodes.label: Load-impedance sensing
new_nodes.detail: The magnetron's loading changes as food heats and dries, and that change is detectable in the HV supply current.

new_nodes.label: Ends cooking at doneness
new_nodes.detail: Cuts power when the food is ready, replacing the guessed-time timer knob.

ideas.rationale: It stops the magnetron when the food is done rather than after a guessed time, so no energy goes into overheating food and no sensor hardware is added.

ideas.title: Switch-mode high-voltage supply

new_nodes.label: GaN switch-mode HV inverter
new_nodes.detail: A solid-state high-frequency inverter with a small ferrite step-up, replacing the 50 Hz iron transformer, capacitor and diode.

new_nodes.label: High-frequency switch-mode power conversion (GaN)
new_nodes.detail: Chopping mains at tens of kHz lets a tiny ferrite core step up the voltage with few conversion losses.

new_nodes.label: Delivers regulated HV DC to magnetron
new_nodes.detail: Produces the same ~4 kV DC as F2 with fewer losses, less stored charge and no mains-frequency hum.

new_edges.to: Delivers regulated HV DC to magnetron

new_edges.from: Delivers regulated HV DC to magnetron
Delivers regulated HV DC to magnetron

ideas.rationale: It converts mains to magnetron high voltage with fewer conversion stages and far less iron, cutting the idle and conversion losses that a 50 Hz transformer dissipates as heat.

ideas.title: Phase-change thermal flywheel plate

new_nodes.label: Phase-change thermal flywheel plate
new_nodes.detail: A turntable of ceramic-encased paraffin that absorbs heat during microwaving and gives it back to the food after power cuts out.

new_nodes.label: Latent heat storage
new_nodes.detail: A phase-change material stores energy at its melting point and releases it as it solidifies.

new_nodes.label: Stores and releases heat for carry-over cooking
new_nodes.detail: Lets food finish cooking after the magnetron stops, reducing the on-time needed.

new_edges.to: Stores and releases heat for carry-over cooking

new_edges.from: Stores and releases heat for carry-over cooking
Stores and releases heat for carry-over cooking

ideas.rationale: It banks waste heat during each microwave burst and releases it afterwards, so the same cooked result needs less magnetron runtime and therefore less electricity.

ideas.title: Photoluminescent Door Liner

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescent door liner
new_nodes.detail: Persistent-phosphor coating on the inner glass charges from kitchen light and glows inside the cavity, so the user can check the food with zero watts drawn during cooking.

new_nodes.label: Incandescent interior lamp (base)
new_nodes.detail: The 20-25 W bulb being retired from the design.

new_nodes.label: Visual inspection of food
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user see inside the cavity to check for mistakes without powering a light.

new_nodes.label: Persistent phosphor photoluminescence
new_nodes.detail: Passive storage and slow re-emission of ambient light.

new_nodes.label: Materials science
new_nodes.detail: Coatings and luminescent materials.

ideas.rationale: Removing the 20-25 W lamp eliminates a power draw on every cooking cycle while keeping the user's ability to check the food, which directly serves energy efficiency.

ideas.title: Steam-Sensing Auto-Stop with Phone Chime

new_nodes.label: Steam-sensing auto-stop
new_nodes.detail: Humidity and gas sensor reads the steam curve from the food and cuts the magnetron the moment it is done.

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob (base)
new_nodes.detail: The 0-30 minute mechanical timer being retired.

new_nodes.label: Phone chime alert
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the mechanical bell with a notification to the user's phone.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical bell (base)
new_nodes.detail: The end-of-cycle bell being retired.

new_nodes.label: Know when food is done
new_nodes.detail: Stops cooking at the right moment instead of by guesswork.

new_nodes.label: Guesswork overcooking
new_nodes.detail: Fixed timers lead to wasted energy on food that is already finished.

new_nodes.label: Humidity and gas sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-power sensing of moisture and volatiles from cooking food.

new_nodes.label: Environmental sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost gas and humidity sensor engineering.

ideas.rationale: Stopping at true doneness rather than at a guessed time cuts wasted cooking energy, and the phone chime removes a component while still delivering the alert.

ideas.title: Fan-Driven Mode Stirrer

new_nodes.label: Rotating mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A small vaned metal stirrer in the cavity spreads microwave energy evenly, driven by the existing vent-fan airflow rather than a separate motor.

new_nodes.label: Turntable and drive motor (base)
new_nodes.detail: The glass plate and its motor being retired.

new_nodes.label: Even heating
new_nodes.detail: Distributes energy across the food so no cold or overheated spots form.

new_nodes.label: Mode stirring in resonant cavities
new_nodes.detail: Changes the field pattern inside the cavity to even out heating.

new_nodes.label: Electromagnetic engineering
new_nodes.detail: Microwave cavity and field design.

ideas.rationale: Even heating without a dedicated turntable motor removes a continuously driven load and avoids reheating a glass plate, so cooking uses less energy.

ideas.title: Inverter Replaces the Duty-Cycle Cam

new_nodes.label: Variable-frequency inverter driver
new_nodes.detail: Continuously varies magnetron power at high efficiency, replacing on-off cycling.

new_nodes.label: 5-step duty-cycle cam (base)
new_nodes.detail: The mechanical power knob cam being retired.

new_nodes.label: Set cooking power
new_nodes.detail: Chooses how much energy reaches the food.

new_nodes.label: Cycling losses
new_nodes.detail: Repeated on-off switching wastes energy in ramp-up and ramp-down.

new_nodes.label: Switch-mode power conversion
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency switching power electronics.

new_nodes.label: Power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Converters and drivers for controlled energy delivery.

ideas.rationale: Continuous inverter power removes the switching waste of the cam, so each cooking level uses the energy it actually needs.

ideas.title: Pence-Per-Cook Dial

new_nodes.label: Pence-per-cook dial
new_nodes.detail: Replaces power-level labels with the running cost of each setting, lit by a live tariff colour from the smart meter.

new_nodes.label: 5-step power knob labels (base)
new_nodes.detail: The High, Medium-High and similar labels being replaced by cost.

new_nodes.label: Choose cooking power
new_nodes.detail: The user selects how much energy to spend on a cook.

new_nodes.label: Compare cost of cooking
new_nodes.detail: Shows the real cost of each setting so users can see the trade-off.

new_nodes.label: Default full-power habit
new_nodes.detail: Users reflexively select maximum power regardless of need.

new_nodes.label: Smart-meter tariff signal
new_nodes.detail: Live electricity price and carbon signal from the grid.

new_nodes.label: Behavioural economics
new_nodes.detail: Changing meaning and framing to shift choices without reducing options.

ideas.rationale: Reframing power levels as their cost in pence makes energy use visible and tempts users to pick lower settings, reducing consumption without any change in performance.

ideas.title: Daylight Light-Pipe Window

new_nodes.label: Non-imaging optics
new_nodes.detail: Design of light-guiding structures that transport ambient light without electrical power.

new_nodes.label: Fibre-optic daylight light-pipe
new_nodes.detail: Fibre bundle in the door frame channels room light into the cavity, with a microwave-safe metal mesh to block RF.

new_nodes.label: Passive light-pipe door insert
new_nodes.detail: Clear acrylic or fibre light guide that replaces the 20-25 W incandescent lamp.

new_nodes.label: Cavity visibility

ideas.rationale: Delivering exactly the power the food needs without cycling the magnetron on and off removes the start-up and cooldown losses that the duty-cycle cam produces.

ideas.title: Solid-state frequency-agile RF defrost head

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier array
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the fixed 2.45 GHz magnetron with phase-controlled GaN amplifiers that sweep frequency and power across the ISM band to match the dielectric loss of ice versus water.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride power semiconductors
new_nodes.detail: Wideband, high-efficiency RF power generation without a vacuum tube or high-voltage filament.

new_nodes.label: Frequency-agile dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Couples energy into ice and water fractions selectively, reducing hot spots and thawing time.

new_nodes.label: RF and microwave engineering
new_nodes.detail: Field in which the solid-state amplifier and sweep control are rooted.

ideas.rationale: Selective, swept-frequency coupling into ice rather than water fractions shortens defrost time while avoiding the cooked-edge and hot-spot failure of single-frequency heating.

ideas.title: Eutectic ice-sink platter replacing the glass turntable

new_nodes.label: Eutectic phase-change platter
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the glass turntable with a salt-hydrate platter that holds at about 0 °C while it absorbs latent heat, so exposed edges cannot rise above freezing.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat phase-change materials
new_nodes.detail: Materials that store and release energy at a fixed melting temperature.

new_nodes.label: Isothermal thaw holding
new_nodes.detail: Keeps the food near 0 °C during thawing, which stops edge cooking and runaway heating.

new_nodes.label: Edge cooking and thermal runaway
new_nodes.detail: Thin edges overheat while the centre is still frozen, which is the main defrost failure mode.

ideas.rationale: Holding the food at the melting point lets the whole load thaw evenly and quickly without the edge damage that defrost cycles normally cause.

ideas.title: Reflected-power endpoint sensor replacing the clockwork timer and bell

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power impedance sensor
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the mechanical clockwork timer and bell with a directional coupler that reads reflected power and the cavity load impedance to detect when the ice fraction has melted.

new_nodes.label: Directional coupling and load impedance sensing
new_nodes.detail: Electronic measurement of forward and reflected RF power, with no user-set time.

new_nodes.label: Automatic defrost endpoint detection
new_nodes.detail: Ends defrost when the load's dielectric signature changes from frozen to thawed.

new_edges.from: Directional coupling and load impedance sensing

ideas.rationale: Stopping on the measured physical change in the food, not on a guessed clock time, removes the overcooking that users currently cause when they defrost by timer.

ideas.title: Closed-loop pulsed power controller replacing the 5-step duty-cycle cam

new_nodes.label: Closed-loop pulsed power controller
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the 5-step mechanical duty-cycle cam with a microcontroller that modulates pulse width from cavity temperature and reflected power.

new_nodes.label: Embedded feedback control
new_nodes.detail: Digital closed-loop control of power delivery.

new_nodes.label: Adaptive pulsed defrost
new_nodes.detail: Delivers high power in short pulses with rest periods so heat can equalise through the frozen mass.

ideas.rationale: Pulsed rest periods let heat conduct into the frozen core, so the food thaws faster and more evenly than a fixed-duty setting allows.

ideas.title: Ultrasonic acoustic thaw bath replacing microwave energy

new_nodes.label: Piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer bath
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the magnetron and cavity with a water-filled chamber driven by piezoelectric transducers at 20-40 kHz that heat frozen food by acoustic vibration.

new_nodes.label: High-intensity ultrasound heating
new_nodes.detail: Converts acoustic energy into heat through viscous and frictional losses in the food.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric acoustic thawing
new_nodes.detail: Heats the bulk of the food by vibration and transmits heat through the liquid medium, with no RF or standing-wave hot spots.

new_nodes.label: Acoustics and ultrasonics
new_nodes.detail: Field in which the transducer and acoustic heating are rooted.

ideas.rationale: Acoustic heating reaches the whole frozen mass without standing-wave hot spots, which can thaw food faster and more evenly than microwaves.

ideas.title: Solid-state RF electrode thaw plate

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz solid-state RF generator
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the 700 W magnetron with a low-cost solid-state RF oscillator that drives the electrodes.

new_nodes.label: Parallel-plate electrode shelf
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the glass turntable with a pair of tray electrodes between which frozen food sits, so RF field penetrates the whole load evenly.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric RF heating
new_nodes.detail: Heats the load volumetrically at low frequency, which penetrates thick frozen blocks better than 2.45 GHz microwaves.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric thaw of frozen blocks
new_nodes.detail: Heats the centre of a frozen block as fast as the surface, reducing edge cooking.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the magnetron and turntable with a solid-state RF electrode shelf heats thick frozen blocks volumetrically and evenly, so they thaw faster than surface-heated microwave cooking.

ideas.title: Steam-condensation thaw chamber

new_nodes.label: Low-pressure steam generator
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the magnetron with a small boiler that produces ~100 °C steam in the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat condensation transfer
new_nodes.detail: Steam condensing on cold food releases about 2260 kJ/kg, a much larger energy transfer per unit than sensible heating.

new_nodes.label: Rapid latent-heat thaw
new_nodes.detail: Delivers heat to the frozen surface by condensation, which warms and melts ice quickly without microwave energy.

ideas.rationale: Replacing microwave emission with condensing steam uses latent heat, which transfers far more energy per contact than air or microwave heating and melts frozen food faster.

ideas.title: Phase-change thermal plate replaces turntable

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat plate
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the glass turntable with a sealed aluminium plate containing sodium acetate trihydrate, which melts at about 58 °C.

new_nodes.label: Latent heat storage
new_nodes.detail: Stores heat in a phase-change material so the plate delivers a steady high-temperature conductive pulse to the food.

new_nodes.label: Conductive bottom thaw
new_nodes.detail: Supplies heat conductively to the base of frozen food while the magnetron warms the top.

ideas.rationale: A pre-charged phase-change plate in place of the turntable adds conductive heat to the base of the food, so the bottom thaws as quickly as the top.

ideas.title: Reflected-power ice-melt auto-stop

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power monitor
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the clockwork bell timer with a directional coupler and detector that tracks reflected power from the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric loss sensing
new_nodes.detail: Ice has a much lower dielectric loss than liquid water, so the load's absorption changes measurably when the ice melts.

new_nodes.label: Automatic end-of-thaw detection
new_nodes.detail: Ends the defrost cycle when the loss signature shows the food has reached the thawed state.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the user-set clockwork timer with a sensor that detects when ice has turned to water stops the cycle at the right point, so frozen food is neither under-thawed nor cooked.

ideas.title: Load-cell energy calculator replaces timer and power cam

new_nodes.detail: Replaces the 0-30 min clockwork timer knob and 5-step power cam with a strain-gauge weight sensor under the turntable.

new_nodes.label: Infrared surface thermometer
new_nodes.detail: Reads the frozen food's surface temperature to estimate its starting energy state.

new_nodes.label: Energy-balance thaw control
new_nodes.detail: Computes energy as mass times (334 kJ/kg latent heat plus sensible heat), then sets power and time automatically.

new_nodes.label: Mass-based thaw dosing
new_nodes.detail: Delivers the energy needed for the measured mass and starting temperature, so the user only selects the food type.

ideas.rationale: Calculating the energy needed from the food's measured mass and temperature removes the guesswork from defrost timing, so frozen food thaws evenly the first time.

new_nodes.detail: Four or more feed ports driven at controlled relative phase create a steerable standing-wave pattern inside a fixed cavity.

ideas.title: Resonant high-frequency converter replaces the 50 Hz transformer and doubler

new_nodes.label: Resonant high-frequency switched-mode HV conversion
new_nodes.detail: A 100 kHz-class resonant inverter with a small ferrite transformer raises rectified mains to magnetron anode voltage, replacing the 50 Hz iron-core transformer.

new_nodes.label: Ferrite HF step-up transformer with resonant tank

new_nodes.label: Continuous variable power output without duty cycling

ideas.title: Adaptive-volume cavity with motorized RF-choke walls

new_nodes.label: Sliding quarter-wave RF-choke shutters
new_nodes.detail: Conductive shutters with quarter-wave choke grooves seal RF-tight at any position, so the cavity volume can shrink without leaking energy.

new_nodes.label: Movable cavity walls (dual sliding conductive panels)
new_nodes.detail: Two steel panels on rails, driven by a small motor, reduce the cavity from 20 L to about 3 L around a single cup.

new_nodes.label: Load-matched cavity volume
new_nodes.detail: Keeps field density high in the food and reduces energy absorbed by empty air and cavity walls.

ideas.rationale: Matching the RF-filled volume to the food stops energy being dumped into empty air and cavity walls, which shortens cook times and cuts wasted power.

ideas.title: Reflected-power load sensing replaces the timer knob

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power load-impedance sensing
new_nodes.detail: A directional coupler measures magnetron reflected power and the cavity's dielectric load to infer food mass, moisture and temperature in real time.

new_nodes.label: Directional coupler and reflected-power ADC
new_nodes.detail: A small coupler on the waveguide feeds a microcontroller that ends cooking when the food reaches a target absorbed-energy level.

new_nodes.label: Cook-to-doneness energy metering
new_nodes.detail: Stops RF output when the food reaches its target state, instead of running a fixed timer that overcooks.

ideas.rationale: Ending RF output when the food reaches its target state avoids the energy wasted on overcooking and on the extra minutes a fixed timer leaves running.

ideas.title: Reflected-Power Doneness Sensing

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power trajectory analysis
new_nodes.detail: Infers food state from how the magnetron's reflected power changes as the load's dielectric loss shifts with moisture and temperature.

new_nodes.label: Directional-coupler reflected-power reader
new_nodes.detail: The magnetron protection sensor already in the base unit is reused as the food-state sensor, with firmware watching for the plateau that marks the end of water phase change.

new_nodes.label: Estimate doneness from electrical load
new_nodes.detail: Converts the reflected-power curve into a ready/not-ready estimate with no camera, lamp, or probe.

ideas.rationale: It tells the user when food is ready by reading the food's own effect on the magnetron, so the user no longer has to guess a time and wait for a bell.

ideas.title: Acoustic Crackle Doneness Sensing

new_nodes.label: Cavity-wall piezo microphone
new_nodes.detail: A piezo disc bonded to the metal cavity wall picks up food crackle and bubbling, which are shielded from the magnetron's own noise by timing.

new_nodes.label: Crackle-frequency doneness classifier
new_nodes.detail: Maps the slowing and softening of popping or bubbling sounds, which reliably signal doneness, to a ready state.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic doneness estimate
new_nodes.detail: Tells the user the food is ready from its sound, without any light inside the cavity.

ideas.rationale: It replaces visual monitoring through the door with a sound-based readiness cue, so the user knows the food is ready without opening the door or looking in.

ideas.title: Scent-Plume Readiness Alert

new_nodes.label: Exhaust-duct VOC sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide gas sensors in the vent path detect the Maillard volatiles released as food browns or heats through.

new_nodes.label: Aroma pulse emitter
new_nodes.detail: A small cartridge of food-neutral aroma is released through a side vent when the VOC threshold is crossed, so the user smells the ready state across the room.

new_nodes.label: Ambient olfactory readiness alert
new_nodes.detail: Gives a non-auditory, non-visual cue that carries through the kitchen.

new_nodes.label: Cartridge replacement and odour carryover
new_nodes.detail: Aroma cartridges need periodic replacement, and scent can linger on the next dish.

ideas.rationale: It turns the smell of cooking into a readiness signal the user can detect from anywhere in the kitchen, so they do not have to stand over the microwave or watch it.

ideas.title: Haptic Progress Knob

new_nodes.label: Motor-driven timer knob
new_nodes.detail: A small motor on the existing timer shaft turns the knob back a detent per interval, so the knob position itself encodes the remaining time.

new_nodes.label: Tactile remaining-time readout
new_nodes.detail: The user feels the time left through the knob's position and resistance, which works in a noisy kitchen.

new_nodes.label: Tactile completion signal
new_nodes.detail: The knob clicks through a rapid detent sequence at the end of the cycle.

ideas.rationale: It gives a tactile readout of time remaining and a physical end-of-cycle signal through the knob the user already touches, so they always know how long is left without reading a display or listening for a bell.

ideas.title: Load-Cell Platter Moisture Tracking

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable hub
new_nodes.detail: The turntable is replaced by a platter on three load cells at the hub, so the rotating plate weighs the food continuously.

new_nodes.label: Evaporative mass-loss tracking
new_nodes.detail: Food is ready once its mass stops falling, because water loss has levelled off at the target temperature.

new_nodes.label: Mass-based doneness estimate
new_nodes.detail: Tracks weight loss as water evaporates and signals when the curve flattens.

ideas.rationale: It uses the turntable the user already has as a scale, so readiness is tied to how much water the food has actually lost rather than to a guessed time.

ideas.title: Ohmic Electrode Thaw: Magnetron Replaced by Food-Contact Electrodes

new_nodes.label: Magnetron (base)
new_nodes.detail: 700 W 2.45 GHz magnetron that heats food from the outside in, leaving frozen cores cold and surfaces cooked.

new_nodes.label: Stainless electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Two low-voltage electrodes on the cavity floor and lid that pass a controlled AC current through the food itself.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric resistive heating
new_nodes.detail: Current flowing through the ice and water generates heat throughout the food's volume, so the whole load thaws at once.

new_nodes.label: Ohmic heating
new_nodes.detail: Joule heating of conductive food using low-frequency AC applied through electrodes.

new_nodes.label: Electrical engineering / food processing
new_nodes.detail: Ohmic heating is established in industrial food processing and is applied here to domestic defrosting.

ideas.rationale: Heating the food volume directly, instead of from the surface inward, removes the cold-core problem that makes frozen food slow to thaw and uneven.

ideas.title: Frost-Core Probe Replaces Clockwork Timer and Bell

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer knob (base)
new_nodes.detail: Dial that sets a fixed 0-30 minute run time and rings a bell at the end, regardless of food state.

new_nodes.label: Thermistor core probe
new_nodes.detail: A slim, food-safe needle probe that tracks the coldest point of the load and reports when it reaches about -2 °C.

new_nodes.label: Stop at target core temperature
new_nodes.detail: Switches off power when the coldest point reaches the thaw threshold, preventing both under-thawing and cooking.

new_nodes.label: NTC thermistor sensing
new_nodes.detail: Resistance-based temperature measurement read by the control board.

new_nodes.label: Sensor engineering
new_nodes.detail: Embedded temperature sensing for appliance control.

ideas.rationale: Ending the defrost when the core reaches the right temperature, rather than after a guessed time, gives a reliable thaw for any load size.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Ice Window Replaces Interior Lamp

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp (base)
new_nodes.detail: 20-25 W bulb that lets the user see inside, but gives no information about how thawed the food is.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door film
new_nodes.detail: A printed film on the door glass that changes from blue to clear as the food inside passes through thaw stages.

new_nodes.label: Show thaw progress without opening
new_nodes.detail: Displays the thaw state through the door, so the user can judge readiness without losing heat.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigment
new_nodes.detail: Pigments that change colour at set temperatures, using the heat conducted from the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Materials chemistry
new_nodes.detail: Reversible colour-change materials.

ideas.rationale: Showing thaw state through the door removes the guesswork that makes users open the door and interrupt defrosting, while using no electricity.

ideas.title: Barcode-Driven Auto-Thaw Replaces Power Knob

new_nodes.label: 5-step power knob with duty-cycle cam (base)
new_nodes.detail: Manual selector that sets the power level, which the user must guess for each food and weight.

new_nodes.label: NFC tag on food packaging
new_nodes.detail: Passive tag printed on frozen food packs that stores the product's weight, type and recommended thaw profile.

new_nodes.label: Automatic thaw profile selection
new_nodes.detail: The oven reads the tag and sets power and pulse pattern to match the specific food and mass.

new_nodes.label: Near-field communication
new_nodes.detail: Short-range passive RF identification read by the oven.

new_nodes.label: Wireless identification / RFID
new_nodes.detail: Contactless identification and data storage on passive tags.

ideas.rationale: Matching the power profile to each packaged food removes guesswork and avoids the overheating that comes from picking a power level by hand.

ideas.title: Induction-Heated Susceptor Tray Replaces Glass Turntable

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable and drive motor (base)
new_nodes.detail: Rotating glass plate that shifts food through the field to even out microwave hot and cold spots.

new_nodes.label: Ferritic induction susceptor tray
new_nodes.detail: A thin stainless or ferritic metal tray that is heated by a coil under the cavity and passes heat into the food by contact.

new_nodes.label: Even conductive heat from below
new_nodes.detail: Supplies steady heat to the underside of the food, filling in the energy the microwave field misses.

new_nodes.label: Induction heating
new_nodes.detail: Eddy-current heating of a conductive load by a high-frequency magnetic field.

new_nodes.label: Power electronics
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency inverter and coil design for induction heating.

ideas.rationale: Adding conductive heat from below to the microwave field thaws the bottom of a frozen block that the field alone reaches slowly, and no moving parts are needed.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Door Window

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic liquid-crystal film
new_nodes.detail: Printed film that shifts colour across a temperature band, a cheap substitute for a filament lamp.

new_nodes.label: Colour-shifting door panel
new_nodes.detail: Door window strip that turns from blue (cold) to amber to red as the food heats.

new_nodes.label: Shows food temperature as colour
new_nodes.detail: The user reads heat progress at a glance without opening the door.

ideas.rationale: The door becomes a heat map, so the user gets continuous progress feedback with no bulb to burn out and no need to watch the food.

ideas.title: Scent Ding

new_nodes.detail: A cheap piezo mist element releases a small puff of the dish's aroma on completion.

new_nodes.label: Aroma end-of-cycle emitter
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the bell with a smell that says 'done' and that the user can smell from another room.

new_nodes.label: Signals completion by smell
new_nodes.detail: Completion is announced through olfaction, which is hard to ignore and tied to appetite.

ideas.rationale: The completion signal turns from a generic ding into the appetising smell of the finished meal, so the user knows the food is ready and wants to eat it.

ideas.title: Fading Sizzle Sensor

new_nodes.label: Acoustic sensing of boiling and sizzle
new_nodes.detail: A cheap piezo microphone tracks the bubbling and steam hiss, which change as the food heats and finishes.

new_nodes.label: Sound-tracking cook monitor
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the open-loop countdown with a listening device that reacts to the food itself.

new_nodes.label: Senses food state from sound
new_nodes.detail: Detects the food state from its acoustic signature, so feedback reflects the food and not the clock.

ideas.rationale: Closing the loop with sound lets the appliance announce doneness when the food is actually ready, which is the feedback the user needs.

new_nodes.detail: A cheap LED ring on the bezel, far cheaper and longer-lived than the interior filament lamp.

ideas.title: Impedance-Sensing Thaw Stop

new_nodes.detail: Conductive plates in the cavity wall measure the food's dielectric change as ice melts, replacing the mechanical 0-30 min timer knob.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric-state sensing
new_nodes.detail: Tracks the phase change from ice to liquid water in real time, so heating ends exactly at the thaw point.

new_nodes.label: Auto-detect thaw completion
new_nodes.detail: Ends the defrost cycle at the right moment without user guesswork.

ideas.title: Vibrating Tray Instead of Turntable

new_nodes.label: Electromagnetic vibration tray
new_nodes.detail: A flat tray driven by a solenoid that jiggles food to expose new frozen surfaces to microwaves, replacing the glass turntable and its motor.

new_nodes.label: Resonant electromagnetic actuation
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost coil and spring resonance moves the tray with no gears or bearings.

new_nodes.label: Continuous surface exposure
new_nodes.detail: Keeps every part of the frozen block facing the magnetron as it thaws.

ideas.rationale: Vibrating the tray keeps frozen surfaces facing the energy source, cutting thaw time and removing a motor and gear train that would otherwise add cost.

ideas.title: Wet-Bag Thaw Chamber

new_nodes.label: Circulating warm-water thaw jacket
new_nodes.detail: A sealed cavity filled with 30 °C water that circulates past the food, replacing the magnetron-only heat path for the defrost stage.

new_nodes.label: Forced-convection water heating
new_nodes.detail: A small pump and heater deliver even, gentle heat without hot spots.

new_nodes.label: Gentle uniform thaw
new_nodes.detail: Thaws frozen food evenly from every side with no edge cooking.

ideas.rationale: Using circulating warm water rapidly and evenly defrosts food from all sides, avoiding the uneven hot spots that slow or spoil thawing with microwaves alone.

ideas.title: Smart Thermistor Curve Replaces Power Knob

new_nodes.label: Software power curve (thermistor-driven)
new_nodes.detail: A cheap thermistor in the food tray feeds a microcontroller that sets power automatically, replacing the 5-step mechanical duty-cycle cam.

new_nodes.label: Embedded PWM control
new_nodes.detail: Pulse-width modulation adjusts magnetron duty cycle continuously.

new_nodes.label: Adaptive defrost power
new_nodes.detail: Runs high power while food is cold and drops it near the melt point to avoid cooking the edges.

ideas.rationale: A continuously adjusting power curve thaws frozen food faster at the start and more gently near the end, which a fixed five-step knob cannot do.

ideas.title: Ultrasonic Core Agitator

new_nodes.label: Ultrasonic transducer pad
new_nodes.detail: A small piezo pad in the base that generates internal heat in frozen food, supplementing the magnetron at lower cost than a second heating source.

new_nodes.label: Piezoelectric ultrasonic heating
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency acoustic vibration warms the food's interior directly.

new_nodes.label: Interior core heating
new_nodes.detail: Heats the centre of frozen blocks where microwaves penetrate poorly.

ideas.rationale: Heating the core acoustically complements microwave penetration limits, so frozen blocks thaw through their centre much faster.

ideas.title: Thaw Window: a thermochromic door that shows the wait as progress

new_nodes.detail: Mica window with a heat-sensitive ink layer that shifts from frosted blue to clear as the food reaches thawing temperature.

new_nodes.label: Shows thaw progress by colour
new_nodes.detail: The window changes colour zone by zone, so users see the food thawing instead of guessing.

new_nodes.label: Users perceive defrost time as wasted waiting
new_nodes.detail: Waiting with no visible progress makes a 15-minute defrost feel far longer than it is.

new_nodes.detail: A near-zero-cost tag encoding food mass, frozen state and recommended defrost profile, read by the oven on placement.

ideas.title: Solid-State Thaw Amp: a continuous low-power source replaces the magnetron duty cycle

new_nodes.label: Continuous low-power thawing
new_nodes.detail: Holds a gentle, steady power level that thaws without cooking the edges, rather than cycling on and off.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the high-voltage chain with a semiconductor amplifier allows steady low power, so frozen food thaws evenly and faster than repeated on-off bursts.

new_nodes.label: Fixed graphite-loaded ceramic susceptor plate
new_nodes.detail: A stationary plate that absorbs microwaves and conducts heat into the frozen underside, replacing the glass turntable, roller ring, and motor.

new_nodes.label: Microwave-coupling ceramic susceptor (SiC/graphite)
new_nodes.detail: The ceramic converts stray microwave energy to heat, which then spreads by conduction into the frozen block.

new_nodes.label: Conducts heat into frozen underside by contact
new_nodes.detail: Provides a second heat path that works alongside dielectric heating to thaw the bottom of the food.

ideas.rationale: Conductive heat coming up through the frozen underside thaws the bottom of the block that the microwave field misses, which speeds up defrosting (M4).

ideas.title: Phase-Change Thermal Battery Defrost Tray

new_nodes.label: Sodium acetate trihydrate latent-heat tray
new_nodes.detail: A sealed tray under the food, charged during a short low-power burst, that releases stored heat during thawing.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat storage in salt hydrate phase change
new_nodes.detail: Melts at ~58 °C and stores roughly 260 kJ/kg, then releases that heat slowly and steadily as it solidifies.

new_nodes.label: Stores microwave energy as heat for later release
new_nodes.detail: Decouples energy input from thawing, so the magnetron only needs to run briefly.

ideas.rationale: Storing energy in a phase-change tray and releasing it as steady conductive heat lets frozen food defrost in a controlled way with less magnetron runtime and less radiation exposure (M4).

ideas.title: Susceptor Turntable Conduction Defrost

new_nodes.label: Silicon carbide susceptor turntable
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the glass turntable with a SiC plate that absorbs microwave energy and conducts heat into the underside of the frozen food.

new_nodes.label: Underside conductive heating
new_nodes.detail: Heats the food from below by conduction, so the bottom thaws while microwaves penetrate from above.

new_nodes.label: Microwave-to-conduction heat transfer
new_nodes.detail: Converts absorbed microwave energy in a lossy ceramic into heat that flows into a contacting solid.

new_nodes.label: Materials science of microwave-absorbing ceramics
new_nodes.detail: Dielectric loss tuning of SiC so the plate heats at a controlled rate without arcing.

ideas.rationale: Heating the frozen block from both the top (microwaves) and the bottom (conduction) shortens the time for the cold underside to reach thawing temperature, which is the slowest part of defrosting.

ideas.title: Impedance-Sensing Cavity Replaces Timer and Power Cam

new_nodes.label: Cavity electrode impedance sensor
new_nodes.detail: Pair of electrodes in the cavity walls that measure the complex permittivity of the load in real time.

new_nodes.label: Real-time load state detection
new_nodes.detail: Determines whether the food is still frozen, partially thawed, or hot, from the dielectric loss signal.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric loss tracking
new_nodes.detail: Uses the change in water's loss tangent as ice melts to track the thaw state.

new_nodes.label: Thaw runaway hot spots
new_nodes.detail: Once part of the food melts, it absorbs energy far more strongly, so it overheats while the rest stays frozen.

new_nodes.label: Closed-loop duty-cycle modulation
new_nodes.detail: Pulses the magnetron automatically to keep the thaw rate even across the load.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the user's guess at time and power with a sensor that tracks the thaw state directly prevents the cooked edges and frozen centres that make manual defrosting slow and wasteful.

ideas.title: 27 MHz RF Electrode Pair Replaces the 2.45 GHz Magnetron

new_nodes.label: 27.12 MHz RF electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Parallel-plate electrodes flanking the food, driven by a solid-state RF generator instead of a magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Deep volumetric frozen-block heating
new_nodes.detail: Penetrates much deeper into frozen food than 2.45 GHz, giving more uniform thawing through the block.

new_nodes.label: Radio-frequency dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Heats the load through dielectric loss at 27 MHz, where the wavelength is about 11 m and the field penetrates the ice.

new_nodes.label: RF power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state RF amplifier and impedance-matching network for low-frequency dielectric heating.

new_nodes.label: Ice surface reflection at 2.45 GHz
new_nodes.detail: Frozen surfaces reflect and shield 2.45 GHz energy, so the outer layer heats while the core stays frozen.

ideas.rationale: The longer RF wavelength penetrates the frozen core directly instead of relying on the outer layer to conduct heat inward, so the whole block thaws faster and more evenly.

ideas.title: Steam Condensation Defrost Replaces Dry Heating

new_nodes.label: Water-tray steam generator
new_nodes.detail: Shallow reservoir in the cavity floor that the magnetron boils to produce steam for a sealed defrost chamber.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat surface delivery
new_nodes.detail: Steam condenses on the cold food surface, releasing about 2260 kJ/kg of latent heat per kg of condensate.

new_nodes.label: Condensation phase-change heat transfer
new_nodes.detail: Uses the high heat transfer coefficient of condensing steam on a cold surface to deliver heat faster than dry convection.

new_nodes.label: Thermal fluid dynamics
new_nodes.detail: Vapour transport and condensate management inside a sealed cavity.

new_nodes.label: Dry microwave surface heating
new_nodes.detail: Direct microwave heating of frozen food is uneven and slow at the surface.

ideas.rationale: Condensing steam delivers latent heat to every cold surface at once, so the frozen food thaws faster than surface-only microwave absorption allows.

ideas.title: Ferrite Pin Array Drives Core Heating Into the Frozen Block

new_nodes.label: Ferrite-tipped heating pin array
new_nodes.detail: A grid of thin ferrite-coated stainless pins lowered from the cavity ceiling into the frozen food, heated by the microwave field.

new_nodes.label: Core heating by conduction through pins
new_nodes.detail: Each pin conducts heat into the centre of the frozen block, reaching the core that microwaves cannot penetrate.

new_nodes.label: Microwave-heated conductive probe
new_nodes.detail: A lossy-magnetic pin absorbs field energy along its length and conducts it into the surrounding solid.

new_nodes.label: Magnetic-loss materials engineering
new_nodes.detail: Ferrite composition tuned so the pin tips absorb energy at 2.45 GHz without overheating the pin shaft.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical pin insertion
new_nodes.detail: Pins descend into the food, then retract after defrosting.

new_nodes.detail: Base-product heating medium, not yet a graph node; replaced by saturated steam.

new_nodes.detail: Plate that absorbs microwaves, heats itself and conducts heat up into the food from below.

new_nodes.detail: RF impedance measurement and signal processing.

ideas.title: Weight-Dosed Energy Platform

new_nodes.detail: Base-product manual power selector; not yet a graph node; replaced.

new_nodes.detail: Base-product 700 W microwave source, not yet a graph node; now driven by the load cell.

new_nodes.label: Mass-proportional energy dosing
new_nodes.detail: Delivers the right amount of energy for the actual load, so small portions are not overcooked and large ones are not starved.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge load sensing
new_nodes.detail: Bridge-circuit measurement of mass and load changes.

new_nodes.label: Sensor engineering
new_nodes.detail: Transducer design, calibration and signal conditioning.

new_edges.to: 5-step power knob with duty-cycle cam (base product)

ideas.rationale: Dosing energy by the mass actually present means a frozen block gets the power it needs to thaw quickly without the manual guesswork of a power setting.

ideas.title: Piezo Acoustic Core-Thaw Array

new_nodes.label: Magnetron (sole heat source)
new_nodes.detail: Base-product 700 W microwave source, not yet a graph node; reduced to a low-power surface-finish role.

new_nodes.label: Piezo transducer array
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost piezoelectric transducers in the cavity walls that send ultrasound through the frozen core.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric acoustic core heating
new_nodes.detail: Ultrasonic energy heats the interior of the ice, where microwaves struggle to reach.

new_nodes.label: Ultrasonic acoustic heating

new_nodes.detail: Ultrasound propagation, coupling and attenuation in solids and ice.

ideas.title: Steam-Sensed Stop

new_nodes.detail: A low-cost sensor in the vent that detects the drop in steam output when food is done.

new_nodes.detail: Extra minutes of magnetron run time waste energy and dry out food.

ideas.title: Thermal Battery Cabinet

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat store
new_nodes.detail: A sealed salt-hydrate block that is heated off-peak and releases stored heat to a resistive element during cooking.

new_nodes.label: Heat delivery on demand
new_nodes.detail: Supplies the cooking energy without drawing 700 W from the mains at peak times.

new_nodes.detail: Phase-change materials that store heat in melting and release it on solidifying.

ideas.title: Turntable Scale

new_nodes.detail: The glass plate sits on a load cell, so it weighs the food and replaces the power dial.

new_nodes.label: Automatic power matching
new_nodes.detail: Sets the power level and duration from the mass of the food, avoiding full-power cooking of small portions.

new_nodes.detail: A single 700 W setting wastes energy when reheating a single cup.

ideas.title: Self-Opening Standby-Free Door

new_nodes.detail: A mechanical latch that needs no power to hold the door shut and releases only when the cook cycle ends.

new_nodes.label: Standby power draw
new_nodes.detail: Electronic controls and displays that stay powered while the oven is idle waste electricity around the clock.

ideas.title: Capacitive RF Defrost Cradle

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz RF dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Radio-frequency electric field heats the food's interior volume evenly, without microwave hot spots.

new_nodes.label: Parallel capacitor plates
new_nodes.detail: Two flat electrodes replace the magnetron-and-cavity heating path and the glass turntable.

new_nodes.label: Uniform volumetric thawing
new_nodes.detail: Thaws frozen blocks from the inside out, so the outer edges do not cook while the centre is still frozen.

ideas.rationale: Substituting the magnetron and turntable with RF capacitive plates heats frozen food throughout its volume, which speeds thawing and avoids the edge-cooking that slows it down.

ideas.title: Self-Weighing Tray Replaces the Clockwork Timer

new_nodes.label: Bioimpedance sensing
new_nodes.detail: Measures how much a food's electrical impedance changes as it thaws, which indicates the thaw state.

new_nodes.label: Conductive sensing tray
new_nodes.detail: A tray with embedded electrodes that replaces the mechanical timer knob and its bell.

new_nodes.label: Auto-stop at thaw point
new_nodes.detail: Ends the defrost cycle when the food reaches the target thaw state, with no user timing.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the guessed clockwork timer with impedance sensing stops each defrost at the right moment, which removes both the overheating and the underthawing that waste time.

ideas.title: Salt-Brine Thermal Bath Replaces the Glass Turntable

new_nodes.label: Sealed brine bath
new_nodes.detail: A shallow tray of microwave-absorbing saline solution that the food sits in or against.

new_nodes.label: Conductive coupling medium
new_nodes.detail: The saline solution absorbs microwave energy and transfers heat to the frozen surface by conduction.

new_nodes.label: Fast surface-to-core transfer
new_nodes.detail: Brings heat into the food quickly and evenly, including its frozen centre.

ideas.rationale: Swapping the turntable for a saline bath that absorbs microwaves and conducts heat into the food delivers heat to the frozen core faster than radiation alone.

ideas.title: Graphene Susceptor Sleeve Replaces the 700 W Magnetron

new_nodes.label: Graphene susceptor sleeve
new_nodes.detail: A disposable sleeve that absorbs microwaves and heats to over 200 °C, then conducts that heat into the food.

new_nodes.label: Microwave-to-conduction heat conversion
new_nodes.detail: Converts microwave energy into surface heat that conducts into frozen food.

new_nodes.label: Low-power sustained thaw
new_nodes.detail: Thaws frozen food with a modest, steady heat source instead of a 700 W burst.

ideas.rationale: A disposable graphene sleeve acts as a conduction heater, so a cheap, low-power source can defrost frozen food steadily without the cooking-edge problem of high-power bursts.

ideas.title: Ultrasonic Lattice Thawing Replaces the Interior Lamp and Door Window

new_nodes.label: Ultrasonic cavitation heating
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency sound waves agitate the water in frozen food and heat it internally.

new_nodes.label: Ultrasonic transducer array
new_nodes.detail: Transducers mounted on the cavity walls, which replace the interior lamp as the thaw-state indicator.

new_nodes.label: Silent internal thaw indication
new_nodes.detail: Shows thaw progress through a status colour or a sound tone instead of the lamp.

ideas.rationale: Using ultrasonic cavitation both heats the frozen food from inside and signals thaw progress, which lets one cheap component replace the lamp and speeds up thawing.

ideas.title: Reflected-Power Doneness Sensing

new_nodes.label: Waveguide directional coupler
new_nodes.detail: Sampling coupler on the magnetron output waveguide that measures reflected (back) power continuously.

new_nodes.label: Load-impedance doneness estimation
new_nodes.detail: Firmware infers moisture loss and food state from the drift of reflected power, since water content changes the cavity load.

new_nodes.label: Detect food state from load
new_nodes.detail: Determines doneness from the food's electrical load rather than from elapsed time.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the guessed clockwork timer with a signal taken from the food's own load gives the user a true done-signal that serves M8 at near-zero added hardware cost.

ideas.title: Door Window Replaced by Thermochromic Doneness Strip

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic film strip
new_nodes.detail: Heat-sensitive film bonded to the outer door glass that changes colour as its temperature rises from steam and conduction.

new_nodes.label: Passive thermochromic indication
new_nodes.detail: Colour change driven by the thermal state of the door and cavity, requiring no power.

new_nodes.label: Show cavity heat state without light
new_nodes.detail: Reveals that food is hot enough to be near done, with no interior illumination.

new_nodes.detail: Detects the sound of food reaching boiling or popping, and signals the user with a tone or light.

ideas.rationale: Listening to the food itself replaces a fixed timer bell with an event-driven alert, which gives M8 the direct cue of boiling or popping.

new_nodes.label: Emit aroma-based done cue
new_nodes.detail: Releases a small scented or tactile cue, such as a heated scent cartridge, when the volatile profile indicates the food is ready.

ideas.rationale: Sensing the food's own volatiles and answering with a scent cue gives M8 an intuitive, sensory signal that works even when the user cannot see or hear the appliance.

new_nodes.detail: Small fragrance cartridge that replaces the bell and releases a scent that strengthens as the cycle nears its end.

new_nodes.label: Micro-atomised fragrance release
new_nodes.detail: Piezo atomiser that vaporises a measured dose of aroma on a timed ramp.

new_nodes.label: Olfactory engineering
new_nodes.detail: Design of scent release and perception for user cues.

new_nodes.label: Smell-ramp progress cue
new_nodes.detail: Conveys how close the food is to done through rising aroma intensity.

ideas.rationale: Smell is the fastest route to a sense of 'nearly ready', so the user gets a continuous readiness signal from the nose instead of a single sudden bell.

ideas.title: Steam Sommelier Dial

new_nodes.label: Ceramic humidity sensor dial
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost ceramic humidity sensor that replaces the cam timer and reads moisture leaving the food.

new_nodes.label: Resistive ceramic humidity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide ceramic whose resistance changes with humidity, read by simple circuitry.

new_nodes.label: Infers doneness from moisture release
new_nodes.detail: Estimates readiness from steam output rather than elapsed minutes.

ideas.rationale: Letting the food report its own steam gives the user true state feedback instead of a guessed countdown, so they no longer need to check the food to know it is ready.

ideas.title: Turntable Mood Ring

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic turntable coating
new_nodes.detail: Colour-shifting film on the glass turntable that replaces the lamp and shows heat distribution.

new_nodes.label: Leuco-dye thermochromic pigment
new_nodes.detail: Pigment that changes colour at set temperatures, with no electricity or filament.

new_nodes.label: Shows heat state as colour
new_nodes.detail: Displays how hot the food zone is by the turntable's colour.

ideas.rationale: Colour is an instant, glanceable readiness signal that works even with the door closed, and the pigment costs less than a lamp that burns out.

new_nodes.detail: Small transducer bonded to the cavity wall that picks up the sounds of cooking.

new_nodes.detail: Analyses crackle, pop and bubble sounds to estimate doneness.

new_nodes.detail: Turns sizzle and pop patterns into a readiness signal.

new_edges.from: Reads cooking sounds as doneness cues

ideas.rationale: Sound tells the user what is happening inside without opening the door, so they can hear readiness rather than peer through a window for it.

ideas.title: Door Invitation

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded door ajar actuator
new_nodes.detail: Cam-driven spring that nudges the door open a few millimetres when cooking ends, replacing the bell.

new_nodes.label: Spring latch with cam release
new_nodes.detail: Simple spring-and-cam mechanism reusing the existing door latch geometry.

new_nodes.label: Signals end by opening the door
new_nodes.detail: Physically invites the user back by releasing steam and a small visible gap.

new_edges.from: Signals end by opening the door

ideas.rationale: A door that visibly opens itself at the end of cooking is an unmissable readiness cue that uses the appliance's own body instead of an added sound.

ideas.title: Cook-cam, not cook-lamp

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp (20-25 W)
new_nodes.detail: Original component: lit for the whole cook cycle, so it is removed.

new_nodes.label: Sub-watt door-seal camera
new_nodes.detail: A tiny CMOS sensor behind the door glass streams live video to the user's phone.

new_nodes.label: Low-power CMOS imaging
new_nodes.detail: Consumer image sensors that draw under 1 W and need no interior illumination.

new_nodes.label: Visual check of food
new_nodes.detail: User confirms doneness without opening the door, which releases trapped heat.

new_nodes.label: Continuous lamp load
new_nodes.detail: A 25 W lamp burns energy for the entire cook time just to be looked at.

ideas.rationale: Replacing a 25 W bulb with a sub-watt camera cuts lighting energy by over 95% and stops door-opening heat loss, while the live feed gives a watch-the-food entertainment hook that makes the check feel like a treat.

ideas.title: Done when it's done

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob (0-30 min)
new_nodes.detail: Original component: a fixed timer that ignores what the food is actually doing.

new_nodes.label: Volatile-compound gas sensor
new_nodes.detail: A low-cost metal-oxide sensor detects steam and aroma peaks that signal doneness.

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide gas sensing
new_nodes.detail: Cheap, mature sensing that reads food emissions in the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Stop heating at doneness
new_nodes.detail: Power cuts off when the food reaches the target state, not when a guessed clock runs out.

new_nodes.label: Overcooking waste
new_nodes.detail: Fixed timers keep the magnetron running after food is ready, wasting energy and drying food.

ideas.rationale: Swapping a guessing timer for a sensor that cuts power the moment food is ready removes the energy spent on overcooking, which is the largest avoidable waste in a typical reheat.

ideas.title: The fan that stirs the food

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable and drive motor
new_nodes.detail: Original component: a motor-driven plate that spins food to even out hot spots.

new_nodes.label: Airflow-driven vane stirrer
new_nodes.detail: A passive metal vane sits in the cavity and is spun by the magnetron's existing cooling-fan exhaust.

new_nodes.label: Airflow-driven mode stirring
new_nodes.detail: Uses air already moving through the unit to redistribute microwave energy.

new_nodes.label: Even heating across food
new_nodes.detail: Microwave energy is spread across the food so cold spots are avoided.

new_nodes.label: Dedicated motor load
new_nodes.detail: A separate turntable motor draws power and adds parts that can fail.

ideas.rationale: Using the cooling fan's existing airflow to turn a stirrer removes the turntable motor's separate power draw entirely, so even heating costs no extra energy.

ideas.title: A nest, not a cave

new_nodes.label: 20 L heated cavity
new_nodes.detail: Original component: the full-size cavity heats large volumes of empty air and walls.

new_nodes.label: Removable insulated ceramic nest
new_nodes.detail: A bowl-sized liner that shrinks the heated volume to the portion and reflects heat back to the food.

new_nodes.label: Insulating ceramic composites
new_nodes.detail: Low-mass, microwave-transparent ceramics that hold heat in the food zone.

new_nodes.label: Contain food efficiently
new_nodes.detail: Holds the food in a small, well-insulated zone so less energy is lost to empty space.

new_nodes.label: Empty-volume heat loss
new_nodes.detail: Most energy in a large cavity heats air and walls rather than food.

ideas.rationale: Shrinking the heated volume to the size of the portion means far less energy goes into empty air and cavity walls, and the small, cosy 'nest' framing makes cooking for one feel personal rather than wasteful.

ideas.title: Fast-feeling slow power

new_nodes.label: 5-step power knob (duty-cycle cam)
new_nodes.detail: Original component: user picks a power level, and high settings are often chosen for speed.

new_nodes.label: Intent selector with preset profiles
new_nodes.detail: User picks what they are doing (reheat, cook, defrost) and the unit runs an efficient duty-cycle curve.

new_nodes.label: Pre-programmed duty-cycle curves
new_nodes.detail: Matched heating profiles that avoid peak-power overshoot for each food type.

new_nodes.label: Match heat to food
new_nodes.detail: Energy delivery is tuned to the food's needs so little is wasted on overshoot.

new_nodes.label: Perceived cooking speed
new_nodes.detail: A progress display that moves quickly early on makes gentle, efficient heating feel fast.

new_nodes.label: Full-power habit
new_nodes.detail: Users crank the knob to maximum to feel the food is cooking quickly, wasting energy.

ideas.rationale: Preset efficient profiles paired with a progress display that feels fast remove the urge to run at full power, so the unit uses gentler, less wasteful heating without the user perceiving a slowdown.
