ideas.title: Olfactory Doneness Sniffer

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide VOC gas sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost semiconductor sensor that detects the rise and shift of food volatiles as heating progresses.

new_nodes.label: Analytical chemistry
new_nodes.detail: Study of volatile organic compounds released during cooking.

new_nodes.label: Aroma sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Small sensor cluster in the vent that tracks the aroma curve of the food.

new_nodes.label: Detect cooking progress from smell
new_nodes.detail: Estimates doneness from the aroma profile instead of elapsed time.

new_nodes.label: Scent-status display
new_nodes.detail: Small LED ring whose colour follows the aroma-derived doneness stage.

ideas.rationale: The user learns when food is ready from the aroma the food itself produces, so the feedback tracks real doneness rather than a guessed time.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Turntable Glow

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic ink coating
new_nodes.detail: Food-safe pigment layer that changes colour at set temperature thresholds.

new_nodes.label: Materials chemistry
new_nodes.detail: Formulation of temperature-responsive pigments.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic turntable
new_nodes.detail: Glass turntable with a printed layer that shifts colour as the plate heats.

new_nodes.label: Show heat state of the food zone
new_nodes.detail: Makes the temperature of the cooking zone visible at a glance.

new_edges.to: Show heat state of the food zone

new_edges.from: Show heat state of the food zone

ideas.rationale: Heat state is shown directly on the surface the food sits on, so the user sees readiness without needing a light inside the cavity.

ideas.title: Acoustic Crackle Listener

new_nodes.label: MEMS acoustic analysis
new_nodes.detail: Micro-microphone with on-chip spectral analysis of popping, bubbling, and sizzling.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic signal processing
new_nodes.detail: Classification of food sounds into cooking stages.

new_nodes.label: Cavity microphone
new_nodes.detail: Small mic mounted in the cavity wall that listens to the food.

new_nodes.label: Infer doneness from food sounds
new_nodes.detail: Detects when popping or bubbling slows, which signals the food is ready.

new_nodes.label: Sound-to-haptic handle pulse
new_nodes.detail: Pulse in the door handle that signals readiness without noise.

ideas.rationale: Food sounds change as food finishes, so listening to the food gives readiness feedback that the user can feel through the handle, not only hear.

ideas.title: Doneness Dial Replaces Power Steps

new_nodes.label: Dielectric permittivity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Measures how the food's dielectric properties change as it heats, using the magnetron's own field.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric spectroscopy
new_nodes.detail: Relationship between food moisture, temperature, and dielectric response.

new_nodes.label: Doneness dial
new_nodes.detail: Knob that sets a target doneness percentage instead of a power level.

new_nodes.label: Auto-adjust power to doneness target
new_nodes.detail: Modulates magnetron duty cycle and stops when the target is reached.

new_nodes.label: Sensor noise from water content variation
new_nodes.detail: Moisture differences between foods can distort the dielectric signal.

new_edges.from: Sensor noise from water content variation

ideas.rationale: The user sets the outcome they want and the machine reports and enforces progress toward it, removing guesswork about power and time.

ideas.title: Shared Doneness Companion

new_nodes.label: Low-power Bluetooth LE
new_nodes.detail: Short-range wireless link to a phone or smart watch.

new_nodes.label: Ubiquitous computing
new_nodes.detail: Ambient, connected devices that report status to people away from the appliance.

new_nodes.label: Cloud-linked status beacon
new_nodes.detail: Radio module that streams live cooking state to the user's phone.

new_nodes.label: Remote readiness alerts
new_nodes.detail: Notifies the user anywhere in the home, or on a shared kitchen display, when food is ready.

new_nodes.label: Dependence on network connectivity
new_nodes.detail: Alerts fail if the phone or network is unavailable.

ideas.rationale: Readiness reaches the person wherever they are, so they do not have to stand at the microwave watching the clock or waiting for the bell.

ideas.title: Doneness by Echo: Reflected-RF Sensing Replaces the Lamp and the Timer

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power doneness sensor
new_nodes.detail: Reads the magnetron's own reflected RF signal to detect moisture loss and stop cooking when food is ready, with no lamp or fixed timer.

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power dielectric monitoring
new_nodes.detail: Tracks changes in cavity impedance as water content falls during heating, using the existing 2.45 GHz field as the sensor.

new_nodes.label: Stops heating at the energy-optimal moment
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle when the dielectric load changes, so no energy is spent past doneness and the user never has to peek.

new_edges.to: Stops heating at the energy-optimal moment

new_edges.from: Stops heating at the energy-optimal moment

ideas.rationale: Removing the 20-25 W lamp and guessing timers, and stopping at true doneness, cuts wasted energy while people feel more in control because the oven watches the food for them.

ideas.title: Self-Turning Tray: Steam-Driven Rotation Replaces the Turntable Motor

new_nodes.label: Steam-vane turntable drive
new_nodes.detail: Small vanes on the underside of the glass tray are spun by the rising steam and convection currents from the food.

new_nodes.label: Passive convective rotation
new_nodes.detail: Uses the heat the food already releases to turn the tray, so no mains-powered motor or gearbox is needed.

new_nodes.label: Rotates food with zero electrical input
new_nodes.detail: Keeps the even-heating rotation going using energy that would otherwise leave the oven as waste steam.

new_edges.to: Rotates food with zero electrical input

new_edges.from: Rotates food with zero electrical input
Rotates food with zero electrical input

ideas.rationale: Powering the turntable from the food's own steam turns a wasted byproduct into motion, which removes a motor's continuous draw while keeping the even heating that users value.

ideas.title: Shrink-Wrapped Cavity: A Dielectric Insert Fills the Empty Air

new_nodes.label: Removable ceramic fill insert
new_nodes.detail: A fitted ceramic or mica block that occupies most of the 20 L cavity, leaving only a food-sized pocket to heat.

new_nodes.label: Low-loss ceramic dielectric filler
new_nodes.detail: Microwave-transparent ceramic that absorbs little RF, so the field goes into food rather than into empty air.

new_nodes.label: Reduces heated air volume
new_nodes.detail: Cuts the amount of cavity space the magnetron must energise for each cooking cycle.

ideas.rationale: Filling the empty air with a cheap ceramic block means the magnetron energises only the food, which is the most direct cut to wasted energy per meal.

ideas.title: Solid-State Right-Sizing: A GaN Amplifier Replaces the Fixed 700 W Magnetron

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Semiconductor RF source that outputs only the power a load needs and has no filament or cathode to wear out.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride RF power amplification
new_nodes.detail: Switched high-frequency RF transistors that run efficiently across a range of output levels.

new_nodes.label: Matches output power to the load
new_nodes.detail: Adjusts RF power to the food's absorption in real time, so the oven never pushes 700 W into a cup of tea.

new_edges.to: Matches output power to the load

new_edges.from: Matches output power to the load
Matches output power to the load

ideas.rationale: Matching RF output to the load stops the oven from overdriving small portions, which cuts energy use while also removing the magnetron's wear-out limit.

ideas.title: Hot Hands Off: Ferrite-Core Transformer Swapped for a Piezo Step-Up

new_nodes.label: Piezoelectric high-voltage step-up element
new_nodes.detail: A ceramic resonant element that steps mains power up to the magnetron's voltage with no iron core, copper winding or bulky rectifier stack.

new_nodes.label: Piezoelectric resonant transformation
new_nodes.detail: Converts electrical energy into mechanical resonance and back again, which yields high voltage with low standby loss.

new_nodes.label: Delivers high voltage with minimal standby loss
new_nodes.detail: Provides the magnetron's supply while drawing almost nothing when the oven is idle, and the element holds no lethal stored charge once power is cut.

new_edges.to: Delivers high voltage with minimal standby loss

new_edges.from: Delivers high voltage with minimal standby loss
Delivers high voltage with minimal standby loss

ideas.rationale: Replacing the heavy iron transformer and capacitor stack with a resonant ceramic element removes most of the conversion and standby losses, so the oven wastes less energy before any food is touched.

ideas.title: Solid-state amplifier with continuous thaw power

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state 2.45 GHz RF amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Transistor amplifier with continuously variable output, replacing the magnetron and its high-voltage chain.

new_nodes.label: GaN RF power amplifier module
new_nodes.detail: Low-voltage transistor stage fed from a 48 V SMPS, with reflected-power feedback.

new_nodes.label: Continuously variable RF output for gentle thaw
new_nodes.detail: Delivers any wattage without on/off cycling, so thawing runs at a steady low power.

new_edges.to: Continuously variable RF output for gentle thaw

new_edges.from: Continuously variable RF output for gentle thaw

ideas.rationale: Steady low-wattage output thaws frozen food evenly without the on/off cycling that leaves some areas soft while others are still frozen.

ideas.title: 27 MHz RF electrodes thaw whole blocks at once

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz capacitive RF heating
new_nodes.detail: Electrode-driven RF field whose ~11 m wavelength gives no standing-wave hot spots across the load.

new_nodes.label: Parallel-plate RF electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Two conductive plates above and below the food replace the waveguide and magnetron antenna.

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz solid-state RF generator
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost transistor generator that drives the electrode pair.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric thawing of frozen blocks
new_nodes.detail: Heats the full thickness of a frozen block together, not from the outside inward.

ideas.rationale: Heating the full thickness of a frozen block at once removes the slow outside-in thaw that makes people wait, so the defrost finishes sooner.

ideas.title: Phased-array virtual turntable

new_nodes.label: Phased-array antenna steering
new_nodes.detail: Multiple RF feeds with independently varied phase steer the standing-wave pattern electronically.

new_nodes.label: Four-feed phased antenna array
new_nodes.detail: Four small antennas on the cavity walls, each driven at a controlled phase.

new_nodes.label: Electronic sweeping of hot spots
new_nodes.detail: Moves the field pattern many times a second so the load is covered without any physical rotation.

ideas.rationale: Sweeping the hot spots across the whole load removes the cold pockets that keep a frozen centre frozen, so the food thaws evenly in one pass.

ideas.title: Load-cell turntable that weighs food and sets the thaw

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge load cell
new_nodes.detail: Bridge-type strain gauges read mass to a few grams, as in kitchen scales.

new_nodes.label: Three-point load-cell turntable support
new_nodes.detail: Strain-gauge pads replace the roller ring as the tray bearing and report the load's mass.

new_nodes.label: Automatic mass-based thaw programming
new_nodes.detail: Sets power and time from weight so the user never turns a knob.

ideas.rationale: Matching power and time to the actual weight of the frozen load removes the guesswork that makes parents under- or over-thaw, so the defrost is right first time.

ideas.title: Thaw-progress bar replaces the countdown

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power thaw sensing
new_nodes.detail: Reads the shift in reflected RF as ice turns to water and converts it into a progress signal.

new_nodes.label: Door thaw-progress bar
new_nodes.detail: A melting ice-cube bar on the door fills as the load thaws, replacing the countdown timer and bell.

new_nodes.label: Visible thaw progress
new_nodes.detail: Shows the defrost advancing in real time, so the wait feels active rather than dead time.

ideas.rationale: A visibly advancing thaw makes the wait feel shorter and removes the anxiety that drives parents to over-thaw, so the frozen food is ready sooner in practice.

new_nodes.label: Resistive humidity sensing in the vent path
new_nodes.detail: A hygroscopic polymer element whose resistance changes with the water vapour food releases; the rise and fall of the signal marks steaming-to-drying.

new_nodes.label: Humidity sensor and comparator board
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the motor-driven cam timer; a comparator on the sensor signal ends the cycle when the vapour curve peaks and falls.

new_nodes.label: Stops cooking at food-determined doneness
new_nodes.detail: Closed-loop endpoint driven by the food's own vapour output instead of elapsed time.

new_nodes.detail: A camera mounted outside the cavity sees through the sub-wavelength mesh holes, which still block microwaves.

new_nodes.label: Door-mounted CMOS camera with shielded RF filter
new_nodes.detail: Small sensor with an IR-cut filter and RF-shielded enclosure that streams live images of the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Estimates browning and doneness from the live image
new_nodes.detail: On-device or app-based image classifier reports a readiness estimate to the user.

new_nodes.detail: A ring of LEDs around the door frame that shifts colour from cold blue to ready green.

new_nodes.label: IR thermopile spot sensor aimed at the food
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost non-contact sensor reads the surface temperature of the food and feeds the colour driver.

new_nodes.detail: Silent, ambient readiness feedback that works without a sound alert.

ideas.title: Load-Cell Turntable Replaces the Power Knob

new_nodes.label: Weighing turntable
new_nodes.detail: The glass turntable is replaced by a thin load-cell platter that measures the mass and temperature of the frozen load and sets the duty cycle automatically.

new_nodes.label: Auto-modulate defrost intensity
new_nodes.detail: Sets power per cycle from measured load, replacing the user-selected 5-step cam.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost strain gauges and a thermistor array, already common in kitchen scales.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the guessed power setting with a measured one removes the user's uncertainty about how long defrosting will take and avoids cooking the edges while the centre stays frozen.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Ice Window Replaces the Bell Timer

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door window
new_nodes.detail: A heat-sensitive film on the door glass turns from frosted white to clear when the food's centre reaches thawing temperature.

new_nodes.label: Signal defrost completion visually
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the clockwork timer and end-of-time bell as the signal that the food is ready.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic pigment
new_nodes.detail: Leuco-dye films, cheap and printable, used in mugs and baby-bottle indicators.

ideas.rationale: A visible clearing window tells the user the food is ready at a glance, so they no longer have to guess a time or stand by the bell, which is the real need behind defrosting quickly.

ideas.title: Infrared Frost Map Replaces the Interior Lamp

new_nodes.label: Low-res thermal sensor
new_nodes.detail: A cheap infrared sensor array behind the door mapping cold spots on the food in colour, replacing the 20-25 W incandescent lamp.

new_nodes.label: Show uneven thawing
new_nodes.detail: Reveals which parts are still frozen so the user can rearrange the load and avoid overcooked edges.

new_nodes.label: Thermopile sensing
new_nodes.detail: Thermopile arrays are mass-produced and inexpensive, used in smart thermostats and phones.

ideas.rationale: The thermal view lets the user see where the ice is still hard, so they can reposition food and finish sooner, and it uses less power than a lamp.

ideas.title: Spiked Ice-Pin Platter Replaces the Glass Turntable

new_nodes.label: Conductive ice-pin platter
new_nodes.detail: The glass turntable is replaced by a rotating platter studded with short stainless pins that pierce the frozen block and carry energy into its centre.

new_nodes.label: Increase thaw surface area
new_nodes.detail: Pins expose the frozen interior to field energy, so the block thaws from the inside as well as the outside.

new_nodes.label: Stainless micro-pin machining
new_nodes.detail: Pins are cheap to stamp and sheath in food-safe coating.

ideas.rationale: Pinning the ice speeds thawing by reaching the frozen core instead of waiting for heat to travel inward, directly shortening the time to defrost.

ideas.title: Door-Close Start Replaces the Push-Release Button

new_nodes.label: Presence-sensing hinge
new_nodes.detail: A hinge with a magnetic reed sensor starts defrost automatically when the door closes on a frozen load, replacing the push-release button.

new_nodes.label: Start defrost with no setup
new_nodes.detail: Removes the steps of selecting the mode and time, so defrosting begins the moment the food goes in.

new_nodes.label: Reed-switch sensing
new_nodes.detail: Cheap magnetic reed switches used in fridge doors and window alarms.

ideas.rationale: Making defrosting start the moment the door shuts removes setup friction, so the user feels the wait has already begun and the speed of the process matters less.

new_nodes.label: GaN HEMT 2.45 GHz RF amplifier array
new_nodes.detail: Multi-die gallium-nitride power amplifier driven from about 48 V DC, replacing the magnetron, HV capacitor and diode.

new_nodes.label: 48 V DC switch-mode supply
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency SMPS replacing the 50 Hz iron-core HV transformer, with no kV stage.

new_nodes.label: Generates 2.45 GHz RF at high DC-to-RF efficiency
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state conversion targeting roughly 65% or better DC-to-RF efficiency, versus about 50-60% wall-to-RF for the magnetron chain.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride HEMT RF power semiconductor
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap transistors operating at 2.45 GHz from a low-voltage, high-current supply.

new_nodes.label: Wide-bandgap semiconductor device physics
new_nodes.detail: Physics of GaN heterostructures for high-power RF switching and amplification.

ideas.title: Dielectric Endpoint Sensor Replaces Clockwork Timer
anchors: base_product: mechanical clockwork timer knob (0-30 min, bell)

new_nodes.label: Dielectric endpoint sensor
new_nodes.detail: Electrode pair in the cavity floor measures load impedance; the sharp rise in dielectric loss at the ice-to-water transition signals that defrost is complete.

new_nodes.label: Detect thaw endpoint automatically
new_nodes.detail: Stops heating when the food reaches target thaw state, so the user no longer estimates minutes from the package weight.

new_nodes.label: Impedance-based load sensing
new_nodes.detail: Uses the change in complex permittivity of food as it thaws to estimate the state of the load.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric heating and RF measurement
new_nodes.detail: Applies electromagnetic dielectric theory to measure load state during heating.

new_edges.to: base_product: mechanical clockwork timer knob (0-30 min, bell)

ideas.rationale: Automatic thaw-endpoint detection stops over-cooking the edges while the centre stays frozen, which speeds up a complete, even defrost.

ideas.title: Thermopile Array Replaces the Incandescent Lamp

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermopile array
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost 8x8 passive IR sensor mounted in the roof of the cavity maps surface temperature of the load every few seconds.

new_nodes.label: Map cold spots in the load
new_nodes.detail: Identifies frozen regions that remain below 0 °C so the controller can direct more energy there.

new_nodes.label: Thermal imaging with feedback control
new_nodes.detail: Closed-loop control that uses a temperature map to modulate heating.

new_nodes.label: Infrared sensing

new_nodes.detail: Thin paper-and-carbon wrap that absorbs microwaves and conducts gentle heat from its outer surface into the frozen block.

new_nodes.label: Microwave susceptor packaging
new_nodes.detail: Lossy conductive film that heats by absorbing RF and transferring heat by conduction, not by dielectric heating of ice.

new_nodes.label: Conducts heat into frozen blocks from the outside
new_nodes.detail: Brings the ice-to-water transition forward at the surface, so the core thaws without deep superheated hot spots.

new_edges.to: Conducts heat into frozen blocks from the outside

new_edges.from: Conducts heat into frozen blocks from the outside

ideas.rationale: Ice is a poor absorber of microwaves, so a cheap sleeve that absorbs the field and conducts heat into the block defrosts frozen food faster and more evenly than the cavity can alone.

new_nodes.label: Turntable load cell with infrared surface probe
new_nodes.detail: Strain-gauge weighing plate and IR sensor under the glass tray that read the mass and surface temperature of the food.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge weighing and IR thermometry
new_nodes.detail: Cheap load cell and thermopile that sense mass and surface temperature without any user input.

new_nodes.label: Sets thaw end-point from food mass and temperature
new_nodes.detail: Calculates the thaw time and power profile automatically, so the user just places the food and presses start.

new_nodes.detail: Metal blade that disturbs standing waves, spreading RF energy across the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Spreads RF energy evenly over a stationary tray

ideas.title: Steam-Plateau Doneness Dial

new_nodes.label: Humidity-sensing doneness dial
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the timer knob with a dial whose needle is driven by a low-cost metal-oxide humidity sensor reading exhaust steam.

new_nodes.label: Infers food readiness from steam plateau
new_nodes.detail: Detects when the steam curve flattens and signals that the food is done without a clock.

ideas.title: Ears Instead of Eyes

new_nodes.detail: A tiny MEMS microphone in the cavity wall listens to sizzling and popping and classifies the sound pattern.

new_nodes.label: MEMS microphone with on-board audio classifier
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost chip that runs a small pattern-matching model on cooking sounds.

new_nodes.label: Conveys cavity state through sound

new_edges.from: MEMS microphone with on-board audio classifier

new_nodes.detail: The glass turntable is coated with a thermochromic film that shifts from clear to amber when the food beneath reaches serving temperature.

ideas.title: Popcorn-Ear Acoustic Stop

new_nodes.label: Acoustic food listener
new_nodes.detail: A cheap piezo microphone picks up the sizzle, pop and bubble rate of the food and reports when the sound fades to the done signature.

new_nodes.label: Sound-based completion detection

new_nodes.label: Acoustic signal classification
new_nodes.detail: Simple amplitude and frequency thresholding on a microphone signal.

ideas.rationale: Listening to the food replaces the guessing game of the timer knob, so the user is told when the food is ready instead of having to predict it.

new_nodes.label: Passive thermal conduction
new_nodes.detail: Heat flows through a metal bridge from the cavity with no electronics.

new_nodes.label: Ceramic frit printing on glass

ideas.title: Light-Pipe Window

new_nodes.label: Passive optical transmission

new_nodes.label: Stop at done

new_nodes.label: Gas-sensing electronics

ideas.rationale: Switching off at the actual end point avoids the wasted energy of overcooking and of guessed minute settings, which is the main source of excess consumption.

ideas.title: Convection Carousel

new_nodes.detail: Replaces the motorised glass turntable drive with a plate that is rotated by the rising hot air inside the cavity, using vanes.

new_nodes.label: Even heating by rotation

new_nodes.label: Thermal fluid dynamics

new_nodes.label: Behavioural nudging

new_nodes.label: Self-regulates heat input by local temperature

new_nodes.label: Energy-capped cooking
new_nodes.detail: Limits how much energy each cook consumes and signals when that limit is reached.

ideas.rationale: Framing the cook as an energy budget instead of a duration makes waste visible and changes behaviour, so people choose smaller, shorter cooks without being told to.

ideas.title: Heat Bank: Store Burst Energy and Release It Slowly
anchors: Gentle heat delivery at low power

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat bank tray
new_nodes.detail: A tray of phase-change salt that absorbs heat during full-power bursts and releases it steadily to the food afterwards.

new_nodes.label: Latent heat storage
new_nodes.detail: Materials that store large amounts of heat in a phase change at a near-constant temperature.

new_nodes.label: Thermodynamics
new_nodes.detail: Study of heat transfer and energy flow.

new_nodes.label: Gentle heat delivery at low power
new_nodes.detail: Provides low, even heat for delicate foods without cycling the magnetron on and off.

new_edges.to: Gentle heat delivery at low power

new_edges.from: Gentle heat delivery at low power

ideas.rationale: Storing energy in a phase-change tray lets the magnetron run in short full-power bursts and lets the food absorb the stored heat, which avoids wasted heat from repeated cycling.

ideas.title: Steam Seal: Door That Tightens Under Its Own Heat

new_nodes.label: Steam-pressure labyrinth seal
new_nodes.detail: A door gasket that tightens as steam pressure builds inside, and a pull-to-open latch replaces the push button.

new_nodes.label: Pressure-activated sealing
new_nodes.detail: Seals that close tighter as internal pressure rises, so they seal better the hotter the cavity gets.

new_nodes.label: Materials science
new_nodes.detail: Study of material properties and their use in engineered components.

new_nodes.label: Heat and steam retention
new_nodes.detail: Keeps heat and moisture inside the cavity so less energy is lost during cooking.

new_nodes.label: Heat leaks through door gap
new_nodes.detail: Heat and steam escape around the door, so the magnetron must work harder to reach the target temperature.

ideas.rationale: A seal that gets tighter as the cavity heats up keeps energy inside exactly when it matters most, so less power is needed to hold the target temperature.

ideas.title: Glow-in-the-dark cavity replaces the lamp

new_nodes.label: Persistent photoluminescence (strontium aluminate phosphor)
new_nodes.detail: Phosphor pigment charges from ambient kitchen light and emits visible glow for up to an hour with zero electrical draw.

new_nodes.label: Photoluminescent cavity-wall coating
new_nodes.detail: Phosphor-loaded enamel on the cavity ceiling replaces the 20-25 W incandescent lamp and is seen through the door screen.

new_nodes.label: Interior visibility without power
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user check food through the door at zero running cost.

ideas.rationale: Powering visibility from ambient light removes the lamp's 20-25 W draw from every cook while keeping the reassurance of seeing inside.

ideas.title: Magnetron senses doneness itself

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power and anode-current sensing
new_nodes.detail: The magnetron's own load signature changes as food absorbs energy, so it can signal when the food is hot.

new_nodes.label: Software-free doneness detector
new_nodes.detail: A comparator on the existing HV feed replaces the clockwork timer and bell.

new_nodes.label: Stops heating at doneness, not at a guessed time
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cook when the food reaches target heat, removing overshoot.

new_edges.to: Stops heating at doneness, not at a guessed time

new_edges.from: Stops heating at doneness, not at a guessed time

ideas.rationale: Stopping the moment food is done eliminates the wasted energy that a guessed timer always spends on overcooking.

ideas.title: Steam-driven turntable

new_nodes.label: Steam-driven convective rotation
new_nodes.detail: Rising steam and hot air from the food push a bladed vane mounted beneath the tray.

new_nodes.label: Passive steam-vane turntable drive
new_nodes.detail: A molded vane ring under the glass tray replaces the 5 rpm synchronous motor and its drive.

new_nodes.label: Rotates food using the food's own heat
new_nodes.detail: Turns the tray with energy the food already gives off, with no mains draw.

new_edges.to: Rotates food using the food's own heat

new_edges.from: Rotates food using the food's own heat

ideas.rationale: Driving the tray from the food's own steam removes the motor's continuous electrical draw while still delivering even heating.

ideas.title: Shrink-wrap cavity insert

new_nodes.label: Field-concentrating reflector liner
new_nodes.detail: A conductive, dish-shaped insert narrows the active cavity to the food footprint, so less volume is energised.

new_nodes.label: Snap-in reflective cavity insert
new_nodes.detail: A removable metallised insert that fits inside the 20 L enamelled cavity.

new_nodes.label: Concentrates field on the food volume
new_nodes.detail: Heats the occupied volume rather than filling the whole chamber.

new_edges.to: Concentrates field on the food volume

new_edges.from: Concentrates field on the food volume

ideas.rationale: Energising only the occupied volume cuts the field energy wasted on empty chamber space in every cook.

ideas.title: Energy-ledger dial replaces the power cam

new_nodes.label: Mains-current sensing with passive e-paper readout
new_nodes.detail: A shunt on the mains feed drives a zero-power e-paper display showing the cost of each cook.

new_nodes.label: Live energy-ledger dial
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the five-step duty-cycle cam knob with a dial that shows cost per cook and suggests a lower power setting.

new_nodes.label: Makes energy cost visible at point of use

new_nodes.detail: Eight to sixteen GaN HEMT amplifier modules replace the magnetron tube and high-voltage chain, all running from a low-voltage DC rail.

new_nodes.label: Electronically phased RF feed array
new_nodes.detail: Several feed probes in the cavity walls, each with independent phase and amplitude, steer the standing-wave pattern across the food.

ideas.title: Cavity as Sensor: Clock and Power Cam Replaced by Dielectric Loading Feedback

ideas.title: Ambient-light fibre pipe replaces the interior lamp

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp
new_nodes.detail: Original 20-25 W interior lamp of the base product, to be removed.

new_nodes.label: Fibre-optic ambient light pipe
new_nodes.detail: Clear light guide through the door frame collects room light and channels it into the cavity, with no electrical input.

new_nodes.label: Passive light guiding
new_nodes.detail: Total internal reflection transports ambient light from the room into the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Optics
new_nodes.detail: Field of light collection and transmission.

new_nodes.label: Illuminate cavity for inspection
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user see food without opening the door.

ideas.rationale: Removing the 20-25 W lamp and powering the cavity light from ambient room light eliminates lamp energy use during every cook cycle.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN amplifier array replaces the magnetron and duty-cycle cam

new_nodes.label: Magnetron
new_nodes.detail: Original 700 W vacuum-tube RF source, roughly 60-65% efficient.

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier array
new_nodes.detail: Phase-combined 2.45 GHz gallium nitride modules with per-module power control and no filament.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride RF power electronics
new_nodes.detail: High-efficiency wide-bandgap transistors for 2.45 GHz amplification.

new_nodes.label: Five-step duty-cycle power cam
new_nodes.detail: Original power knob that switches the magnetron on and off in cycles.

new_nodes.label: Continuous digital power control
new_nodes.detail: Electronic setpoint that varies RF output smoothly with no off-phase.

new_nodes.label: Deliver variable RF power to cavity
new_nodes.detail: Supplies the cooking field at the level the user selects.

new_nodes.label: Duty-cycling wastes energy
new_nodes.detail: Off-phases and warm-up losses of cyclic magnetron operation waste input energy.

new_edges.to: Deliver variable RF power to cavity

new_edges.from: Deliver variable RF power to cavity

ideas.rationale: Solid-state amplifiers with continuous power control convert more input energy into heating and avoid the off-phase losses of a duty-cycled magnetron.

ideas.title: Food-sensing termination replaces the clockwork timer and bell

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer knob
new_nodes.detail: Original 0-30 min mechanical timer with bell, which runs on a fixed schedule regardless of food state.

new_nodes.label: Humidity and volatile-gas sensor
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide gas sensor and capacitive humidity sensor that detect steam and volatiles as food reaches doneness.

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide gas sensing
new_nodes.detail: Resistive change in a heated metal-oxide film in response to volatile compounds.

new_nodes.label: Chemical sensing
new_nodes.detail: Field of detecting gases and vapours for process control.

new_nodes.label: Terminate heating at doneness
new_nodes.detail: Stops the magnetron when the food is cooked, not after a set time.

new_nodes.label: Overcooking wastes energy
new_nodes.detail: Fixed-time cooking continues past doneness, consuming extra energy and reheating food.

ideas.rationale: Ending heat at the moment the food is done removes the energy spent on overcooking and on reheating food that a fixed timer has overdone.

ideas.title: Phased-array feed ring replaces the turntable motor and mechanical stirring

new_nodes.label: Turntable drive motor and glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Original motor-driven glass turntable that rotates food to average out uneven heating.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array feed ring
new_nodes.detail: Ring of electronically phased feed elements around the cavity that steers the field across the load with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array beam steering
new_nodes.detail: Electronic control of the phase of multiple RF feeds to shape and move the field pattern.

new_nodes.label: Distribute field evenly
new_nodes.detail: Spreads RF energy over the whole load so the food heats uniformly.

new_nodes.label: Uneven heating causes reheats
new_nodes.detail: Cold spots force extra cooking time or reheating, using more energy.

new_edges.to: Turntable drive motor and glass turntable

new_edges.from: Turntable drive motor and glass turntable

ideas.rationale: Even electronic field steering removes cold spots and the need for repeat cooking, cutting the total energy per meal.

ideas.title: Heat-pipe loop replaces the exhaust fan and feeds a water pre-heat tank

new_nodes.label: Magnetron cooling fan and exhaust vent
new_nodes.detail: Original fan that dumps magnetron and cavity waste heat into the room.

new_nodes.label: Sealed heat-pipe loop
new_nodes.detail: Sealed heat pipe that carries magnetron and cavity waste heat to a water reservoir.

new_nodes.label: Water pre-heat tank
new_nodes.detail: Insulated reservoir that is pre-warmed for the next use, such as tea, soup or defrost water.

new_nodes.label: Heat-pipe thermal transport
new_nodes.detail: Phase-change heat transport with very low thermal resistance and no pumps.

new_nodes.label: Thermal management
new_nodes.detail: Field of heat transfer and heat recovery.

new_nodes.label: Preheat water for next use
new_nodes.detail: Stores recovered heat in water so later heating needs less input energy.

new_nodes.label: Waste heat exhausted to room
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron and cavity heat that leaves the appliance unused.

new_edges.to: Magnetron cooling fan and exhaust vent

new_edges.from: Magnetron cooling fan and exhaust vent

ideas.rationale: Recovering magnetron waste heat into stored water turns energy that is normally lost to the room into useful pre-heating, reducing net consumption.

new_nodes.detail: Keeps heat inside the cavity during cooking and in standby, reducing thermal leakage.

new_nodes.label: Evacuated multilayer insulation

new_nodes.label: Heat leakage through walls
new_nodes.detail: Conductive wall losses and warm casing waste energy during cooking and after shutdown.

ideas.title: Daylight Window Instead of Interior Lamp

new_nodes.label: Visibility of food during cooking

new_nodes.label: Passive optical light guiding

ideas.rationale: Removing the lamp's 20-25 W draw from every cook serves M13 while the cavity still looks bright and inviting, so the user perceives no loss.

ideas.title: Done-When-Done Moisture Sensing

new_nodes.detail: Gas or humidity sensor that stops the magnetron when steam signals the food has reached serving temperature.

new_nodes.label: Stop heating at the right moment
new_nodes.detail: Replaces guessing a time with sensing the actual cooking state.

new_nodes.label: Gas sensing via metal-oxide semiconductor
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost sensing technology already used in kitchen hobs.

new_edges.to: Stop heating at the right moment

new_edges.from: Stop heating at the right moment

ideas.title: Energy Budget Dial in Joules

new_nodes.label: Energy budget dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial sets a target energy amount in watt-hours, replacing the time-and-power pair.

new_nodes.label: Show cost of each reheat

ideas.title: Motorless Field Rotation Replaces the Turntable

new_nodes.detail: Two magnetron feeds with timed phase shifting create a moving hot spot, so the food need not rotate.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Achieves uniform cooking without a motor-driven plate.

new_nodes.label: Phased electromagnetic field control
new_nodes.detail: Electronic phase control, rooted in radio engineering.

ideas.rationale: Dropping the turntable and its drive motor removes a moving mechanical load and its standby losses, and it lets the whole plate area be used for food, which saves energy.

ideas.title: Carbon-Aware Scheduled Cooking

new_nodes.label: Grid-aware start scheduler
new_nodes.detail: Connects to the grid carbon signal and delays start until the cleanest window, with a user override.

new_nodes.label: Choose when energy is used
new_nodes.detail: Shifts the moment of consumption to low-carbon, low-price periods.

new_nodes.label: Household energy-conscious user
new_nodes.detail: Wants lower bills and emissions but not extra effort.

ideas.rationale: Shifting when the microwave draws power cuts emissions and cost per cook without any hardware change, reframing the clock from a countdown into a choice of cleaner moments.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Thaw Strip

new_nodes.label: Shows thaw progress without power

ideas.title: Thaw-on-Arrival Scheduler

new_nodes.label: Connected thaw scheduler
new_nodes.detail: Wi-Fi module that starts the thaw so it finishes when the user is due home, replacing the dial.

new_nodes.label: Finishes thaw at arrival time

new_nodes.label: Wi-Fi / IoT connectivity
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost wireless link to a phone app or calendar.

new_nodes.label: Connected appliances
new_nodes.detail: Consumer IoT and scheduling software.

ideas.title: Meltdown Soundscape

new_nodes.label: Signals thaw completion by ear

new_nodes.label: Sound design

new_edges.from: Conducts heat into ice from below

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge load cell

new_nodes.label: Instrumentation

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable motor drive

new_nodes.label: Dielectric field shaping
new_nodes.detail: Engineered permittivity gradients redistribute electromagnetic energy without moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Even heating across the load
new_nodes.detail: Achieves uniform energy deposition throughout the food without mechanical rotation.

ideas.rationale: Removing the motor-driven turntable eliminates its standing power draw and mechanical losses while a passive lens maintains heating uniformity, so less energy is needed for the same result.

ideas.title: Solid-State Inverter Replaces Mechanical Power Cam

new_nodes.detail: Mechanical cam that switches the magnetron on and off in coarse steps to approximate lower power levels.

new_nodes.label: Resonant soft-switching power conversion
new_nodes.detail: Zero-voltage switching cuts switching losses and reactive current in the high-voltage transformer.

ideas.title: Thermoelectric Exhaust Recovery Powers Electronics

new_nodes.detail: Seebeck effect converts waste heat gradients into usable DC power for control and sensing loads.

new_nodes.label: Power control electronics and sensors
new_nodes.detail: Supplies the low-voltage electronics, sensors and display from recovered heat.

ideas.title: Lamp-free cavity with fibre-guided sensing light

new_nodes.detail: A 0.1 W LED behind the door feeds an optical fibre that runs along the cavity roof and emits diffuse light through a sealed, microwave-blocking lens.

new_nodes.label: Cavity visibility without heat
new_nodes.detail: Gives the user a view of the food while adding almost no heat load inside the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Fibre optic light transmission
new_nodes.detail: Light is carried by total internal reflection, so the light source can sit outside the hot, RF-filled cavity.

ideas.title: Solid-state inverter replaces cam-cycled transformer

new_nodes.detail: A high-frequency gallium nitride inverter drives the magnetron with continuously variable power instead of on/off duty cycling.

new_nodes.label: Continuous power modulation
new_nodes.detail: Delivers any power level without the on/off surges of the cam, so the magnetron runs at its efficient operating point.

new_nodes.label: Wide-bandgap power electronics
new_nodes.detail: GaN switches run at high frequency with low conduction and switching losses.

ideas.rationale: Continuous power modulation removes the wasteful start-stop cycling of the cam, which wastes energy on each ramp and cuts the 5-step control to smooth, efficient output.

ideas.title: Phased-array feed replaces the turntable motor

new_nodes.label: Dual-feed phase-steered waveguide array
new_nodes.detail: Two phase-locked feeds on the cavity wall steer the field pattern electronically, so the food needs no mechanical rotation.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Spreads energy across the load via electronic beam steering, so no motor or turntable is needed to avoid cold spots.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array RF control
new_nodes.detail: Adjusts the relative phase of two RF sources to move the hot spots of the standing-wave pattern.

ideas.rationale: Removing the turntable motor and its drag losses, along with the heat-soaked glass plate, lowers energy use while keeping the heating even.

ideas.title: Doneness sensing replaces the clockwork timer

new_nodes.label: Stop at doneness
new_nodes.detail: Ends heating when the food is ready, not after a fixed time, so no energy is spent overcooking or leaving the oven running.

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermography
new_nodes.detail: Thermal radiation from the surface is converted into a temperature reading without contact.

ideas.rationale: Ending the cycle at the target temperature instead of at a fixed time removes the energy wasted on overcooking and idle run time.

ideas.title: Magnetron heat pipe feeds a water-preheat reservoir

new_nodes.detail: Sets the output power at any level by varying the inverter frequency or duty cycle, with no on/off cycling.

new_nodes.label: Resonant soft-switching power conversion
new_nodes.detail: Switching method that keeps voltage or current near zero at switch transitions, which lowers switching losses.

new_nodes.label: Thermal cycling from on/off duty cam
new_nodes.detail: Cycling the magnetron on and off wastes energy in start-up transients and stresses the magnetron and its supply.

new_edges.to: Thermal cycling from on/off duty cam
Thermal cycling from on/off duty cam

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 50 Hz transformer and the on/off duty cam with a resonant inverter removes the transformer's core losses and the start-stop waste, so the magnetron receives the energy it needs with fewer conversion losses.

ideas.title: Motor-free quadrature magnetron feed replaces the turntable drive

new_nodes.label: Dual-feed quadrature waveguide launchers
new_nodes.detail: Two RF feeds at 90 degrees phase offset that couple energy into the cavity from opposite walls.

new_nodes.label: Phase-sweep controller
new_nodes.detail: Electronic controller that continuously varies the relative phase of the two feeds to move the field pattern across the cavity.

new_nodes.label: Electronic mode stirring via phase modulation
new_nodes.detail: Spreads the RF field pattern over time by shifting feed phase, replacing mechanical stirring or turntable rotation.

new_nodes.label: Spatially uniform field without moving parts
new_nodes.detail: Achieves even heating across the cavity with no rotating glass plate or drive motor.

new_nodes.label: Turntable motor parasitic load
new_nodes.detail: The turntable drive motor draws continuous power and adds mechanical complexity and wear.

new_edges.to: Spatially uniform field without moving parts

new_edges.to: Spatially uniform field without moving parts

new_edges.from: Spatially uniform field without moving parts

ideas.rationale: Electronically sweeping the field pattern with two phase-offset feeds removes the turntable motor's continuous draw and delivers even heating sooner, so less cooking time and energy are needed.

ideas.title: Thermoelectric harvesting of magnetron waste heat powers standby electronics

new_nodes.label: Bi2Te3 thermoelectric generator on magnetron heat sink
new_nodes.detail: Seebeck modules clamped between the magnetron fin stack and the chassis, converting the temperature gradient into DC power.

new_nodes.label: Supercapacitor energy buffer
new_nodes.detail: Stores the harvested DC so that the controller and LED draw from the buffer during standby.

new_nodes.label: Passive heat pipe cooling assembly
new_nodes.detail: Heat pipe that moves magnetron waste heat to the fin stack, so the cooling fan is no longer needed for heat removal.

new_nodes.label: Thermoelectric (Seebeck) energy conversion
new_nodes.detail: Direct conversion of a temperature difference into electrical power with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Power standby electronics from waste heat
new_nodes.detail: Supplies the controller, sensors and LED from recovered magnetron heat instead of mains.

ideas.rationale: Ending the cycle when the food is done, rather than at a fixed time, stops the magnetron from running past the point where further energy does useful work.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state RF electronics
new_nodes.detail: Semiconductor power amplifiers operating at 2.45 GHz.

new_nodes.label: GaN RF power amplification
new_nodes.detail: Gallium nitride transistor amplifiers with continuously variable output power and high efficiency.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state GaN 2.45 GHz amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Continuously variable RF source that replaces the magnetron and its fixed duty-cycle steps.

new_nodes.label: Rectenna reflected-power recycler
new_nodes.detail: Patch-antenna array that rectifies reflected microwave energy back to DC to feed the amplifier and controller.

new_nodes.label: Delivers only the power the load absorbs

new_nodes.label: Phased-array antennas
new_nodes.detail: Control of radiated field pattern through relative phase between feeds.

new_nodes.label: Electronic field steering
new_nodes.detail: Programmed phase offsets move the standing-wave pattern across the cavity without any moving part.

new_nodes.detail: Baseline rotating plate and few-watt motor, resolved by electronic steering.

ideas.rationale: Removing the motor and rotating mass eliminates a continuous electrical load while the phase-swept field keeps heating uniform, so energy goes into food rather than drive hardware.

new_nodes.label: Electromagnetic cavity design
new_nodes.detail: Shaping of conductive enclosures to control field distribution and volume.

new_nodes.label: Mechanical cavity-volume adaptation
new_nodes.detail: Conductive wall position set by a mechanical linkage to change active cavity size.

new_nodes.label: Door-linkage cam
new_nodes.detail: Cam on the door hinge that converts door closing into liner travel.

new_nodes.label: Door-driven sliding metal cavity liner

ideas.rationale: Shrinking the active cavity to fit the food concentrates microwave energy on the load, so small portions cook with less wasted field and less electricity.

ideas.title: Scent Bell

new_nodes.label: Bell (end-of-cycle chime)
new_nodes.detail: Legacy base_product component: an audible end signal that is only heard in the kitchen.

new_nodes.label: Volatile-sensing gas array
new_nodes.detail: Metal-oxide sensor that detects the aroma compounds released as food approaches serving temperature.

new_nodes.label: Aroma cartridge
new_nodes.detail: Releases a toasted-bread note into the room when the sensor reports readiness.

new_nodes.label: Sense food readiness by smell
new_nodes.detail: Reads doneness from the same cue people use when they sniff a dish to judge it.

new_nodes.label: Signal readiness olfactorily
new_nodes.detail: Makes the end point perceptible from any room in the house.

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide gas sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost semiconductor sensing of volatile organic compounds.

new_nodes.label: Analytical chemistry
new_nodes.detail: Discipline underlying volatile compound detection and aroma science.

ideas.rationale: Smell is the cue people already trust for doneness, so the machine delivers readiness through the sense they use to judge food and reaches them wherever they are in the home.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Door

new_nodes.label: Interior lamp
new_nodes.detail: Legacy base_product component: a 20-25 W incandescent bulb used only so the user can see inside.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door window
new_nodes.detail: Glass panel with a heat-sensitive film that shifts colour from cool blue to amber as the cavity heats.

new_nodes.label: Show heat progress at a glance
new_nodes.detail: Gives a continuous visual gradient of how close the food is to ready instead of a binary on or off state.

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic liquid-crystal film
new_nodes.detail: Passive colour-changing film that needs no power and no bulb.

new_nodes.label: Materials science
new_nodes.detail: Discipline behind thermochromic polymers and coatings.

new_edges.to: Show heat progress at a glance

new_edges.from: Show heat progress at a glance

ideas.rationale: A colour gradient on the door shows the user how far along the food is at any moment, which answers the real question of whether it is ready and removes both the bulb and its energy use.

ideas.title: Fuel-Gauge Plate

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob
new_nodes.detail: Legacy base_product component: a 0-30 minute mechanical dial that shows time remaining, not food state.

new_nodes.label: Infrared surface-temperature array
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost IR sensor array that reads the surface temperature of the food.

new_nodes.label: Analogue progress needle
new_nodes.detail: Fuel-gauge style needle that sweeps from cold to ready on the front panel.

new_nodes.label: Measure food state directly
new_nodes.detail: Reads the food itself rather than inferring doneness from elapsed time.

new_nodes.label: Show readiness as a gauge
new_nodes.detail: Displays how close the food is to ready, which a countdown never does.

new_nodes.label: Passive infrared thermometry
new_nodes.detail: Non-contact temperature sensing from emitted infrared radiation.

new_nodes.label: Thermal physics
new_nodes.detail: Discipline governing heat transfer and infrared emission from surfaces.

ideas.rationale: A gauge that fills toward done tells users whether the food is ready, which is the feedback they actually want, instead of how many minutes are left.

ideas.title: Weigh-to-Ready Platform

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Legacy base_product component: a glass plate that rotates food for even heating.

new_nodes.label: Rotating load-cell platform
new_nodes.detail: Turntable on a strain-gauge load cell that tracks the mass lost to steam.

new_nodes.label: Track moisture loss as mass drop
new_nodes.detail: Uses the weight lost to steam as a physical signature that cooking is complete.

new_nodes.label: Signal readiness from mass threshold
new_nodes.detail: Triggers a ready cue when the food has lost a target fraction of its starting weight.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge load cell
new_nodes.detail: Inexpensive bridge sensor that measures small changes in weight.

new_nodes.label: Metrology
new_nodes.detail: Discipline of precise measurement, including mass and calibration.

new_edges.to: Track moisture loss as mass drop

new_edges.from: Track moisture loss as mass drop

ideas.rationale: Steam loss is the physical sign that food is done, so a platform that weighs the food gives a direct readiness signal and turns an ordinary plate into the feedback instrument.

ideas.title: Warm Handle

new_nodes.label: Door push-release button
new_nodes.detail: Legacy base_product component: a mechanical push button that releases the door latch.

new_nodes.label: Thermal haptic handle
new_nodes.detail: Door handle that warms through a conductive link to the cavity so its temperature mirrors the food.

new_nodes.label: Convey doneness through touch
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user feel how hot the food is before opening the door, with no need to look or listen.

new_nodes.label: Conductive heat-pipe linkage
new_nodes.detail: Passive heat transfer from the cavity to the handle, with no electronics needed.

new_nodes.label: Haptics and thermal perception
new_nodes.detail: Study of how people sense and interpret temperature through touch.

ideas.rationale: A handle that warms with the food gives a tactile readout of doneness that works for anyone, including people who cannot see the panel or who are across the room, and needs no power.

ideas.title: 27 MHz capacitive RF thaw replacing the 2.45 GHz magnetron

new_nodes.label: 27.12 MHz capacitive RF dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Electrodes on either side of the load drive displacement current through the food; the ~11 m wavelength gives a nearly uniform field across a frozen block, unlike the 12 cm wave at 2.45 GHz.

new_nodes.label: Solid-state 27.12 MHz RF oscillator
new_nodes.detail: LDMOS or GaN transistor oscillator running from a low-voltage DC rail; replaces the magnetron, filament and cathode, so there is no thermionic wear.

new_nodes.label: Parallel-plate thaw electrode pair
new_nodes.detail: Upper plate in the cavity ceiling and lower plate as a raised shelf, separated by ceramic spacers; replaces the waveguide and mica cover.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric thawing by displacement-current heating
new_nodes.detail: Heats the full thickness of a frozen block at once instead of from the surface inward.

ideas.rationale: Volumetric RF heating at 27 MHz thaws the whole block at once with fewer hot and cold spots, so frozen food defrosts faster and more evenly than surface-first 2.45 GHz heating.

ideas.title: Load-sensing auto-defrost governor replacing the power knob and timer

new_nodes.label: Dielectric-loss tracking by forward/reflected power ratio
new_nodes.detail: As ice melts its loss factor rises sharply, so the forward-to-reflected power ratio at the magnetron feed signals the thaw state in real time.

new_nodes.label: Directional coupler on magnetron feed
new_nodes.detail: Coupled-line sensor on the waveguide feed reads forward and reflected power continuously; a low-cost printed-circuit part.

new_nodes.label: Microcontroller duty-cycle governor
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the 5-step cam switch and the clockwork timer; sets the on/off ratio per thaw stage and drops duty near melt to limit superheating.

new_nodes.label: Detects thaw point and ends defrost automatically
new_nodes.detail: Steps down or stops power when the loss signature shows the block is near 0 C, so the user never has to guess a time.

new_edges.from: Dielectric-loss tracking by forward/reflected power ratio

ideas.rationale: Closed-loop control that ends the thaw at the melt point removes the guesswork that makes parents over-cook or under-thaw frozen food.

ideas.title: Stationary susceptor-spreader replacing the rotating turntable

new_nodes.label: Susceptor-to-conduction hybrid heating
new_nodes.detail: A ferrite-loaded layer absorbs microwave energy and conducts it through a high-conductivity core into the underside of the food, so heating no longer depends on the field pattern alone.

new_nodes.label: Stationary aluminium-graphite thermal spreader plate
new_nodes.detail: Fixed plate with a ferrite absorber layer and fins; replaces the glass turntable, roller ring and motor with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Spreads heat by conduction without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Distributes energy uniformly across the base of the food and flattens standing-wave hot spots.

new_edges.to: Spreads heat by conduction without rotation

new_edges.from: Spreads heat by conduction without rotation

Spreads heat by conduction without rotation

ideas.rationale: Conducting heat up into the frozen base from a stationary plate lets the block thaw from below as well as from the field, which shortens the thaw and removes the motor.

ideas.title: Supercapacitor-buffered pulsed magnetron for burst thawing

new_nodes.label: Supercapacitor-buffered pulsed magnetron drive
new_nodes.detail: A low-voltage supercapacitor stores energy and a switched boost converter lifts it to about 4 kV only during short pulses, so peak power rises for fast thaw while average power is set by pulse rate.

new_nodes.label: Low-voltage supercapacitor energy bank (under 50 J)
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the high-voltage capacitor; with stored energy under 50 J and a bleed path, the discharge hazard is greatly reduced.

new_nodes.label: Switched-mode boost converter to 4 kV pulse stage
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency ferrite-core converter replaces the 50 Hz leakage transformer and diode doubler, removing the bulky iron core.

new_nodes.label: Delivers high-peak-power pulses for fast thawing
new_nodes.detail: Pulse width and repetition rate set the energy delivered to the block in discrete bursts.

new_nodes.label: Ultrasonic mechanical-viscous thaw heating
new_nodes.detail: Piezoelectric vibration in a coupling plate heats the ice-water interface through viscous loss and cavitation in liquid films, and speeds conduction; no electromagnetic radiation is involved.

new_nodes.label: Capacitive load sensing
new_nodes.detail: Electrode measures food mass and dielectric load to estimate absorbable energy.

new_nodes.label: Auto-dosing power controller
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the 5-step duty-cycle cam with continuous output matched to the detected load.

new_nodes.label: Deliver only absorbed energy
new_nodes.detail: Output tracks what the food can absorb, avoiding full-power bursts into small loads.

ideas.rationale: Matching RF output to the actual load means a small reheat no longer burns a full 700 W, cutting energy use at its source.

ideas.title: Solid-State Field Stirring

new_nodes.label: Solid-state phased-array RF
new_nodes.detail: Multiple low-power antennas electronically steer the field with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Phased-array feed panel
new_nodes.detail: Replaces the glass turntable and its drive motor with electronic field stirring.

new_nodes.label: Even heating without rotation
new_nodes.detail: Uniform field distribution across the cavity with no mechanical drive.

ideas.rationale: Removing the turntable motor and its drive eliminates a continuously running electrical load while still delivering even heating.

ideas.title: Thermal-Store Residual Cooking

new_nodes.label: Phase-change thermal store
new_nodes.detail: Salt-hydrate phase-change material in the cavity walls stores heat and releases it after power cut-off.

new_nodes.label: Thermal-store cavity liner
new_nodes.detail: Vacuum-insulated, PCM-lined cavity keeps food cooking after the magnetron stops.

new_nodes.label: Residual cooking
new_nodes.detail: Finishes cooking from stored heat, shortening the active magnetron run time.

ideas.rationale: Recycling heat that would otherwise be lost lets the magnetron run for less time, so each cook draws less total energy.

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF amplifier array (2.45 GHz)
new_nodes.detail: Low-voltage (48 V DC) transistor modules, each 50-100 W, combined into one feed; no cathode, no HV transformer, no doubler.

new_nodes.label: Gallium nitride RF power transistors
new_nodes.detail: Wide-bandgap semiconductors with high RF efficiency and no kilovolt rail, so transformer and rectifier losses disappear.

new_nodes.label: Generates RF with per-module power modulation
new_nodes.detail: Output scales to the load in real time instead of running at full power and cycling on and off.

ideas.title: Load-Sensing Auto-Stop Replaces Timer Knob

new_nodes.label: Dielectric load sensor and IR food-surface probe
new_nodes.detail: Reads reflected power and surface temperature to judge when the food reaches the target state.

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power dielectric sensing
new_nodes.detail: The cavity impedance changes with food mass and moisture, which can be measured from the feed line.

new_nodes.label: Terminates heating at target temperature
new_nodes.detail: Stops energy input when the food is ready, replacing a guessed clockwork time.

ideas.title: Magnetron Waste-Heat Recovery Store

new_nodes.label: Phase-change heat store (paraffin-graphite) on magnetron
new_nodes.detail: Captures the large share of magnetron input lost as heat and releases it to preheat the cavity or water.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat phase-change storage
new_nodes.detail: Stores heat in a material's melting transition, so it can be held and released at a near-constant temperature.

new_nodes.label: Recycles waste heat into cooking
new_nodes.detail: Returns stored heat to the cooking cycle, reducing the electricity needed to heat food from cold.

ideas.rationale: Reusing heat that the magnetron would otherwise waste reduces the net energy each cooking cycle draws from the mains, which serves M13.

ideas.title: Ambient Light-Pipe Replaces Interior Lamp

new_nodes.label: Metal-screened acrylic light-pipe in door
new_nodes.detail: Carries room light from the door edge into the cavity, with a mesh screen that blocks microwaves.

new_nodes.label: Acrylic light-guide optics
new_nodes.detail: Total internal reflection channels light along a polymer rod with almost no loss.

new_nodes.label: Illuminates cavity from ambient light
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user see inside the cavity using light that is already in the kitchen, at zero electrical draw.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the 20-25 W incandescent lamp with borrowed room light removes a constant electrical load for the lamp's whole life, which serves M13.

ideas.title: Thermal-Vision Auto-Defrost

new_nodes.label: Thermal imaging array
new_nodes.detail: Low-res IR camera mapping surface temperature of the load every few seconds; replaces the clockwork timer knob and bell.

new_nodes.label: On-device ML core-temperature model
new_nodes.detail: Infers internal core temperature from surface gradients, so the appliance knows when the centre is thawed, not just warm.

new_nodes.label: Continuous thaw-state detection
new_nodes.detail: Stops or steps down power per zone the moment the core reaches just-below-freezing, preventing cooked edges.

new_nodes.label: Hands-free end-of-cycle alert
new_nodes.detail: Pushes a notification to the user's phone when the food is ready, replacing the bell.

ideas.rationale: By sensing the actual core temperature of the frozen food instead of guessing from a clock, the appliance thaws each item fully and quickly without overheating its edges.

ideas.title: RF Electrode Thaw Chamber

new_nodes.label: 27 MHz RF electrode plates
new_nodes.detail: Two parallel plates above and below the food that create an alternating field, replacing the magnetron and its waveguide.

new_nodes.label: Capacitive RF dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Heats the food volumetrically through its thickness, the same principle as industrial frozen-block thawing.

new_nodes.label: Volumetric thawing of thick blocks
new_nodes.detail: Thaws meat blocks evenly from centre to surface, where microwave penetration fails.

ideas.rationale: Field-based thickness-independent heating drives into the centre of a frozen block far faster than surface-first microwave heating, directly cutting defrost time.

ideas.title: Phased-Array Hotspot Steering

new_nodes.label: Solid-state GaN phased-array emitters
new_nodes.detail: A grid of small solid-state amplifiers that steer and focus energy electronically, replacing the glass turntable.

new_nodes.label: Electronic beam steering
new_nodes.detail: Shifts the phase of each emitter so the beam sweeps the load with no moving parts.

new_nodes.label: Electronic uniform field sweep
new_nodes.detail: Moves energy across the food in software, so every region gets the same dose without rotation.

ideas.rationale: Electronically steered energy removes cold spots and the wait for rotation, so frozen food defrosts evenly and faster in a single pass.

ideas.title: Continuous Ice-Aware Power Ramp

new_nodes.label: Solid-state continuous power modulator
new_nodes.detail: Fine-grained digital power control that replaces the 5-step duty-cycle power knob and its cam.

new_nodes.label: Dielectric-loss feedback control
new_nodes.detail: Reads the food's changing absorption as ice melts into water and adjusts power to match.

new_nodes.label: Adaptive thaw curve
new_nodes.detail: Ramps power up and down through the ice-to-water transition, the point where frozen food otherwise runs away and cooks.

ideas.rationale: Matching power to the ice-to-water transition keeps the heating rate high throughout the thaw without the overheating that fixed power steps cause.

ideas.title: Overnight Thermal Battery Thaw Plate

new_nodes.label: Phase-change salt thaw plate
new_nodes.detail: A flat plate of phase-change material that is charged slowly at off-peak times and releases stored heat by conduction, replacing the magnetron.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat energy storage
new_nodes.detail: Stores large amounts of heat in a phase change at a fixed temperature, so the plate delivers steady heat on demand.

new_nodes.label: Conductive thawing from below
new_nodes.detail: Pulls heat into the food from its contact surface, which is a gentle, cheap, and quiet way to thaw.

ideas.rationale: A pre-charged phase-change plate removes the need for a high-power magnet entirely, making thawing cheap to run and safe for food while still giving a fast contact-thaw.

new_nodes.detail: Reads magnetron reflected power and feed impedance, which shift sharply as ice melts near 0°C because the dielectric loss rises.

new_nodes.label: Feed-impedance monitor
new_nodes.detail: Directional coupler and comparator on the existing waveguide feed, with firmware thresholds that flag the thaw transition.

new_nodes.label: Detect ice-to-water transition
new_nodes.detail: Infers the thaw state from the RF feed signature without any food probe.

new_nodes.label: Thermal runaway at thaw edges
new_nodes.detail: Thin edges overheat once the bulk is liquid, so power must drop as soon as the transition is detected.

ideas.rationale: The defrost stop is set by the food's own physical state, so the user no longer has to guess a time for each load, which shortens defrosting and avoids cooking the edges.

ideas.title: 915 MHz Solid-State Source Replaces Magnetron and Duty-Cycle Cam

new_nodes.label: RF dielectric heating
new_nodes.detail: Heating of lossy dielectrics by RF energy absorption, the physics behind all microwave defrosting.

new_nodes.detail: Transistor-based 915 MHz ISM-band source with continuously adjustable output power and no vacuum tube.

new_nodes.label: Deep volumetric penetration
new_nodes.detail: The longer 915 MHz wavelength penetrates roughly twice as deep as 2.45 GHz, so a frozen block heats through instead of only at the surface.

new_nodes.label: Digital power controller
new_nodes.detail: Software-defined power curve that replaces the mechanical 5-step cam.

ideas.rationale: Deeper, more even penetration at 915 MHz heats a frozen core instead of the outside, so the block defrosts faster and with less edge cooking.

new_nodes.detail: Ion-doped lossy dielectric that heats strongly at microwave frequencies and transfers that heat by conduction.

new_nodes.detail: Delivers heat from the sleeve surface into the frozen food, bypassing the poor direct absorption of ice.

ideas.title: Steam Condensation Replaces Dry Cavity Air

new_nodes.detail: Small heated water reservoir that injects saturated steam into the cavity through a micro-nozzle.

new_nodes.detail: Steam condenses on cold surfaces and releases latent heat, roughly 2260 kJ/kg, at the frozen interface.

new_nodes.label: Wireless communications
new_nodes.detail: Short-range low-power radio links between devices.

new_nodes.label: Bluetooth Low Energy link
new_nodes.detail: Low-power radio that pairs a small device with the microwave's controller.

new_nodes.label: Haptic pebble
new_nodes.detail: Pocket-sized, rechargeable token that vibrates and glows when the food is ready.

new_nodes.label: Alert user remotely by touch
new_nodes.detail: Delivers a tactile and visual notification to wherever the user is in the home.

ideas.rationale: The bell only works if the user is within earshot, whereas a pebble carries the readiness signal to the user wherever they are.

ideas.title: Doneness Dial

new_nodes.label: Food thermodynamics
new_nodes.detail: Heat transfer and thermal behaviour of food under microwave energy.

new_nodes.label: Food-state estimation model
new_nodes.detail: Maps food type, mass, and starting temperature to expected heating curves.

new_nodes.label: Food-state dial
new_nodes.detail: Single dial labelled with outcomes such as warm, steaming, and piping hot rather than minutes or power levels.

new_nodes.label: Set target outcome instead of time
new_nodes.detail: The user specifies the desired end state, and the appliance decides how to get there and when it is reached.

new_edges.to: Set target outcome instead of time

new_edges.from: Set target outcome instead of time

ideas.rationale: Users state the readiness they want, and the appliance manages the heating and tells them when that state is reached, which removes the guesswork about power and time.

ideas.title: Solid-State Heart

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state RF power amplifier
new_nodes.detail: Semiconductor amplifier chain at 2.45 GHz replaces the magnetron and its ~4 kV supply, with no cathode, filament or HV.

new_nodes.label: Gallium-nitride RF transistor amplification
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state RF gain that can be phase-controlled and metered continuously.

new_nodes.label: 48 V switch-mode power supply
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency SMPS replaces the 50 Hz mains transformer, voltage doubler and bleeder resistor.

new_nodes.label: Continuous metered RF power
new_nodes.detail: Output set by transistor bias, replacing the duty-cycle cam and its on/off cycling.

ideas.rationale: Removing the filament preheat, the 4 kV supply and its standby bleed losses, and replacing duty-cycling with metered continuous power, cuts the energy wasted on every cook.

ideas.title: Wind-Driven Turntable

new_nodes.label: Wind-vane mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: Passive vane in the cooling-fan exhaust path turns the platter and stirs the field.

new_nodes.label: Cooling fan
new_nodes.detail: Existing fan that already cools the magnetron; it now also drives the stirrer.

new_nodes.label: Aerodynamic drag coupling
new_nodes.detail: Airflow torque transferred through a magnetic coupler to the platter, with no motor.

new_nodes.label: Zero-power food tumbling
new_nodes.detail: Rotation and mode stirring powered by air the machine already moves.

ideas.rationale: Powering the turntable from air the cooling fan already moves eliminates the dedicated motor's draw while keeping even heating, so the platter costs no extra electricity.

ideas.title: Done, Not Timed

new_nodes.label: Mechanical clockwork timer knob (retired)
new_nodes.detail: Runs for a guessed time and rings a bell whether or not the food is ready.

new_nodes.label: Steam-humidity sensor array
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost MEMS sensor reads moisture rising from food and falling as it dries out.

new_nodes.label: Vapour sensing of food moisture
new_nodes.detail: Humidity change in the cavity is used as a proxy for cooking progress.

new_nodes.label: Stops cooking when food is done
new_nodes.detail: The cycle ends at the moment of readiness, not when a guessed time elapses.

new_edges.to: Stops cooking when food is done

new_edges.from: Stops cooking when food is done
Stops cooking when food is done

ideas.rationale: Ending each cycle when food is actually done removes the energy spent on overcooking, drying and reheating, which is the largest source of waste in guessed timings.

ideas.title: The Cost Glow

new_nodes.label: Incandescent interior lamp (retired)
new_nodes.detail: A 20–25 W bulb lit only so the user can peek inside.

new_nodes.label: Energy-meter glow ring
new_nodes.detail: A ~0.1 W LED ring behind the door glass, with colour and fill showing kWh used and time left.

new_nodes.label: Low-power LED colour mapping
new_nodes.detail: Colour and fill mapped to cumulative energy and remaining time.

new_nodes.label: Makes the energy cost of cooking visible
new_nodes.detail: Turns energy use into live feedback, so users see the cost and choose lower-energy settings.

new_edges.to: Makes the energy cost of cooking visible

new_edges.from: Makes the energy cost of cooking visible
Makes the energy cost of cooking visible

ideas.rationale: Swapping a 20–25 W lamp for a ~0.1 W glow that shows the cost of cooking cuts lighting energy by over 99% and uses feedback to nudge people toward shorter, lower-energy cycles.

ideas.title: Steam Battery

new_nodes.label: Stamped vent louvres (retired)
new_nodes.detail: Open slots that let hot steam and heat escape the cavity unused.

new_nodes.label: Condensing vent with heat recovery
new_nodes.detail: A small condenser that cools exhaust steam, returning its latent heat and condensate.

new_nodes.label: Phase-change thermal store
new_nodes.detail: Paraffin tile in the base that stores recovered heat for the next cook.

new_nodes.label: Latent-heat recovery via phase-change material
new_nodes.detail: Steam's latent heat is absorbed by a phase-change material and released later.

new_nodes.label: Recovers waste steam heat for the next cycle
new_nodes.detail: Escaped heat is captured and used to preheat the next cook.

new_edges.to: Recovers waste steam heat for the next cycle

new_edges.from: Recovers waste steam heat for the next cycle
Recovers waste steam heat for the next cycle

ideas.rationale: Steam is the cavity's largest escape of heat, and capturing its latent heat for the next cook lowers the net energy drawn from the mains per meal.

ideas.title: Lens-Eye Doneness Camera

new_nodes.label: Shielded CMOS camera with IR LED ring
new_nodes.detail: A tiny sensor behind a sub-wavelength shield replaces the lamp and mesh, and its IR light works even after a bulb would have burnt out.

new_nodes.label: On-device browning and doneness vision model
new_nodes.detail: Classifies surface colour and texture to output a doneness percentage.

new_nodes.label: Computer vision & machine learning
new_nodes.detail: Image recognition and on-device inference.

new_nodes.label: Streams live doneness estimate to user's phone
new_nodes.detail: Shows a progress bar and sends an alert when the food reaches the target state.

new_edges.from: Shielded CMOS camera with IR LED ring
Shielded CMOS camera with IR LED ring
Shielded CMOS camera with IR LED ring
Shielded CMOS camera with IR LED ring

new_edges.from: On-device browning and doneness vision model

ideas.rationale: Replacing the blind lamp with a camera that reports doneness directly gives the user a live answer to 'is it ready?' instead of a view they must interpret themselves.

ideas.title: Weighing Turntable

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable hub
new_nodes.detail: A strain-gauge hub under the glass turntable reads food mass several times per second.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge mass-loss sensing
new_nodes.detail: Tracks the weight drop as water evaporates and infers doneness from the mass curve.

new_nodes.label: Infers doneness from real-time mass loss
new_nodes.detail: Replaces guessed minutes with a measured moisture-loss target for each food type.

new_edges.to: Infers doneness from real-time mass loss

new_edges.from: Infers doneness from real-time mass loss

ideas.rationale: Measuring the food's own mass loss tells the user when it is actually done, which is the honest feedback a timer can only guess at.

ideas.title: Sizzle Listener

new_nodes.label: Cavity acoustic microphone with magnetron-noise filter
new_nodes.detail: A sealed mic in the cavity wall listens to popping and bubbling while filtering out the magnetron hum.

new_nodes.label: Acoustic food-state pattern recognition
new_nodes.detail: Detects changes in popping or sizzle rhythm, such as popcorn slowing down, that mark readiness.

new_nodes.label: Detects food-state change from sound
new_nodes.detail: Recognises the moment the food's acoustic signature shifts, which means it is ready.

new_edges.from: Cavity acoustic microphone with magnetron-noise filter
Cavity acoustic microphone with magnetron-noise filter
Cavity acoustic microphone with magnetron-noise filter
Cavity acoustic microphone with magnetron-noise filter

ideas.rationale: Listening to the food itself turns the bell into a signal that fires when the food is ready, not when a timer runs out.

ideas.title: Scent Bell

new_nodes.label: Aerosol & fluidics engineering
new_nodes.detail: Controlled micro-dosing of volatile liquids into air.

new_nodes.label: Piezo micro-atomisation of aroma cartridge
new_nodes.detail: A piezo disc atomises a small dose of food-matched aroma into the vent when cooking ends.

new_nodes.label: Aroma atomiser cartridge
new_nodes.detail: A replaceable cartridge with a piezo atomiser that replaces the mechanical bell striker.

new_nodes.label: Signals completion by scent from any room
new_nodes.detail: The smell of finished food carries through the kitchen, so the user knows without being in view or hearing a bell.

new_edges.to: Signals completion by scent from any room

new_edges.from: Signals completion by scent from any room

ideas.rationale: A scent that drifts through the home tells people in any room that food is ready, which serves the need for feedback without a loud bell.

ideas.title: Package Talks to Oven

new_nodes.label: Printed chipless RF tag on food packaging
new_nodes.detail: A printed backscatter tag encodes the food's cook profile and replaces the manual timer knob.

new_nodes.label: Passive backscatter RF signature encoding
new_nodes.detail: The cavity antenna reads the tag's reflected RF signature, and the signature changes as the food's dielectric properties shift.

new_nodes.label: Reads cook profile and doneness from package
new_nodes.detail: The oven sets its own duration and end point from the package, so the user never has to set a time.
